The Numbers You'll Own

Stage-Gate Readiness: Programs meeting required customer, technical, regulatory, operational, supply-chain and commercial criteria before advancing

Customer Requirements Validation: Critical product requirements validated with target customers before major investment

Target BOM Attainment: Actual/forecast BOM vs. approved target at each development gate

What You'll Own

The hardware roadmap: multi-generation, grounded in customer evidence and portfolio priorities.

Business cases before NPI: target BOM, capital cost, margin, payback, and IRR, plus build, buy, or partner calls.

Requirements: cross-team needs translated into hardware and edge-compute specs, including privacy, appearance, and acceptance barriers in assisted living.

Sensing modality selection with AI & Intelligence, and convergence on common platforms to avoid SKU sprawl.

Stage gates from concept through EVT, DVT, PVT, and launch, with life-safety certification (e.g., UL 2560) planned in from day one.

Launch and lifecycle: whole-product readiness with Operations and Support, and end-of-life transitions with Device & Fleet.

The Ideal Candidate:

  • The hard requirement:you've taken connected hardware (IoT, edge, or smart devices) from concept through NPI to mass production.

  • 6+ years of product management, with strong business modeling (BOM, margin, ROI/IRR).

  • Experience partnering with contract manufacturers through NPI and ramp.

Career Category

Medical Affairs

Job Description

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Asset Medical Lead Medical Director – Cardiovascular & Metabolic (CVM) Strategy

What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role, you will lead the development and delivery of U.S. Cardiovascular & Metabolic (CVM) Medical strategy for maridebart cafraglutide (also known as MariTide), an investigational therapy developed by Amgen and being studied for obesity and obesity-related conditions. You will establish the cross-indication scientific, evidence, stakeholder, and implementation foundation that supports chronic weight management (CWM) launch readiness and prepares the organization for maturation in CVM. In partnership with the U.S. Medical Portfolio Lead, TA Head, Global Medical, and cross-functional colleagues, you will translate global strategy into an integrated U.S. Medical plan.


Responsibilities:

• Lead U.S. CVM Medical strategy, with initial emphasis on CWM launch support and early CV readiness.

• Build an integrated, evidence-based CVM narrative linking obesity and the broader care continuum.

• Define U.S. scientific evidence gaps and shape local evidence, RWE, HEOR, and Access and Use Evidence Generation priorities in alignment with global plans.

• Synthesize customer, field, market, and medical insights to inform U.S. Medical, Brand, evidence, and implementation decisions.

• Develop the early external-engagement plan for cardiologists, HF specialists, integrated delivery networks, professional societies, payers, and other priority stakeholders.

• Partner with Global Medical, Global Development, CfOR, HEOR, Medical Value and Access, and Scientific Communications to translate emerging evidence into U.S. strategy and execution.

• Lead or support U.S. scientific communications, including the scientific platform, core content, publication implementation, congress plans, and medical education.

• Support clinical trial activities and data interpretation as a U.S. Medical interface with Global Clinical Development and evidence-generation teams.

• Lead or support advisory boards, expert panels, and implementation-science initiatives that clarify real-world care pathways, referral patterns, and barriers to appropriate care.

• Provide medical input into reimbursement, policy, regulatory, label, and promotional-material discussions consistent with governance and evidence.

• Serve as a medical representative in leadership, governance, launch-readiness, and cross-functional teams; recommend priorities and resource trade-offs for the U.S. Medical plan.

• Contribute to medical training and field scientific readiness for CWM/OSA and evolving CVM evidence needs.

• Support decisions on independent medical education, medical grants, sponsorships, and advocacy activities in accordance with Amgen governance.

• Ensure Medical activities comply with applicable laws, regulations, policies, and standard operating procedures.

• Use established planning and performance-management processes to measure progress, identify risks, and improve execution.

What we expect of you

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The Medical Affairs Asset Lead we seek is a strategy leader with these qualifications.


Basic Qualifications:

Doctorate degree and 4 years of Medical Affairs, clinical research, or cardiometabolic science research experience

OR

Master’s degree and 7 years of Medical Affairs, clinical research, or cardiometabolic science research experience

OR

Bachelor’s degree and 9 years of Medical Affairs, clinical research, or cardiometabolic science research experience


Preferred Qualifications:

  • PharmD, PhD, MD, or other advanced scientific or clinical degree with experience in cardiometabolic disease, obesity, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or related conditions.
  • Strong clinical and scientific knowledge of cardiometabolic disease, including obesity and its related conditions.
  • Experience in U.S. Medical Affairs within the biopharmaceutical industry, including scientific engagement with cardiologists, endocrinologists, obesity-medicine clinicians, integrated delivery networks, and/or payers.
  • Experience developing or implementing medical strategy, evidence-generation plans, RWE, HEOR, or access-and-use evidence in a matrixed organization.
  • Knowledge of pharmaceutical product development, lifecycle planning, launch readiness, and collaboration across Clinical Operations, Commercial, Regulatory, Market Access, and Medical Affairs.
  • Experience engaging external experts, professional societies, advocacy organizations, health systems, and payers for scientific exchange and insight generation.
  • Ability to integrate multiple indications, scientific narratives, and stakeholder needs into a clear U.S. Medical strategy.
  • Familiarity with global regulatory organizations, guidelines, and practices, including Good Clinical Practice requirements.
  • Sound judgment, strong communication skills, and a track record of solving complex cross-functional problems.
  • Demonstrated success leading through influence and working across matrixed, cross-functional teams.

What you can expect of us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

The expected annual salary range for this role in the U.S. (excluding Puerto Rico) is posted. Actual salary will vary based on several factors including but not limited to, relevant skills, experience, and qualifications.

In addition to the base salary, Amgen offers a Total Rewards Plan, based on eligibility, comprising of health and welfare plans for staff and eligible dependents, financial plans with opportunities to save towards retirement or other goals, work/life balance, and career development opportunities that may include:

  • A comprehensive employee benefits package, including a Retirement and Savings Plan with generous company contributions, group medical, dental and vision coverage, life and disability insurance, and flexible spending accounts
  • A discretionary annual bonus program, or for field sales representatives, a sales-based incentive plan
  • Stock-based long-term incentives

jobs.description:
Natera is seeking a Lead Bioinformatics Scientist to join our Oncology Bioinformatics team and support the development, validation, and clinical application of our NGS-based assays. The ideal candidate has a strong background in data analysis for wet lab support and extensive experience with NGS data, with a focus on building solutions for oncology applications. In this role, you will shape the analytical validation strategy for an NGS assay, design and analyze feasibility and performance evaluation studies, and generate real-world evidence demonstrating its clinical utility. You will work with interdisciplinary teams to turn complex, multi-source data into actionable recommendations, supporting research, product development, validation, regulatory submissions, clinical studies, and scientific publications.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Lead the analytical validation strategy for an NGS-based assay, including designing, analyzing, and troubleshooting feasibility and performance evaluation studies (e.g., PPA and LoD) with bench scientists and biostatisticians.
  • Drive real-world evidence (RWE) studies that demonstrate the clinical utility of for therapy selection and patient management, from cohort selection through analysis of plasma mutation calls.
  • Build rapid prototypes and pipelines for custom analyses that integrate data from multiple Natera products.
  • Develop algorithms and tools to support new products, including contributions to the production bioinformatics pipeline.
  • Act as an internal technical consultant on bioinformatics methodology for other functional groups.
  • Work closely with assay development, engineering, biostatistics, clinical, commercial, regulatory, and lab operations teams.
  • Contribute to regulatory submissions, clinical study reports, and scientific publications.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master’s degree in bioinformatics (or a related field) with 10 years of post-graduate experience, or PhD with 5 years of post-graduate experience (preferred).

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

  • Expert knowledge of bioinformatics tools for NGS, including sequencing QC and secondary analysis such as variant calling.
  • Experience with WES/WGS/targeted sequencing of tissue and cfDNA, and with somatic variant calling (SNVs, indels, CNVs, fusions) on these data.
  • Working knowledge of statistical methods for assay performance evaluation, and ability to collaborate with biostatisticians on study design.
  • Strong programming and scripting skills in Python, R, and shell.
  • Fluency in exploratory data analysis and visualization of complex datasets, with the ability to distill observations into actionable recommendations.
  • Deep understanding of NGS workflows from sample extraction to sequencing, and the ability to link bioinformatic findings to wet lab root causes.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with wet lab groups and cross-functional partners, and to explain technical concepts clearly.
  • Ability to work independently while managing multiple objectives and timelines.
  • Comfort adapting quickly when experimental results change the plan, and a desire to work in a fast-paced environment with high impact in a small team.

PREFERRED:

  • Experience supporting regulated or clinical-grade assay development (e.g., CLIA/CAP, FDA submissions), including analytical validation studies.
  • Familiarity with clinical genomics, including oncogenic drivers, actionable biomarkers, targeted therapies, and variant interpretation in oncology.
  • Experience with translational or real-world data analysis, including integrating clinical and genomic data.

About the Opportunity

We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to join our Data and Partner Platform team (DAP) and help shape the future of energy technology. In this role, you will operate at the intersection of deep technical craft and broad organizational impact - driving architectural decisions, mentoring engineers, and building systems that are reliable, scalable, and grounded in the realities of the energy industry. You will be a key technical voice across engineering and a trusted partner to product, operations, and business teams alike.

The Data and Partner Platform team manages partner integrations, data translation, and our Snowflake account. We work closely with most teams across the organization and drive critical platform engineering that runs core business functionality. The team is driven, diverse, and wildly talented. We are driving foundational improvements that improve our agility and speed while maintaining legacy systems.

Main Responsibilities

Technical leadership and vision

  • Champion long-term excellence by envisioning ideal approaches to complex processes and translating the vision into well-scoped, measurable initiatives that can be prioritized alongside business goals.
  • Coordinate across engineering teams to align on technical direction, standards, and best practices.
  • Develop deep domain expertise in utility programs, demand responses, DER lifecycles, wholesale energy markets, and the regulatory realities that shape them, so every technical decision is grounded in how the energy industry actually operates.
  • Collaborate with product and engineering leadership to strike the right balance between business-driven and team-driven priorities, maximizing both velocity and reliability.
  • Build the absolutely coolest stuff of your career and give yourself something to be deeply proud of.

Systems design and data engineering

  • Architect and implement scalable systems for ingesting, processing, observing, and maintaining billions of data points, with performance, accuracy, security, and compliance considered across the full lifecycle.
  • Lead schema design and data flow architecture through a collaborative and inclusive process.
  • Design and build integrations with partner and third party APIs, including OEMs, utility, and data partners, as well as file-driven pipelines (CSV/SFTP/Airflow) that support them.
  • Build and maintain microservices and APIs that other teams confidently depend on, using contract-driven development practices.

Operational excellence and incident response

  • Drive investigations end to end, from initial alert through root cause analysis to resolution, with the composure to lead under pressure and the rigor to prevent recurrence.
  • Build operational scripts, runbooks, and detection tooling that transform one-time triage into repeatable capability for the team.
  • Pursue root causes beyond their symptoms, never accepting "it's working now” without a clear understanding of why it failed and what prevents it from happening again.
  • Monitor cloud costs across the team’s toolset to maintain efficiency and justify expenditure.

Cross functional collaboration and mentorship

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with partner teams across engineering, partner solutions, and business development, leveraging trust to solve cross-team problems no single group could address alone.
  • Mentor and develop engineers across the team and broader organization while remaining open to learning from their experiences and perspectives.
  • Manage access and roles across the stack to deliver predictable, compliant experiences that meet privacy and security requirements.
  • Contribute to product quality by building new features, improving existing ones, and retiring deprecated functionality.

Key Skills & Experience

Engineering craft

  • 7+ years of professional software engineering experience with demonstrated staff-level responsibilities or equivalent scope
  • Proven full-stack engineering background with experience scaling distributed systems and designing solidly-architected microservices
  • Strong proficiency with gRPC/protobuf, RESTful APIs, and contract driven development across multi-repository service meshes.
  • Clear understanding of the distinction between OLAP and OLTP relational databases, with hands-on experience planning and implementing high-performance data processes using both.
  • Demonstrated experience integrating complex partner and third party APIs as well as building and maintaining file-driven data pipelines.

Engineering instincts

  • Relentless drive for quality and performance, with strong testing discipline spanning unit, integration, TDD, and end to end approaches.
  • Proactive approach to observability. You ensure the right context surfaces in exceptions and logs to enable rapid and accurate troubleshooting.
  • Strong data-integrity instincts and incident-response composure, with the ability to lead high-severity, multi-system investigations from first alert to final root cause.
  • Experience in support-adjacent roles including on-call rotations, triage, or customer facing resolution that has provided you empathy for how systems fail and how users get stuck.
  • Thoughtful, judicious use of AI/LLM tooling to improve efficiency without over-reliance.

Communication and presence

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills. You have a talent for producing clear, concise design documents, data model references, and runbooks that become team-standard reference material.
  • Ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy while providing technical vision and guiding the team toward scalable, well-considered solutions.
  • Collaborative, warm, and generous with colleagues, with a genuine investment in helping others succeed.

Nice to haves

  • Prior experience in the energy industry, including familiarity with utility programs, demand response, DER management, or wholesale energy markets.
  • Experience working in regulated industries with compliance and data privacy requirements.
  • Background in building internal developer tooling, platform capabilities, or shared infrastructure that improves team-wide productivity.
  • Familiarity with data quality monitoring and observability tooling.

Technologies we use

We embrace modern technology and are excited to grow our stack collaboratively. For this role, we're looking for strong familiarity with the majority of these technologies and solid expertise in several:

  • AWS, S3, SNS/SQS, RabbitMQ
  • Snowflake, dbt, Fivetran, Postgres, and MongoDB
  • gRPC/protobuf, React, TypeScript, Java, Spring Boot, Python
  • DataDog, Metaplane
  • Airflow, Docker, Robot Framework
  • Sigma

  • Make an immediate impact: New employees can expect to be given real responsibility for bringing new technologies to the marketplace. You are empowered to perform as soon as you join the team!

EnergyHub empowers utilities and their customers to create a clean, distributed energy future. We help consumers turn their smart thermostats, EVs, batteries, and other products into virtual power plants that keep the grid stable and enable higher penetration of solar and wind power.

  • You have built and run an AEO program from first principles. You write question-based prompts and define the KPIs (citation share, visibility, share of voice). You pick a tracking tool and can say what is working, what is not, and what to do next.
  • You have deep technical SEO skills on a large, complex site. Rendering and prerendering, crawl behavior, structured data, internal linking, migrations, and recovery from Google algorithm updates. Babylist has XM+ registry URLs and XK guides, so scale problems are the normal case.
  • You measure results beyond clicks. You link AI visibility, citations, and brand search to signups and revenue, and you work with paid search on how to attribute them.
  • You build with AI.You have shipped AI-assisted workflows, programmatic pages, or internal tools that moved rankings or citations. You would rather build a system that compounds than ship one-off pages.
  • Applied AEO or GEO experience, paired with a proven track record owning organic growth results. Experience at a consumer brand, marketplace, or publisher with a large content library is a plus.
  • You set content standards that drive organic traffic. FAQ structure, freshness cadence, and formatting that earns citations, delivered to editors and freelance writers as guidance they can use.
  • You are hands-on. You pull the data, write the brief, and fix the markup yourself.Nice to have: experience driving discovery through Reddit, YouTube, or short-form video, and building partner or sponsored organic programs without hurting editorial trust.
  • You naturally reach for AI in your work — at Babylist, every team uses AI daily. You're already using it to move faster and improve your output, and you stay curious about what's coming next.
  • You understand agentic commerce, where AI assistants research and buy products for parents. You make sure Babylist’s product data, registry, and shop pages are structured so those agents can read, compare, and recommend them.

How You'll Make an Impact

  • Own the organic search roadmap and its KPIs: SEO-driven activated registries against plan, clicks, top-3 rankings, and AEO citation share and visibility.
  • In your first 90 days, review our AEO tracking (two overlapping tools today), pick one, and lock the prompt framework and KPIs for Registry, Health and Shop.
  • Keep Google rankings stable and growing across the top categories of Babylist’s business. That covers the technical backlog, internal linking, and content freshness.
  • Move non-Registry visibility up in the categories where we trail the category leader today, with a thoughtful and actionable roadmap.
  • Build AI-driven systems with the internal AI Enablement team and Engineering. Replace vendor tools where an in-house build does the job, and articulate the tradeoffs.
  • Set the content playbook with Editorial: FAQ structure, update cadence, and what earns citations.
  • Partner with marketing to find new discovery channels like social and Reddit and measure whether they change AI citations and overall discoverability.
  • Co-own brand search strategy and attribution with Paid Search.
  • Publish a monthly and quarterly SEO and AEO reviews for the organization with information on performance vs. plan and key projects.
  • Be the company's source of SEO and AEO guidance across internal communications.
  • Tie organic discoverability to actual business impact including traffic that converts to registry signups and revenue.
  • Implement an agentic commerce roadmap for Babylist.

Why This Role

  • Babylist has the highest citation and visibility scores in its competitive set of registry queries. Holding that position as AI search changes takes a real roadmap, and you will build it.
  • Room to grow in Health. Health is a newer area for Babylist, and there is a real opportunity to expand our reach with strong content and a sharp roadmap.
  • You help define success. You co-build the 2027 goals with leadership and own the measurement behind them.

About Compensation

We use a market-based approach to compensation. The starting salary range for this role is:

$143,788.00 to $191,730.00

Your starting salary will be based on your location, experience, and qualifications, with increases over time tied to performance, role growth, and internal pay equity.

Who We Are

Babylist is the leading platform for expecting and new families. More than 10 million people shop with Babylist every year, making it the go-to destination for seamless purchasing, guidance, and expert recommendations. As a modern, AI-forward tech company, Babylist has expanded from a universal registry into a full ecosystem — the Babylist Shop, Babylist Health, Babylist Money, NYC and LA showrooms, branded content, and more — generating $750M in revenue in 2025. Building the generational brand in baby, Babylist is reshaping the $235B kids and baby market and helping parents feel confident, connected, and cared for at every step.

Our Ways of Working

Babylist is remote-first with team members across the U.S. and Canada who move fast, think smart, and use AI as part of how they work every day — not as an experiment, as an expectation. We come together twice a year to build the relationships behind the work, and we hire people who are genuinely excited about what's possible and prove it through how they show up.

Why You Will Love Working At Babylist

Our Culture

  • We work with focus and intention, then step away to recharge
  • We believe in exceptional management, and we invest in the tools and the time to connect with colleagues
  • We build products that positively impact millions of people's lives
  • AI is part of how we work, not a side experiment. You'll have leading tools like Claude and ChatGPT from day one, with no waiting on access, so the busywork gets handled and your judgment goes where it counts

We are a cloud-based public safety platform and design powerful, scalable, and elegant software products that set a new standard for the tools upon which our first responders rely. Our users are diverse, and we are therefore committed to embracing diversity of thought and experience within our team.

Product Designers at Mark43 lead strategically, integrate various systems, champion design ideation, simplify complex workflows by collaborating with stakeholders, advocate for users, and deliver impactful designs for direct users in law enforcement agencies. You will be focusing on one product area, but have an impact on a breathe of various product areas including Computer Aided Dispatch, Records Management, Advanced Analytics/Insights, and mobile applications. At Mark43,

  • You will lead design solutions for law enforcement, EMS, firefighters, other first responders, and 911 dispatchers. The design focus will be on enhancing public safety, improving their focus, and minimizing cognitive load through effective information design, intuitive visual designs, dynamic animations, and responsive feedback mechanisms.

jobs.excerpt: Reports to: Senior Manager, Security Operations Center Location: Remote AustraliaCompensation Range: $110,000 to $140,000 AUD base plus bonus and equity What We Do:Cybercrime is growing, and more businesses are getting hit by threats that used to target only the biggest organizations.
jobs.description:
Reports to: Senior Manager, Security Operations Center

Location: Remote Australia

Compensation Range: $110,000 to $140,000 AUD base plus bonus and equity

What We Do:

Cybercrime is growing, and more businesses are getting hit by threats that used to target only the biggest organizations. That pushes defenders like us to operate at the highest level, and it deepens our need for good people who want to make a meaningful impact.

Founded in 2015 by former NSA cyber operators, Huntress is a remote-first team working to make enterprise-grade cybersecurity accessible to businesses of all sizes. We work closely with security teams and service providers protecting complex environments, often without the time or headcount to handle it all. That’s why we build our technology in-house and back it with a 24/7 human-led Security Operations Center (SOC). As a result, our platform is never disconnected from the experts who manage it, ensuring our customers' protection.

Huntress now secures more than 5M endpoints and 14M identities worldwide. Those numbers keep growing because more businesses rely on us to help carry the load and operate with more confidence. Every day, you can see that commitment in how we stand with our customers and how we show up for each other.

What You’ll Do:

You’re a hands-on SOC Analyst who thrives on detecting and responding to cybercrime. You’ll triage Active Hands-On Keyboard intrusions, track attackers through networks, and help remove them before they achieve their objectives. You’ll contextualise endpoint telemetry, analyse logs, leverage forensic artifacts, and understand malware to uncover the full scope of an intrusion.

You give a $ht about protecting customers and improving how the team operates, taking ownership of investigations and acting on the information available. You bring Warrior Spirit to complex incidents, staying resilient and composed under pressure. You are Outcome-Obsessed, measuring your work by the threats contained, customers protected, and actionable remediation delivered. Alongside alert triage and intrusion response, you’ll support sales, collaborate with Product to shape Huntress’ MDR service and platform, and have opportunities to contribute across Incident Response, Security Operations, Threat Hunting, and Detection Engineering. We’ll also support you in sharing your work through blogs, conference talks, webinars, and research publications that build your personal brand and the broader security community.

You’ll need to be available to work one of the following shifts:

  • Western Australia: Monday to Friday, 8:00 am - 4:00 pm AWST
  • East Coast: Monday to Friday, 9:00 am - 5:00 pm AEST
  • East Coast: Tuesday to Friday, 8:00 am - 6:00 pm AEST

Responsibilities:

  • Triage, investigate, respond to, and remediate alerts generated by the Huntress platform.
  • Review EDR/SIEM telemetry, log sources, and forensic artifacts to determine the root cause of attacks where possible and provide the remediation needed to remove the threat.
  • Perform dynamic analysis of malware when required to extract indicators of compromise or determine a file’s malicious intent.
  • Contribute to and refine detection capabilities and queue hygiene through crafting and tuning signals to address emerging threats.
  • Investigate activity in Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace and deliver actionable remediation advice for compromised tenants.
  • Continue to grow your skills and knowledge through real-world intrusion data, paid training opportunities, and responsible use of AI tools to support research, summarise findings, and accelerate routine analysis while validating outputs.
  • Support customer success by assisting our SOC Support team with customer/partner escalations related to threat-related and SOC-relevant questions.
  • Help through partnering with Product and Engineering Teams to continue to evolve Human Led Agentic workflows

What You Bring To The Team:

  • You have 2+ years of experience in SOC, Incident Response, Managed Detection and Response, or Digital Forensics roles.
  • You have demonstrated experience with at least one of Windows, Linux, or macOS, including attack surfaces, malware analysis, and basic threat actor tools and techniques.
  • You understand common system administration skills and how threat actors abuse them to achieve their goals, including Active Directory, PowerShell, Group Policy, and local account creation.
  • You are familiar with the techniques and tactics in MITRE ATT&CK, including credential dumping, lateral movement, persistence mechanisms, and exfiltration techniques.
  • You have a working knowledge of core networking concepts, including common ports and protocols, NAT, public and private IP addresses, and VLANs.
  • You have a passion for forensics and enjoy digging into logs, processes, and artifacts to understand intrusions and outmaneuver attackers.
  • You communicate clearly in writing and verbally, simplify complex technical findings for diverse audiences, and demonstrate self-guided learning that keeps your skills current.
  • You use AI to work faster and smarter in day-to-day security analysis, applying sound judgment and validating its output before acting on it.
  • You enjoy working with a fun, supportive team, bring a genuine team-player mindset, and help deliver great outcomes with a smile, a laugh, and a dash of witty (but accurate) memes.
  • A desire to hold your manager accountable for delivering ice cream at the Australian Security Offsite.

What We Offer:

  • Fully remote work
  • At least one annual trip to the US for Summer Summit, with additional local events in Australia!
  • New starter home office set up reimbursement ($800 AUD)
  • 12 weeks paid parental leave for both primary and secondary carers
  • Monthly digital allowance for personal phone and internet costs ($185 AUD)
  • Monthly home office tech stipend to upgrade or replace equipment ($40 AUD)
  • Subsidised private health insurance through our preferred provider
  • Stock options for all full-time employees
  • Access to the BetterUp platform for coaching, personal, and professional growth

Huntress is committed to creating a culture of inclusivity where every single member of our team is valued, has a voice, and is empowered to come to work every day just as they are.

We do not discriminate based on race, ethnicity, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, veteran status, genetic information, marital status, or any other legally protected status.

People from all culturally diverse backgrounds, including Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander Peoples, are encouraged to apply.

We do discriminate against hackers who try to exploit businesses of all sizes.

Accommodations:

If you require reasonable accommodation to complete this application, interview, or pre-employment testing or participate in the employee selection process, please direct your inquiries to . Please note that non-accommodation requests to this inbox will not receive a response.

Huntress uses artificial intelligence tools to assist in reviewing and evaluating job applications, including resume screening, skills assessment, and candidate matching and comparisons. These AI tools support our human recruiters in the initial review process, but do not make final hiring decisions without human involvement. By submitting your application, you acknowledge this use of AI in our recruitment process. Please review our Candidate Privacy Notice for more details on our practices and your data privacy rights.

jobs.description:
Job Title: General Manager
Company: Teletask
Location: US, Remote
Employment Type : Full-time

About Teletask

Teletask powers public sector communication. Government and public health agencies use our automated text, voice and email outreach, two-way texting and digital workflows (surveys, e-signature, scheduling) to reach the families they serve. Our largest footprint is WIC (Women, Infants & Children) nutrition programs, where Teletask messaging drives appointment attendance for over 6 million participants across 38 US states, with more than 100 million messages sent each year.

Teletask is part of Solen Software Group, which acquires and holds vertical market software businesses for the long term. The business is now at an inflection point and looking for a General Manager who will lead its next chapter of growth and build the commercial engine, team, and operating infrastructure to match the product.

The Opportunity

This is a general-manager role for someone who knows the industry from the inside. You will own the business's P&L, its growth, its product direction, its most important customer relationships, and its team, reporting to a Solen Portfolio Leader or Operating Partner and working within Solen's business systems and targets.

What You Will Own

Business Performance

  • Own the full P&L: revenue, gross margin, EBITDA, net revenue retention and cash.
  • Run a monthly operating cadence (KPIs, forecast vs. plan, actions) and report it to your Solen Portfolio Leader.
  • Move the business up a Business Health Score (BHS) tier and improve its Rule of 40 through deliberate trade-offs between growth and profitability.
  • Deliver the business's EBITDA growth as its contribution to Solen's Yearly Operations Goal (YOG), our portfolio-wide EBITDA growth target.
  • Lead budgeting and forecasting with ROI discipline on every initiative and hire.

Organic & Inorganic Growth

  • Grow ARR at a double-digit rate every year through new logos, expansion, pricing and retention.
  • Own the pipeline from first contact to signed agreement across agency directors, state IT and operations leaders, and procurement officers.
  • Build the sales playbook: ICP, outreach, discovery, proposal framework and RFP responses, with a repeatable path from local agency to statewide contract.
  • Own pricing: re-evaluate customer usage, then set packaging, contract terms and price increases on the existing customer base.
  • Cut churn by finding at-risk accounts early and running retention plays.
  • Map the acquirable companies in the industry; source and qualify add-on targets and support integration.

Industry Vision & Product Roadmap

  • Own a 1–3 year thesis on where the industry is heading: regulation, workflows, buyers and technology.
  • Turn the thesis and customer needs into a roadmap ranked by ROI and by development effort vs. time-to-market.
  • Partner with product and engineering leads on delivery; find adjacent workflows the business can serve.

Customer & Market Leadership

  • Personally own executive relationships with the top accounts, including renewals, escalations and major expansions.
  • Hold growth, NRR and logo-retention targets.
  • Coordinate client services, onboarding and product so customers adopt more and expand.
  • Represent the business at WIC, public health and government technology conferences and associations to build brand and pipeline; work with Solen Marketing on materials and web presence.

Team, AI Leverage & Value Creation Plan

  • Lead a team of 5–10. Hire, develop and, where needed, replace people so that 90%+ of key seats are held by A players, and build the documentation and cross-training that keep the business running through any leadership change.
  • Drive AI adoption across every function and build revenue-generating AI capabilities into the product.
  • Own and deliver the multi-year value creation plan (VCP) that drives the business's contribution to the YOG.

Who You Are

  • Hands-on industry operator. Real depth in the industry; equally comfortable in a strategy session, a customer escalation and a roadmap trade-off.
  • Player-coach. Gets outsized output from a small team through systems, not headcount.
  • Commercially credible. Sells, retains and expands accounts personally.
  • Numbers-driven owner. Applies ROI discipline to every roadmap item, initiative and hire, and thinks in years, not quarters.
  • Principled. Lives the Solen-isms and the Solen Principles of Transformation, and runs the business on Solen's business systems.

Requires Qialifications

  • 8+ years in operations, sales, business development or general management, including 5+ years in the industry or selling into it.
  • Fluent in how government health and human services programs operate, who buys, and how they are funded.
  • Has owned a P&L or a functional budget and can speak to its figures and the monthly metrics they reported.
  • Documented multi-year revenue growth that they personally owned, with before and after numbers.
  • Has personally closed and expanded major accounts; can provide customer references in the vertical.
  • Has hired and, where needed, replaced direct reports.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience buying or selling B2B software to customers in the industry.
  • Has led price increases, packaging changes, churn reduction or product repositioning.
  • Has sourced, diligenced or integrated an acquisition.
  • Visible in the industry through speaking, associations, analyst relationships or a recognized network.
  • Has built and delivered a multi-year operating or value creation plan with stated targets.
  • Has deployed AI in a business function or product.
  • Understands how state and local health department procurement works: RFPs, statewide contracts and reseller channels.

What Success Looks Like

First 90 days

  • Meet the top state and local agency accounts, take over founder-held relationships, and surface upsell opportunities and at-risk accounts.
  • Map the customer base by program (statewide WIC, local WIC, public health, other), usage, price per participant, expansion potential and risk.
  • Learn the P&L and set up the monthly operating cadence.
  • Assess the team against key seats, name any gaps, and identify processes that depend on a single person.
  • Build the first outbound sales playbook: ICP, outreach, discovery questions and proposal framework, starting with WIC states not yet served.
  • Draft the first industry thesis and a shortlist of AI opportunities, building on the AI features already in the product.

First 12 months

  • ARR growing at double digits, in line with the VCP target, with new states won and local agencies converted to statewide contracts.
  • BHS tier improved and EBITDA contribution to the YOG on track.
  • A usage-based pricing strategy agreed with your Portfolio Leader and applied at renewals.
  • An ROI-ranked roadmap in delivery.
  • Key seats held by A players, with onboarding materials and documented processes so no critical function depends on one person.
  • An outbound sales motion in place alongside a qualified list of add-on targets.
  • Value creation plan agreed and on track.

Who You Will Work With

You run the business day to day and report to a Solen Portfolio Leader or Operating Partner. You have real decision rights, exercised within Solen's business systems and against the targets agreed with your Portfolio Leader (BHS, YOG and the VCP). You will see the company's financials, product strategy and customer relationships from day one. You will lead a team of 5–10 across sales, client services, product and operations and work closely with product and engineering leads. You will also draw on Solen's functional leads in marketing, pricing, finance, talent and AI.

What We Offer

  • Ownership of a profitable software business and its P&L from day one, accountable to your Portfolio Leader.
  • Autonomy to build the commercial engine, the processes and the team, within Solen's business systems and targets.
  • A long-term horizon: Solen buys and holds, so there is no forced exit.
  • Direct coaching from your Portfolio Leader, plus access to the portfolio, best-practice guilds and functional leads across vertical software.

Recruitment Disclaimer

Solen Software Group will never request payment, banking information, or other sensitive personal or financial details during any stage of the recruitment process. All official communication will come from a verified @solensoftwaregroup.com email address. Any outreach outside these standards should be disregarded and reported through our official channels.

We thank all applicants for their interest in joining Solen Software Group. Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

Salary: $160,000 – $200,000 / year

Together with Anthropic, CodePath launched Claude Corps in June 2026, a national fellowship program with a $150 million commitment to place 1,000 AI-trained fellows at nonprofits across America.

As a CodePath Mentor, you are the full-time coach and guide for a portfolio of roughly ten pods: about 20 fellows across 8–12 host organizations, from pre-Basecamp through the final day of the program. Your job is to help each fellow succeed not only in building with AI, but in navigating the organization around the work: understanding the problem, identifying the right stakeholders, communicating ideas clearly, building buy-in, and turning an AI-enabled solution into something people will actually use.

The host organization directs the fellow's day-to-day work, the curriculum team owns what they learn, and your Sr. Manager of AI Practice is the manager of record who holds the performance bar. You carry the throughline across the fellow experience: you know your pods end to end, spot patterns and roadblocks early, coach fellows through ambiguity, and bring in deeper technical expertise when needed.

The work combines asynchronous coaching and feedback with regular 1:1s, office hours, milestone reviews, roadmap and project feedback, and synchronous coaching when a fellow needs more than text. Fellows may be building technical integrations, designing AI-enabled workflows, educating an organization on AI, or helping a nonprofit adopt an entirely new way of working.

You do not need to be the deepest software engineer in the room. You do need enough technical fluency to understand what fellows are building, learn unfamiliar technologies quickly, and help them reason through AI-enabled solutions. Just as importantly, you need the judgment and coaching ability to help an early-career fellow navigate the people, communication, and organizational challenges that determine whether their work succeeds.

This role is built for someone who gets energy from helping other people succeed. You may come from engineering, consulting, implementation, technical program management, AI enablement, education, or another client-facing technical environment. What matters most is that you have personally navigated ambiguity, helped people or organizations adopt technology, and can coach fellows through doing the same.

Key Responsibilities

Coach your pods

  • Carry roughly 20 pods (up to 40 fellows across 16 to 24 host organizations) full-time from pre-Basecamp through final day, calibrating your time across the portfolio rather than sinking into one pod
  • Facilitate weekly 1:1s with all Fellows who report to you and document their progress, challenges, and successes using the tooling Claude Corps operates on
  • Coach fellows through ambiguous projects, helping them clarify the problem, understand organizational context, identify stakeholders, and determine the right next step
  • Give structured feedback on fellows' real work, including project plans, roadmap drafts, architecture proposals, presentations, technical implementations, and QBR deliverables
  • Help fellows strengthen the professional skills required to succeed inside their host organizations, including communication, stakeholder management, presentations, prioritization, and navigating feedback
  • Lead each fellow's Day 30/90/180/270 milestone review; own the fellow-level synthesis and hand it up to your Sr. Manager of AI Practice, who owns the roll-up and performance call

Deliver the curriculum in your pods

  • Deliver the just-in-time modules the curriculum team designs; author lane- or pod-specific content when they commission it because you have seen the gap from closer in
  • Coach fellows on applying AI tools and workflows to real organizational problems rather than simply completing technical exercises
  • Frame and debrief the cohort-wide all-hands your Sr. Manager of AI Practice runs, and the sessions where the curriculum team or a guest teaches your fellows directly
  • Co-lead the Basecamp practical assessment alongside Anthropic's instructors; it is your first calibration on each cohort

Help fellows navigate organizations

  • Coach fellows through stakeholder discovery, requirements gathering, presentations, organizational buy-in, and change management
  • Help fellows translate between technical possibilities and the business or mission needs of their host organizations
  • Guide fellows through situations where the technical solution is only part of the challenge and adoption, communication, or organizational alignment is the real blocker
  • Model how to work effectively with technical and nontechnical stakeholders, particularly in organizations that may be early in their AI adoption journey

Keep the program honest

  • When the same problem shows up across three fellows, raise it to the right owner: the Claude Corps leadership team for program efficacy, the curriculum team for curriculum, partner experts for technical depth, host-org managers for a host issue, or your Sr. Manager of AI Practice for a delivery or performance issue
  • Be the first stop when a fellow's work is at risk, whether the roadblock is technical, organizational, or professional; surface significant risks to your Sr. Manager of AI Practice, who owns the escalation
  • Work AI-natively: Claude and other modern AI tools should be core to how you research, build, coach, problem-solve, identify patterns, and provide feedback at scale
  • Help fellows develop the judgment to use AI effectively, not simply the ability to operate a particular tool

Key Success Metrics

  • Fellows can point to concrete examples of how your coaching improved their technical judgment, communication, or ability to navigate their host organization
  • 100% of host-org managers you've worked with in the last 30 days can produce one concrete example of your impact
  • You consistently identify recurring technical, professional, and organizational patterns across your pods and surface them to the right program owner
  • Every Day 30 review is done and documented, handed up to your Sr. Manager of AI Practice, with a plan for any fellow whose work is at risk or ready for the next challenge

Qualifications

Required

  • 2–5 years of previous professional experience in software engineering, IT, data, technical program management, implementation, solutions engineering, forward deployed engineering, technical consulting, AI operations, or another technically adjacent role
  • Hands-on, current experience using modern AI tools and workflows. You should be able to speak concretely about how you use tools such as Claude, AI agents, LLM-based applications, automation, or similar technologies to solve real problems
  • Real coaching, mentorship, people-development, or management experience with concrete examples of helping someone navigate a challenge and become more successful
  • Experience working across stakeholders to understand a problem, clarify needs, recommend or implement a solution, and help people adopt a new way of working
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to facilitate discussions, coach someone through an important presentation, and provide thoughtful asynchronous feedback
  • Comfortable operating as a technical generalist: you can learn quickly, ask the right questions, understand unfamiliar systems, and bring in deeper expertise when needed
  • Comfortable coaching early-career professionals through ambiguity, feedback, organizational dynamics, and the expectations of working in a professional environment
  • Comfortable with remote, synchronous obligations across U.S. time zones and about two evenings a month for cohort sessions and milestone reviews

Preferred

  • Client-facing consulting or implementation experience, particularly working with small businesses, nonprofits, education organizations, or teams adopting new technology
  • Experience helping an organization adopt AI, automation, new software, or another significant change in how work gets done
  • TA, bootcamp coach, fellowship mentor, instructor, manager, career coach, or other experience developing early-career technical talent
  • Experience facilitating workshops, presentations, professional learning, or technical training
  • Experience in a small or scrappy organization where understanding the business context was as important as delivering the technical solution

Compensation

CodePath has standardized salaries based on the position's level, no matter where you live. For this role, we're hiring for an Individual Contributor level position at an annual salary of $110,000 to $124,500. Salary is determined based on your relevant experience and skills as evaluated through our interview process.

Full-Time Employee Benefits

This is a 100% remote position—work from anywhere in the U.S.! CodePath prioritizes employee well-being with a competitive benefits package to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance.

  • Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance (90% employer-covered for employees and dependents), employer-funded healthcare reimbursement, FSAs, and Employee Assistance Program
  • Financial Security: 401(k), employer-paid life & disability insurance, and identity theft protection
  • Work-Life Balance: Generous PTO, paid holidays, 10 weeks of fully paid parental leave, and an annual year-end company closure (Dec 24 – Jan 2)
  • Professional Growth: $1,000 annual professional development stipend and home office setup support
  • Student Loan Forgiveness: CodePath is a qualifying employer for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), helping employees manage student loan debt
  • Additional Perks: Pet wellness plans, legal services, home/auto insurance discounts, and exclusive marketplace savings

jobs.description:
About AlphaSense:

AlphaSense is the AI platform redefining market intelligence and workflow orchestration, trusted by thousands of leading organizations to drive faster, more confident decisions in business and finance. The platform combines domain-specific AI with a vast content universe of over 500 million premium business documents — including equity research, earnings calls, expert interviews, filings, news, and internal proprietary content. Purpose-built for speed, accuracy, and enterprise-grade security, AlphaSense helps teams extract critical insights, uncover market-moving trends, and automate complex workflows with high-quality outputs. With AI solutions like Generative Search, Generative Grid, and Deep Research, AlphaSense delivers the clarity and depth professionals need to navigate complexity and obtain accurate, real-time information quickly. For more information, visit . Come join us.

About the Role:

AlphaSense runs a large-scale, Kubernetes-native platform built on a modern microservices architecture, serving the majority of the Fortune 500. We are moving it to a cell-based architecture, where each cell is an independent deployment of the platform.

The hardest part is data. Our platform relies on a broad ecosystem of data platforms and storage systems, including Vespa, MongoDB, ClickHouse, Redis, ScyllaDB, PostgreSQL, Temporal, and Kafka, to name a few. This role is focused on the Data Platform: the capabilities that let engineering teams build, run, and scale their storage at large scale without each team becoming an expert in every system.

You will help set the technical direction for the Data Platform and build it rather than only specify it. A central part of the work is building the capabilities for large-scale data migrations, so we can create, move, split, and rebalance data across cells and geographies as the cell-based architecture rolls out.

We prefer managed solutions over self-hosted ones, and we expect engineers to own their storage. Teams run what they build, and this role makes that model work at scale: you build it, you run it, and you scale it. Your job is to give teams the platform, standards, and tooling to do that safely, and to own the reliability and scalability of the platform itself.

Responsibilities:

  • Help set the architecture and roadmap for the Data Platform and the storage ecosystem behind it
  • Build the capabilities for large-scale data migrations across cells, regions, and geographies, including tooling for moving, splitting, validating, and rolling back data with minimal downtime
  • Enable product teams self-service ways to provision, operate, and scale their own storage
  • Drive the data-layer changes that cell-based architecture requires, including data placement, tenant routing, replication, and isolation
  • Define and apply the managed-first approach: choose managed services where they fit, and build and run self-managed systems only where there is a clear reason
  • Find and close scalability gaps in data stores across regions, cells and deployment models
  • Build shared libraries that give product teams self-service storage capabilities
  • Closely partner with Cloud Platform, SRE, and DevEx teams
  • Raise the architectural bar across the organization and mentor Staff and Senior engineers
  • Apply AI tooling to data platform work, such as slow query reviews and incident diagnosis

Requirements:

  • Deep hands-on experience designing and operating data platforms and storage systems
  • Production large-scale experience with storages (e.g. MongoDB, ClickHouse, Redis, PostgreSQL)
  • Cloud-native data storage experience, including managed data services on AWS
  • Strong background in Kubernetes and containers
  • Track record of designing and running large-scale data migrations, including live migrations
  • Experience with cell-based, multi-tenant or multi-region architectures
  • Experience building platforms and tooling that other engineers use, and comfort with a model where engineers own their storage and run what they build
  • Demonstrated ability to land significant changes in code owned by other teams
  • A record of spotting data scalability and reliability limits before they turn into incidents
  • Ability and desire to design, lead, influence, and deliver on ambitious technical roadmaps

Nice to have:

  • Experience running storage systems on top of Kubernetes
  • Experience building control planes with Crossplane
  • Experience with private, isolated, on-premises, or air-gapped deployments

We work closely with teams across the company to design systems that meet real-world operational, regulatory, and business needs.

  • Stay current with fintech, tech, and compliance trends, and evolve our systems accordingly

Preferred Qualifications

  • Domain knowledge: Experience in financial domains—such as payments, disbursements, custody, or cards—is a strong plus, but not required.

jobs.excerpt: At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.
jobs.description:
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

Affirm's engineering team is building a large-scale, fault-tolerant, and global infrastructure that is shared across multiple financial products, merchants, and vendors. Ensuring that our infrastructure is transparently available to all engineers is critical to the success of the business. We pride ourselves on our culture across engineering of writing blameless postmortems as well as writing detailed tech specs and gathering feedback before large changes to systems.

The AI Platform team owns Affirm's paved path for building, running, evaluating, and governing AI systems. Our customers are not only Affirm users, but also every engineer and a growing set of production workloads at Affirm. As a team, we are responsible for building and exposing simple, governed interfaces to models, tools, and agents, with identity, cost attribution, reliability, and security built in. Examples of components we own include the LLM Gateway that fronts every approved model (Claude, ChatGPT, and open-weight models across AWS Bedrock and other providers), the MCP Gateway that mediates and audits tool calls, the Agent Runtime that gives agentic workloads bounded execution, and the evals and observability layer that tells teams whether an AI change is better, cheaper, or safe to ship. We are early: the gateway is in daily use across engineering, the first production agent is live, and the next year takes us from developer productivity to production inference and agents.


What You'll Do

  • Plan, execute, and own technical decisions and projects within the AI Platform team, from design through launch and on-call.
  • Design and build the gateway, runtime, and evaluation services that take AI workloads at Affirm from pilot to production, securely scaling across millions of users and their transactions.
  • Make AI spend attributable and governable: build the identity, quota, routing, caching, and failover controls that let teams adopt new models and tools without re-solving the same platform problems.
  • Partner with security, infrastructure, and product engineering teams to set the guardrails for agentic workloads and the on-behalf-of identity model for tool access.
  • Create and monitor metrics for your team's systems, and own the operational health of what you ship: monitoring, alerting, runbooks, and on-call.
  • Set and improve code review and design standards, and advocate for them beyond your team through writing and tech talks.
  • Use AI tools and agentic workflows every day as a multiplier for your own code, design review, and operations, and push the team on what a small AI-native team can deliver.
  • Educate, mentor, and grow engineers in the team, and drive best practices around design, coding, and testing.

What We Look For

  • You have 4+ years of experience designing, developing and launching backend systems at scale using languages like Python or Kotlin.
  • You have a track record of developing highly available distributed systems using technologies like AWS, MySQL and Kubernetes.
  • You have practical experience building with LLMs, agents, or AI frameworks in production: inference APIs, LLM gateways (LiteLLM or similar), MCP, tool calling, evals, or agent runtimes.
  • You understand AI usage and the infrastructure needed to support and leverage AI workloads across different disciplines.
  • You have experience defining a technical plan for the delivery of a significant feature or system component with an elegant, simple and extensible design. You write high quality code that is easily understood and used by others.
  • You are proficient at making significant changes in a large code base, and have developed a suite of tools and practices that enable you and your team to do so safely.
  • Your experience demonstrates that you take ownership of your growth, proactively seeking feedback from your team, your manager, and your stakeholders.
  • You have strong verbal and written communication skills that support effective collaboration with our global engineering team.
  • This position requires either equivalent practical experience or a Bachelor’s degree in a related field.

This remote role is open only to candidates residing in Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, Ontario, Prince Edward Island, or Saskatchewan

Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include equity rewards, monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents.)

CAN base pay range per year: $153,000 - $213,000 CAD

Remote-first with flexibility built inAffirm is proud to be a remote-first company. Most roles can be done from almost anywhere within the country of employment. Some positions may occasionally require in-person work at an Affirm office, and a few are office-based due to the nature of the work. All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience.

Benefits designed for youOur benefits reflect our commitment to care, transparency, and flexibility. Here are a few highlights:

  • Health coverage at no cost: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and their dependents.
  • Spending stipends: Monthly stipends support your tech setup, and the ability to choose health and wellness options that are right for you.
  • Time off to recharge: Flexible time off and generous holiday calendars help you rest when you need to.
  • Own a piece of what you build: Our employee stock purchase plan (ESPP) lets you buy Affirm stock at a discount.

We’re committed to providing an inclusive interview process, including accommodations for candidates with disabilities. If you need support, we’re happy to help.

Voltus is the leading DER technology platform and virtual power plant operator, connecting distributed energy resources to electricity markets to deliver less expensive, more reliable, and more sustainable electricity. We hire teammates who are bright, gritty, and good, with a genuine passion for a cleaner energy future.

The Role

As a Product Manager on the Market Product Team, you will own product outcomes that drive growth, margin and retention in our market products in MISO and IESO. From the moment a new opportunity is identified until that value is realized by the business, you are the connective tissue between customer needs, energy market complexity and the operations and engineering team that builds the systems that maximize financial return and operate to ensure we meet our commitments to markets, customers and Voltans.

Voltus is a fully distributed company and this job is remote. You have the flexibility to work from anywhere, but your workday must align with a US-based time zone.

  • Own the product vision, roadmap, success criteria and metrics for MISO and IESO, starting with delivering the upcoming MISO and IESO launches.

  • Collaborate with market leaders to develop and prioritize outcomes for MISO and IESO that will drive the most impact on business objectives and communicate results with stakeholders across the organization

  • Collaborate with engineering manager(s) and tech leads to align on product requirements and manage the day-to-day efforts of ongoing initiatives and workstreams

  • Formulate and propose investment theses grounded in user needs, market mechanics, and business objectives

  • Effectively validate hypotheses and assumptions about market mechanics, user needs, and system behavior

  • Ensure product solutions are operationally viable, adequately supported, and aligned with business and regulatory strategy

Qualifications

  • At least 2-3 years of experience as a product manager or a role building products

  • Ability to read market rules and tariffs directly and reason through complex logic like baseline and performance calculations. Energy experience is a bonus, but you’ll need to get fluent quickly.

  • Exceptionally strong written and verbal communication skills

  • Strong technical acumen — comfortable reviewing specs and engaging deeply with engineers

  • Self-starter with the ability to manage and prioritize multiple work streams simultaneously

  • Ability to distill qualitative and quantitative information into a business case and actionable product decisions

Please note that at this time, we do not sponsor visas or transfers for new hires. Voltus teammates need to be authorized to work from their home location (in the US or Canada, unless otherwise indicated on the role description).

Additionally, while Voltus is an all-remote workplace, we have limitations on where employees are able to work for regulatory and security reasons. jobs.excerpt: Team Leadership & Functional Ownership• Manage, develop, and provide technical oversight to the provider compensation team responsible for more than 200 providers across multiple legal entities and compensation structures.
jobs.description:
Team Leadership & Functional Ownership

• Manage, develop, and provide technical oversight to the provider compensation team responsible for more than 200 providers across multiple legal entities and compensation structures.

• Own the monthly provider compensation close process, including work allocation, review standards, deadlines, issue escalation, and final approval of calculations and accounting entries.

• Establish procedures, review controls, documentation standards, and cross-training to ensure continuity, accuracy, and scalability.

• Serve as the senior escalation point for complex provider compensation questions and disputes.

Provider Compensation Governance & Master Matrix

• Own and maintain the master provider compensation matrix as the authoritative source for all arrangements, including legal entity, effective dates, methodology, rates/percentages, thresholds, guarantees, draws, profit/loss sharing, expense allocations, supervisory fees, incentives, true-up provisions, payment timing, and other contractual terms.

• Ensure new agreements, amendments, renewals, terminations, and provider changes are reflected timely and accurately in the matrix and supporting calculation models.

• Maintain supporting documentation and version control so each calculation can be traced directly to the applicable contractual provision.

• Perform periodic audits of the master matrix against executed agreements, payroll records, accounting schedules, and provider rosters.

Contract Review & Translation to Calculation

• Proactively participate in provider contracting and amendments before execution to ensure compensation terms can be operationalized and calculated accurately.

• Review proposed contractual language and translate economic terms into clear mathematical formulas, calculation examples, data requirements, accounting treatment, and payment schedules.

• Identify ambiguous, conflicting, incomplete, or administratively burdensome provisions and work with Legal, Operations, and leadership to resolve them before execution.

• Assess downstream impacts on payroll, general ledger accounting, intercompany allocations, provider reporting, and system requirements.

• Document approved calculation methodologies and ensure the final model is consistent with the executed agreement.

• Review model and calculations with the provider prior to first pay check to ensure mutual understanding and alignment on timing of deliverables, method of receiving the information, and payment.

Complex Provider Compensation Accounting

• Oversee and review monthly calculations across models including percentage of collections, productivity-based compensation, profit and loss sharing, allocated profit pools, growth incentives, guarantees, draws, supervisory fees, and other custom arrangements.

• Oversee complex profit and loss calculations requiring revenue attribution, direct expenses, shared overhead allocations, provider-specific adjustments, and contractual exclusions or add-backs.

• Ensure accruals, true-ups, liabilities, and related journal entries are recorded accurately and timely in accordance with U.S. GAAP and company policy.

• Own accounting for arrangements spanning multiple entities, including identification, calculation, reconciliation, and documentation of intercompany charges, receivables/payables, and allocations.

• Reconcile compensation calculations and payments to collections, payroll, accounts payable, provider statements, and the general ledger.

Financial Analysis, Reporting & Provider Support

• Review monthly compensation reporting packages, provider statements, variance analyses, and management reporting for accuracy and completeness.

• Analyze productivity, collections, profitability, compensation trends, and material variances; investigate and resolve anomalies.

• Develop dashboards, schedules, and KPIs providing visibility into compensation expense, accrual accuracy, true-ups, and outstanding issues.

• Explain complex calculations, variances, and adjustments clearly to providers, practice administrators, operational leaders, and executives.

Controls, Audit & Process Improvement

• Design and maintain a strong control environment including preparer/reviewer controls, contract-to-calculation validation, change controls, reconciliations, and documented approvals.

• Support internal and external audits with complete, organized, and auditable compensation documentation.

• Identify opportunities to standardize and automate calculations, reporting, provider onboarding, and change-management workflows while preserving individual contract requirements.

• Lead compensation workstreams for acquisitions, provider onboarding, system implementations, and transitions to new compensation models.

• Partner with Finance and executive leadership to identify recurring contractual complexity and recommend more scalable structures and processes.

• Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field required; CPA or advanced degree preferred.

• 7+ years of progressive accounting, financial analysis, or provider compensation experience, including team leadership or ownership of a complex functional process.

• Healthcare accounting experience strongly preferred; physician practice management or multi-site provider compensation experience required.

• Demonstrated experience interpreting complex contracts and converting contractual terms into mathematical calculations, accounting treatments, and repeatable operational processes.

• Experience with complex physician compensation models, including percentage of collections, profit/loss sharing, productivity incentives, guarantees/draws, and custom calculations.

• Experience with multi-entity accounting and intercompany transactions, allocations, reconciliations, and eliminations.

• Strong understanding of U.S. GAAP, accrual accounting, reconciliations, and internal controls.

• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills; experience with ERP, payroll, reporting, and data systems. Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, organizational, documentation, leadership, and communication skills.

Education:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or related field required
  • CPA or advanced degree preferred

Job Type:

  • Full-time

jobs.description:
Role: Senior Manager – Teacher Training and Professional Development, Remote/ Delhi.

Experience: 10-15 years

Salary: Up to 15-20 LPA

About the role -

Building teacher capacity within large-scale government education systems to facilitate student agency is deeply challenging. It requires educators to reexamine long-held beliefs about teaching and gradually build confidence in new classroom practices. We believe that nurturing student agency begins with investing in teachers' own sense of agency.

At scale, the quality of professional development is often compromised by systemic challenges—such as cascade loss, one-size-fits-all approaches, weak feedback loops, and complex classroom realities. Consequently, a gap frequently exists between training delivery and meaningful classroom change.

We are seeking a seasoned professional who brings a strong diagnostic lens to this work. Sitting at the heart of our Curriculum and Pedagogy team, you will own the Teacher Professional Development (TPD) vertical. You will diagnose core systemic gaps, understand the constraints of public education (time, hierarchy, and geography), and work backwards to design practical, scalable, and context-sensitive solutions.

Roles & Responsibilities -

1. Research and Design

  • Model Evolution: Articulate strategic objectives and extend the existing model of teacher learning.
  • Evidence-Based Practices: Research global and local best practices in continuous professional development, mitigating cascade loss, mindset shifts, and instructional coaching.
  • Continuous Improvement: Gather participant feedback and field data to iteratively improve training content.
  • Strategic Ecosystem Partnerships: Collaborate with peer organizations and ecosystem partners in the education domain.
  • Tech Integration: Adapt and integrate tech-based or blended training solutions for scalability.

2. Learning and Development

  • Facilitation: Design and facilitate engaging, high-impact learning experiences for educators.
  • Capacity Building: Upskill internal team members and external Master Trainers to ensure high-quality delivery.

3. Program Management & Collaboration

  • Cross-Functional Alignment: Work closely with the core curriculum team to ensure training design aligns with pedagogical goals.
  • Stakeholder Management: Collaborate with government bodies (such as SCERTs) and internal operations teams to align on training schedules and implementation realities.
  • Team Leadership: Manage and mentor a small, dedicated team to achieve the vertical's strategic goals.

Skills, Experience, and Mindsets

  • Experience: Minimum 10–12 years of overall work experience, with a proven track record in curriculum design and large-scale teacher training for public schools.
  • Classroom Grounding: Prior experience working as a classroom teacher for a few years is highly desirable.
  • Government Relations: Direct experience navigating and working alongside government stakeholders, system leaders, and government school teachers.
  • Domain Expertise: Deep pedagogical knowledge of effective TPD models, adult learning principles, and experiential learning frameworks.
  • Analytical Abilities: Strong capacity to conduct research, analyze qualitative/quantitative data, and clearly articulate systemic bottlenecks.
  • Core Competencies: Outstanding facilitation skills for both small and large groups; exceptional observation skills to assess teacher needs accurately.
  • Mindset: Highly creative, collaborative, resilient, and entrepreneurial—capable of balancing design rigor with the flexibility required for ground-level implementation.

Hiring Process-

  • Round 1 (R1)
  • Pre-Work
  • Final Interview (In-Person)
