jobs.description:
About the team

Zillow’s Contingent Workforce Program team sits within the Employee Services & Operations (ES&O) organization and plays a vital role in managing our contractor and contingent labor population. The team aligns people, processes, and systems to deliver a consistent, compliant, and high-quality experience for contingent workers and their managers.

Focused on operational excellence and cross-functional partnership, the team strengthens program governance, streamlines workflows, and partners across the People organization, Product & Technology, Strategic Sourcing, and other shared services to deliver scalable solutions that support business agility.

About the role

As Senior Program Manager, Contingent Workforce, you will lead the strategy, operations, and continuous improvement of Zillow Group’s contingent workforce program. Reporting to the Senior Manager of ES&O Programs, you’ll lead a team responsible for business partnership, supplier management, systems, and program operations.


In this highly cross-functional role, you’ll partner with Strategic Sourcing, HR Compliance, Product & Technology, IT, Finance, Legal, and the Employee Service Center to strengthen centralized processes, governance, and service delivery. You’ll translate program strategy into actionable roadmaps, develop internal capabilities, and guide the program’s international expansion while supporting the needs of contingent workers, hiring managers, and the business.


You Will

  • Lead the end-to-end strategy, operations, and continuous improvement of the contingent workforce program, strengthening centralized ownership within ES&O through clear decision-making authority, consistent program standards, and defined responsibilities across partner teams.
  • Lead the evolution of the contingent workforce operating model, including bringing key program functions in-house, managing knowledge transfer, and establishing clear ownership, documented processes, and cross-functional handoffs to ensure operational readiness and continuity.
  • Lead and develop the contingent workforce program team, setting priorities, coaching team members, and establishing clear accountability across business partnership, supplier management, systems, and operations.
  • Develop and execute a roadmap for international expansion, partnering with Legal, Strategic Sourcing, and regional People teams to assess local requirements, establish supplier and service delivery models, and implement scalable processes.
  • Design and maintain a program framework that defines intake, engagement models, worker classification, and lifecycle management for staffing, independent contractor, employer-of-record, and statement-of-work engagements in partnership with the appropriate business and functional owners.
  • Establish program governance and controls across worker classification, engagement approvals, assignment duration, onboarding and offboarding, and supplier compliance, partnering with Legal and HR Compliance to address risks and exceptions.
  • Oversee and improve hiring and onboarding workflows, partnering with IT, suppliers, and operational teams to coordinate timely hardware, software, and access provisioning.
  • Own the contingent workforce systems roadmap and business requirements, partnering with Product & Technology and Procurement Systems to strengthen Beeline and Workday integrations, improve data integrity, and deliver automation and system enhancements.
  • Establish scalable financial and supplier management processes with Finance, Procurement, and Strategic Sourcing, including invoice reconciliation, issue resolution, supplier performance monitoring, and contingent workforce spend reporting.
  • Lead program-side supplier lifecycle management, including onboarding, performance reviews, issue resolution, and renewal planning; partner with Strategic Sourcing and Procurement on supplier evaluation, RFPs, commercial negotiations, and sourcing strategies.
  • Define and monitor program performance measures across service delivery, compliance, data quality, supplier performance, and spend; use insights to prioritize improvements and communicate results, risks, and recommendations to leadership.
  • Deliver actionable workforce and spend insights to People partners and business leaders to support workforce planning, budget forecasting, and contingent worker visibility.
  • Develop self-service guidance, training, and communications that help managers, HRBPs, suppliers, and operational partners understand program requirements and navigate support channels.
  • Serve as the point of escalation for complex program issues, coordinating resolution across internal teams and external partners.
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives from discovery through implementation, including project planning, stakeholder alignment, change management, and adoption.
  • Deliver a consistent, well-supported contingent worker and manager experience through clear onboarding, access, support, and offboarding processes appropriate to each engagement type.
This role has been categorized as a Remote position. “Remote” employees do not have a permanent corporate office workplace and, instead, work from a physical location of their choice, which must be identified to the Company. U.S. employees may live in any of the 50 United States, with limited exceptions.In California, Connecticut, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Washington state, and Washington DC the standard base pay range for this role is $112,800.00 - $180,200.00 annually. This base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.In Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Minnesota, Nevada, Ohio, Rhode Island, Vermont, and Virginia the standard base pay range for this role is $107,200.00 - $171,200.00 annually. The base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.In addition to a competitive base salary this position is also eligible for equity awards based on factors such as experience, performance and location. Actual amounts will vary depending on experience, performance and location. Employees in this role will not be paid below the salary threshold for exempt employees in the state where they reside.

Who you are


  • 7+ years of experience designing, implementing, and leading contingent workforce programs in complex, cross-functional environments.
  • Deep expertise in contingent workforce practices, worker classification assessments, engagement requirements, and program governance, with experience partnering with Legal and compliance teams on domestic and international requirements.
  • Proven experience building or transforming contingent workforce programs, translating strategy into clear operating processes, governance, and sustainable service delivery.
  • Experience leading and developing a team, setting priorities, coaching others, and driving accountability for shared outcomes.
  • A strong track record managing MSP, VMS, staffing supplier, and other service provider relationships, with a focus on performance, compliance, cost effectiveness, and continuous improvement.
  • Experience partnering on VMS and HR system integrations, translating business needs into requirements, and improving data quality and operational workflows.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret workforce, supplier, and financial data and translate insights into actionable improvements.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead change, build consensus, and influence stakeholders at all levels.
  • Highly collaborative, with experience working across shared services and matrixed organizations.
  • Comfortable navigating ambiguity, balancing strategic priorities with hands-on problem solving, and providing structure in evolving environments.
  • Excellent communication, project management, and stakeholder engagement skills.

Here at Zillow, we value the experience and perspective of candidates with non-traditional backgrounds. We encourage you to apply if you have transferable skills or related experiences.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience improving contingent workforce invoicing, reconciliation, and spend reporting processes.

At Zillow, we’re reimagining how people move—through the real estate market and through their careers. As the most-visited real estate platform in the U.S., we help people navigate buying, selling, financing and renting with greater ease and confidence. Whether you're working in tech, sales, operations, or design, you’ll be part of a company reshaping an industry and helping more people make home a reality.


How we work is a key part of that transformation. Through Cloud HQ, our strategic approach to distributed work, most employees have the flexibility to work from wherever they’re most productive—enabling us to move fast, stay connected and deliver on our people promise.


Zillow is honored to be recognized among the best workplaces in the U.S. Zillow was named one of FORTUNE 100 Best Companies to Work For® in 2026, and included on TIME’s America’s Best Companies 2026 list, reflecting our commitment to creating an innovative, inclusive, and engaging culture where employees are empowered to grow.


No matter where you sit in the organization, your work will help drive innovation, support our customers, and move the industry—and your career—forward, together.

Overview

DecisionPoint Corporation is seeking a collaborative, detail-oriented UI/Interface Designer, Junior to support the Department of Defense (DoD) Military Community and Family Policy (MC&FP) MODES III program.

The UI/Interface Designer will contribute to the design, enhancement, and optimization of user-centered digital experiences across MC&FP's portfolio of public-facing websites, digital platforms, applications, and internal tools. This role focuses on creating intuitive, visually cohesive, accessible, and responsive user interfaces that improve how service members, military families, survivors, service providers, and internal stakeholders discover, access, and interact with critical programs, information, and resources.

As a member of the Digital Experience & Strategy Team, the UI/Interface Designer will work closely with the Senior UX/UI Researcher & Designer as well as other UX/UI professionals, content strategists, creative specialists, data analysts, data scientists, developers, and cross-functional delivery teams.

The ideal candidate combines strong visual and interaction design capabilities with a human-centered, research-informed approach. They are comfortable translating complex requirements, user insights, research findings, and technical constraints into practical design solutions and thrive in a collaborative, iterative environment.

This position is fully remote.

  • Apply established design principles, including visual hierarchy, typography, color, layout, navigation, and interaction patterns, to improve usability and consistency.

  • Design and refine interactive elements, including forms, navigation structures, search interfaces, dashboards, and content-driven experiences.
  • Support mobile-first and responsive design approaches while considering performance, low-bandwidth environments, and cross-device compatibility.

  • Contribute to a consistent and connected user experience across MC&FP digital products and services.

  • Partner with content strategists, information architects, copywriters, graphic designers, and other content & creative services team members to ensure interfaces integrate clear messaging, meaningful content, and consistent visual branding.

  • Working knowledge of human-centered design methodologies and the ability to apply UX research findings to interface design.
  • Familiarity with Section 508 accessibility requirements and WCAG principles.

 

Technical Knowledge 

Required: 

  • Familiarity with Section 508 and WCAG accessibility standards. 
  • Ability to evaluate designs, interfaces, and content for accessibility. 
  • Demonstrated proficiency with modern interface design and prototyping tools such as Figma, Adobe XD, Sketch, or comparable platforms.

Preferred: 

  • Experience working in Agile or iterative delivery environments. 
  • Experience supporting Federal Government, DoD, military community, or other large-scale public-sector digital initiatives

 

Certifications 

Preferred: 

  • Certifications in accessibility or inclusive design 

Skills 

  • Strong advocacy for inclusive and accessible design. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication abilities. 
  • Attention to detail and compliance accuracy. 
  • Ability to collaborate across design and development teams. 
  • Strong organizational and documentation skills.

Evio Overview

Evio is a highly unique pharmacy solutions company that was founded by and works closely with health plans to implement transformative (to cost, quality, access and experience) initiatives primarily focused on specialty and other high-cost medication solutions.

In 2020, a group of five amazing Blue Cross Blue Shield health plans that in total serve more than 20 million members recognized that the way medications get to patients needs significant reform—rapidly rising costs and massive system complexities are detrimental to patients and the entire industry. In 2025, Wellmark joined as Evio's first non-founding investor and sixth owner health plan. Each company made, and continues to make, significant investments to establish Evio as an independent entity to lead this transformation.  

Evio has advanced analytics and contracting capabilities at scale, and a suite of digital tools, to power our high-cost medication solutions. Our solutions act as a self-reinforcing “flywheel” where each element strengthens and feeds into the next, and support an “Only Evio can do that,” mindset and prioritization.

Evio is also a company that has invested heavily in and been highly intentional about people, team and culture. We believe we have created a very special place to work and encourage candidates to observe and ask us about our culture and decide for themselves.

Evio's Values

  • Empathy– The people our business serves always come first. We care for our teammates and put ourselves in the shoes of our health plan customers and the patients and clinicians our solutions benefit.
  • Diversity – We are committed to fostering a culture where everyone belongs and is valued for their background, experience and insights – one that encourages diversity of ideas, and is a nurturing, trusting, and accepting place for all.
  • Adventure – We are flexible, thrive in ambiguity, fail fast, and pivot quickly to get to a better answer. We celebrate wins and pivots with equal intensity.
  • Relentless – Guided by evidence and data, we are creative, curious, and unwavering in our pursuit of challenging the status quo and each other.
  • Transparency – Just as we seek to bring transparency to the pharmacy supply chain, authenticity and integrity are core to the way we communicate.
  • Excellence – We strive to raise the bar in all we do by hiring and developing exceptional talent and holding ourselves and our thinking to the highest standard.

Contract Development Manager

About the role

Evio and the six health plans we represent are uniquely positioned in the market and have demonstrated success in creating innovative partnerships with pharmaceutical manufacturers. As the regulatory environment for health plans, PBMs/GPOs, and manufacturers rapidly evolves over the next several years, Evio is expanding our direct manufacturer contracting capabilities and growing the team supporting this work.

The Contract Development Manager will contribute to the team by managing the pre-execution contract development process across pharmacy and medical benefit contracting. This role will translate negotiated business terms into clear, executable agreements, coordinate contracts through review and approval, support medication contracting RFPs, and help ensure contracts are handed off accurately for ongoing administration.

You’ll work closely with Negotiators, Legal, Strategy and Contract Operations throughout the contracting lifecycle. This is a hands-on role for someone who can manage detailed contract work, coordinate across teams, and help improve the tools and processes that support Evio’s medication contracting capabilities.

What you’ll do:

jobs.title: Account Executive - DACH
jobs.excerpt: Dixa is the agentic customer service platform behind more than 1,000 consumer brands.
jobs.description:
Dixa is the agentic customer service platform behind more than 1,000 consumer brands. We combine AI with a human touch, so brands can resolve customer questions instantly and still feel personal. Our AI agent, Mim, can resolve most routine enquiries on its own. Every email, chat, call and DM sits in one connected conversation, so no customer ever feels like a ticket number.

Customer service is changing faster than ever, and the deals you close will put Dixa at the heart of how leading brands make that change. Most closing roles follow the same pattern. You inherit meetings from an SDR floor you rarely speak to, work your deals alone, chase a solutions engineer when you need one, and hand the customer over at signature without ever hearing how it went. This role is built differently.

At Dixa we call this role a CX Consultant. You’ll be part of a Sales Pod, a small team that owns the DACH territory from start to finish. You’ll work every day alongside a CX Growth Associate on pipeline and a CX Architect on solution design. You’ll lead deals from qualified opportunities to close and take direct accountability for the revenue they bring in. You won’t just work the deals you’re given. You’ll help create them, shape them and see them through to a successful customer.

What you'll be doing

  • Owning the commercial relationship with prospects across DACH, running discovery, negotiations and executive conversations in German and English
  • Leading commercial deal execution from qualified opportunity to close, owning discovery, solution alignment, negotiation and commercial agreement
  • Running deep discovery to understand each prospect’s business challenges, decision-making structure and commercial priorities
  • Building and presenting compelling business cases that connect Dixa’s value to each prospect’s business outcomes
  • Handling complex negotiations independently, adapting your approach to each account’s stakeholders and deal structure
  • Generating pipeline alongside your CX Growth Associate, as an active part of the Pod’s outbound motion rather than an observer
  • Shaping account planning and territory prioritisation with your Pod, bringing a commercial view on where to focus and how to sequence the approach
  • Co-owning the Pod’s pipeline and forecast, keeping CRM data accurate and bringing a clear commercial read to pipeline reviews
  • Partnering with your CX Architect on solution scoping and customer handoff, and joining onboarding debriefs to improve future deals
  • Sharing what works (deal strategies, negotiation approaches, objection handling) with CX Consultants in other Pods

About you

  • You’re fluent in German and English, and confident negotiating and presenting to senior stakeholders in both
  • You’ve sold in the DACH market and understand how buying decisions, procurement and stakeholder dynamics work there
  • You have experience in a closing sales role in B2B SaaS or tech, with a track record of owning the full sales cycle and consistently hitting revenue targets
  • You’re confident leading complex, multi-stakeholder discovery and negotiations, including with VP and C-suite buyers
  • You’ve built and presented business cases with quantified ROI and economic impact to senior decision-makers
  • You sell through deep discovery and well-reasoned business cases, not feature-led pitches
  • You know structured sales methodologies. MEDDPICC and Command of Message experience is a plus, and we’ll support you through onboarding either way
  • You’re comfortable in a CRM (Salesforce ideally) and disciplined about pipeline hygiene and forecasting
  • Familiarity with customer service or contact centre solutions is a bonus
  • You’re competitive and resilient, with the drive to perform consistently across longer, more complex sales cycles
  • You’re calm and composed in high-stakes moments: tough negotiations, objections and senior conversations
  • You’re comfortable using AI to speed up the groundwork, like account research, call prep, follow-ups and CRM updates, so more of your time goes into high-value conversations with buyers
  • You’d rather win as a team than as an individual, and you’re happy to share pipeline ownership and roll up your sleeves on outbound
  • You’re always sharpening your craft, and you welcome debriefs and peer feedback

What makes this different

You’re part of a team, not a solo seller. There’s no wall between the people who book meetings and the people who close them. You sit in the Pod with your CX Consultant colleague, CX Growth Associate and CX Architect. You plan accounts together, decide which ones to go after together, and share the credit when deals close.

You own the deal, end to end. From discovery through negotiation to commercial agreement, you lead the process and you’re the prospect’s trusted adviser throughout. You’ll build business cases with quantified ROI and take them to director, VP and C-suite buyers.

Expertise joins the deal early, not late. Your CX Architect is someone you lean on as a sparring partner. You’ll bring them in early wherever technical depth adds commercial value, so solutions are shaped around the customer’s real problems from the start.

You’ll see what happens after signature. You’ll support the handoff into onboarding so the relationship and context carry through. You’ll also sit in on post-onboarding debriefs to hear what customers actually got compared with what they were promised, and use that to sharpen how you sell.

There’s a real community behind you. Our CX Consultant community of practice brings consultants from every Pod together to share deal strategies, negotiation learnings and what’s working in the market. You’ll learn from it and help shape it.

Salesforce and GTM stack

Contract to cash

AI and automation

Ownership

  • Be the single RevOps contact for Sales, CS, Marketing, Finance and Product. Turn each request into a task with an owner, date and success metric.

jobs.description:
About Accenture:


Accenture helps the world's leading enterprises reinvent by building their digital core and unleashing the power of AI to create value at speed for organizations across industries. Our strategy is to be the reinvention partner of choice for our clients and lead in the safe, widespread adoption of AI, and to be the most client-focused, AI-enabled, great place to work in the world. We bring together the talent of our approximately 814,000 people with proprietary assets and platforms, deep process and industry expertise, and leading ecosystem relationships to deliver end-to-end solutions and measurable outcomes at scale. Through our Reinvention Services, we offer broad expertise across Cybersecurity, Digital Core, Finance, Industry and Enterprise, Song, Supply Chain and Engineering, and Talent, with advanced capabilities in AI and Data, Industry and Process, and Technology. We serve approximately 9,000 clients and generated approximately $74 billion in FY26 revenue. Visit us at accenture.com.


We are:


A forward-thinking services company at the forefront of AI-native engineering. We partner with enterprise clients to design, build, and run production systems in which AI is a first-class engineering capability, engineered into the product and into the way our teams build it. Our engineers embed deeply with customers, own the code they ship, and move work past experimentation into operational reality.


You are:


An engineer who builds across the stack: front end, APIs, services, data, and the infrastructure it runs on. You take ownership of a feature through to production, including the parts that sit outside your strongest layer, and you have shipped software that real users depend on. You can explain the design decisions behind your work and what you would do differently.

AI is part of how you work. You use AI tools daily to generate, test, debug, and document code, and you have built at least one production feature in which a model performs meaningful work. You understand what it takes for a system to hold up under production load, security review, and real users.

You'll grow into an engineer who can own an entire system, developing depth in cloud, security, data, and agentic engineering alongside senior engineers who remain hands-on in the code with you.


The Work:


You'll work as part of a client-embedded engineering team, taking real features from design through production. You will be handed problems to solve, and you will be expected to ask precise questions, make progress under ambiguity, and put working software in front of stakeholders quickly.


Build Across the Stack

  • Build and ship production features across front end, APIs, backend services, integration, and data, taking a feature end to end across every layer it touches.
  • Read and debug unfamiliar code, trace a problem across application, data, and infrastructure boundaries, and fix the underlying cause.
  • Build and Run on Cloud-Native Platforms
  • Develop, containerize, and deploy services on a major cloud platform using Docker, Kubernetes or serverless, and managed cloud services.
  • Apply infrastructure as code (Terraform, Helm, or equivalent), and take part in keeping your services healthy, observable, and recoverable in production.
  • Work Inside the Delivery Pipeline
  • Work within automated CI/CD pipelines, writing the automated tests, resolving pipeline failures, and taking your own changes through to production.
  • Apply secure engineering practices as you code, including identity and access fundamentals, secrets handling, dependency hygiene, and input validation.

Work With Data and Context:


  • Design and implement the data access your features need across relational and non-relational stores, APIs, object storage, and event platforms.
  • Build the retrieval and context layers AI features depend on, including knowledge sources, embeddings, metadata, and context management, applying data quality, access, and privacy controls as you go.

Build AI Features and Agent Workflows:


  • Integrate commercial and open models through APIs and enterprise AI platforms, using tool calling, structured outputs, retrieval, and context engineering to make them useful inside live business workflows.
  • Build agent workflows with tools, memory, and human checkpoints, and write the evaluations that measure their behavior against accuracy, latency, safety, and cost.

Engineer With AI Every Day:


  • Use AI-native development techniques throughout your own workflow, including code generation, test generation, debugging, refactoring, documentation, and code comprehension, and measure the effect on your throughput and quality.
  • Give agents the context, tools, and boundaries they need to safely handle bounded engineering tasks, and review their output to the same standard you would apply to a colleague's code.

Grow and Contribute:


  • Participate in design reviews, code reviews, and production troubleshooting, applying feedback quickly and raising the quality of the work around you.
  • Document what you learn and contribute patterns, reusable components, and tooling back to the team and to our internal AI-native engineering community.

Travel may be required for this role. The amount of travel will vary from 25% to 75% depending on business need and client requirements.


Here's What You Need:


  • Minimum of 3 years of professional software engineering experience building production software.
  • Minimum of 2 years of hands-on experience working across more than one layer of the stack, for example front end and API, or services and data.
  • Minimum of 3 years of programming experience in at least one major language such as Java, Python, Go, TypeScript/JavaScript, or C#.
  • Minimum of 3 year of hands-on experience with a major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP), including building and deploying containerized services.
  • Minimum of 3 year of experience working within an automated CI/CD pipeline, including writing automated tests.
  • Minimum of 1 year of hands-on experience building and shipping AI-enabled features or agent workflows, including model integration through APIs, tool calling, structured outputs, retrieval, and context engineering.
  • Minimum of 1 year of experience applying AI coding tools to day-to-day software development, including code generation, test generation, debugging, and documentation
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent (minimum 12 years) work experience. (If Associate’s Degree, must have minimum 6 years work experience)

Bonus Points If You Have:


  • A public repository, portfolio, or open-source contribution featuring agents, tools, or plugins you built yourself.
  • Experience with an agent framework such as LangGraph, Crew AI, the Claude Agent SDK, or the OpenAI SDK.
  • Experience writing evaluations or test harnesses that measure AI behavior.
  • Hands-on experience with infrastructure as code and observability tooling.
  • Relevant cloud or AI certifications.
  • Experience in a client-facing or product-facing role presenting your own technical work to stakeholders.
  • Experience in a startup, product company, or hyperscaler environment where you owned a feature from idea through production.

jobs.description:
Software Engagement and Ecosystem

ROLE TYPE

Senior technical individual contributor

PRIMARY MANDATE

Own customer-value playbooks

SCOPE

Global / cross-functional

Position Overview

NI is creating a more repeatable approach for helping customers realize value from its software portfolio. Central to this approach is a set of customer-value playbooks that translate recurring customer challenges into structured, technically credible engagement methods.

The Senior Technical Engagement Lead owns the creation, validation, curation, and continuous improvement of these playbooks.

This is a senior, highly technical, customer-facing role. The person combines deep software and systems expertise with customer discovery, technical strategy, content development, and cross-functional leadership. The role works directly with selected customers to understand engineering workflows, validate proposed approaches, and convert successful engagements into reusable assets that other teams can apply across additional accounts.

The role does not own account strategy and does not replace Customer Success, Product Management, technical support, field engineering, Education Services, Sales, or partners. The role creates the technical system those organizations use to execute credible, outcome-oriented software engagements at scale.

Key Responsibilities

Own Customer-Value Playbooks

  • Create and maintain a prioritized portfolio of reusable customer-value playbooks addressing recurring engineering and business challenges.
  • Define the customer outcome hypothesis, applicability signals, discovery questions, current-state assessment, desired future state, and measurable success criteria for each playbook.
  • Document the technical transformation path that connects NI software capabilities to customer outcomes.
  • Define the demonstrations, reference architectures, examples, technical guidance, workshops, and supporting assets required to execute each playbook.
  • Identify the expertise and delivery resources required at each stage, including Customer Success, Software Growth Managers, Product Management, TSC/TSE, FAE, Education Services, specialists, partners, consultants, and systems integrators.
  • Establish clear entry, success, expansion, and stop criteria so the playbooks guide decisions rather than become generic sales content.

Validate Technical Understanding Through Direct Customer Engagement

  • Participate selectively in strategic customer engagements where deep technical expertise is required.
  • Lead or support technical discovery workshops with engineers, technical leaders, and account stakeholders.
  • Examine customer development practices, deployed systems, data flows, operational constraints, adoption barriers, and software architecture.
  • Test whether playbook assumptions, activities, and success measures are credible in actual customer environments.
  • Support technically complex demonstrations, assessments, architecture discussions, pilots, and validation activities.
  • Convert successful customer work into reusable methods without exposing confidential customer information.

Enable Cross-Functional Execution

  • Prepare Customer Success teams to recognize when a playbook is relevant and connect it to account priorities.
  • Help Customer Success adapt the reusable playbook to the customer’s stakeholders, workflows, maturity, and desired outcomes.
  • Enable Software Growth Managers to apply established playbooks in white-space accounts and high-growth software opportunities.
  • Provide technical guidance to TSC/TSE, FAE, Education Services, specialists, and partners executing specific playbook activities.
  • Develop facilitator guides, workshop materials, technical examples, training, and field-ready engagement assets.
  • Help account teams determine which resources are required rather than assuming every organization participates in every engagement.
  • Support strategic coordination of engagement narratives, agendas, experts, and technical contributors when multiple organizations are involved.

Connect Technical Work to Customer Value

  • Ensure each playbook begins with a customer outcome rather than a product pitch.
  • Translate technical improvements into measurable effects such as engineering capacity, development speed, product quality, operational efficiency, risk reduction, asset utilization, or avoided cost.
  • Establish baselines and evidence requirements before recommending pilots or implementation work.
  • Define how technical results should be documented and reviewed with customer stakeholders.
  • Help teams distinguish product usage from demonstrated customer value.
  • Build the technical and value evidence needed to support account expansion and renewal readiness.

Support Adoption and Account Expansion

  • Design playbooks so a successful foothold can expand across additional teams, programs, sites, and workflows.
  • Identify repeatable approaches for stakeholder mapping, champion development, pilot selection, validation, customer showcases, and cross-program visibility.
  • Help account teams use validated evidence to build credibility beyond the original customer team.
  • Define the technical conditions required to scale from a pilot into a sustained operating practice.
  • Package successful implementations into customer references, reusable examples, standards, and expansion methods.
  • Ensure recurring adoption and value reviews are built into the engagement model.

Maintain the Feedback Loop

  • Capture recurring customer needs, technical barriers, adoption gaps, and evidence of successful approaches.
  • Separate isolated requests from patterns that warrant broader investment.
  • Translate field learning into actionable input for Product Management, R&D, Product Marketing, Customer Success, and technical delivery organizations.
  • Recommend improvements to product capabilities, technical content, demonstrations, training, partner offerings, and future playbook versions.
  • Maintain clear version ownership and governance for the playbook portfolio.
  • Retire or revise playbooks that do not produce credible customer outcomes.

Cross-Functional Relationships

Customer Success

Owns account-specific strategy and execution oversight. The Senior Technical Engagement Lead owns reusable playbook content and technical methodology. The roles jointly contextualize the playbook for selected accounts, but this position does not assume responsibility for the account plan or Customer Success process.

Software Growth Managers

Provides playbook guidance and technical enablement for white-space and high-growth opportunities, while respecting the evolving scope of the Software Growth Manager role.

Product Management and R&D

Obtains roadmap direction and product expertise; returns recurring customer evidence, validated needs, and product gaps.

Product Marketing

Connects validated technical and customer evidence to positioning and broader-market narratives without reducing the playbook to marketing content.

TSC/TSE, FAE, Education Services, and Specialists

Defines where demonstrations, startup assistance, troubleshooting, consultation, proof-of-concept work, customized enablement, or specialist services are required. Preserves the distinction between FAE-led pre-sale proof of concept and TSC/TSE demonstrations, startup, consultation, troubleshooting, and post-sale activity.

Partners, Consultants, and Systems Integrators

Identifies activities external experts can deliver or operationalize at scale and defines the enablement and qualification required.

Sales and Renewal Teams

Provides technical and value evidence for commercial conversations. Sales and Renewals retain ownership of commercial strategy, pricing, negotiation, and contract execution.

Required Qualifications

  • Deep expertise in LabVIEW, SystemLink, TestStand, DIAdem, VeriStand, or related NI software platforms.
  • Experience with software development lifecycle practices, continuous integration and delivery, source-code management, automated validation, containerization, test-data management, or AI-assisted engineering workflows.
  • Significant technical experience with software used in engineering, test, measurement, automation, or adjacent technical domains.
  • Demonstrated ability to understand complex software architectures, development workflows, deployed systems, data pipelines, or engineering operations.
  • Experience engaging directly with highly technical customers and leading discovery without defaulting immediately to product recommendations.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate technical concepts into structured methods, guidance, demonstrations, and reusable assets.
  • Ability to connect technical activities to measurable customer outcomes.
  • Strong written, presentation, workshop facilitation, and technical storytelling skills.
  • Ability to influence teams and coordinate work without formal reporting authority.
  • Ability to identify patterns across customer engagements while distinguishing reusable insight from account-specific detail.
  • Willingness to travel for selected customer, partner, and industry engagements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working across Product Management, engineering, sales, customer-facing, support, and partner organizations.
  • Experience architecting or supporting large, distributed test and measurement systems.
  • Experience developing customer-facing technical programs, reference architectures, workshops, enablement materials, or adoption frameworks.
  • Experience with enterprise environments involving multiple business units, sites, programs, or engineering disciplines.
  • Experience translating customer feedback into product or roadmap recommendations.
  • Experience enabling partners, consultants, systems integrators, or other external technical resources.

Measures of Success

Success is evaluated based on the quality, usability, adoption, and demonstrated impact of the playbooks, not simply the quantity of content produced.

  • A prioritized portfolio of clearly defined customer-value playbooks.
  • Playbooks used in active account or white-space motions.
  • Account teams able to select and apply playbooks with less dependency on ad hoc expert intervention.
  • Customer engagements that establish explicit baselines, success measures, and evidence.
  • Validated examples converted into reusable technical assets.
  • Expansion of successful approaches into additional customer teams, workflows, programs, or sites.
  • Improved field readiness across Customer Success, Software Growth, technical teams, and partners.
  • Recurring customer insights translated into specific product, content, training, or roadmap recommendations.
  • Earlier visibility into adoption, value, stakeholders, and commercial implications before renewal.
  • Clear evidence that ineffective playbooks are refined or retired.

Role Boundaries

  • Owns creation, technical integrity, curation, validation, governance, and lifecycle management of customer-value playbooks.
  • Contributes to selected customer discovery, technical validation, strategic engagements, enablement, and product feedback.
  • Does not own individual account strategy, account execution oversight, Customer Success processes, commercial negotiations, routine technical support, or every customer implementation.
  • Does not replace Customer Success, Software Growth Managers, Product Management, Product Marketing, TSC/TSE, FAE, Education Services, Sales, Renewals, partners, consultants, or systems integrators

Our Culture & Commitment to You

At Emerson, we prioritize a workplace where every employee is valued, respected, and empowered to grow. We foster an environment that encourages innovation, collaboration, and diverse perspectives—because we know that great ideas come from great teams. Our commitment to ongoing career development and growing an inclusive culture ensures you have the support to thrive. Whether through mentorship, training, or leadership opportunities, we invest in your success so you can make a lasting impact. We believe diverse teams, working together are key to driving growth and delivering business results.

We recognize the importance of employee wellbeing. We prioritize providing flexible, competitive benefits plans to meet you and your family’s physical, mental, financial, and social needs. We provide a variety of medical insurance plans, with dental and vision coverage, Employee Assistance Program, 401(k), tuition reimbursement, employee resource groups, recognition, and much more. Our culture offers flexible time off plans, including paid parental leave (maternal and paternal), vacation and holiday leave.

At Emerson, our employee’s passion for innovation and results drives our success. We actively pursue new technologies, capabilities and approaches to drive tangible value for our customers. To reward this passion for innovation and results, Emerson

makes meaningful investments in our people. We provide competitive compensation, integrated benefits offerings and fulfilling career journeys

that support the growth of each employee. We firmly believe that when Emerson is successful in achieving its operational and financial goals, our

employees share in the company’s success. The salary/pay range for this role is 101,000 - 188,100 commensurate with the skills, talent,

capabilities, and experience each candidate brings to the role.

jobs.description:
Statut :Régulier, temps plein

Satus : Regular, full-time


(Version française à la suite)


Institutional Key Account Manager (IKAM) – Pfizer Canada Global Hospital & Biosimilar (GH&B)

Own Global Hospital & Biosimilar territory strategy to drive access and deliver portfolio growth through strategic stakeholder engagement.

Role Purpose:

Responsible for driving the sales growth and access within hospital and institutional accounts by influencing treatment decisions, formularies and protocols. The incumbent is accountable for achieving or surpassing sales results aligned with the marketing strategies within their defined territory and respective region. This will be done by delivering value to providers through effective account management ensuring optimal patient care and management, as well as maximizing sales opportunities.

Core Responsibilities:

  • Develop and execute account business plans that address the business priorities of assigned territory within Pfizer GH&B.
  • Establish and maintain long-term business relationships with key stakeholders, including chief pharmacists, healthcare professionals, physician group practices, decision-makers within health authorities, institutions, and purchasing groups
  • Has comprehensive knowledge of customer’s objectives, strategies, & priorities, and applies knowledge to the business strategy and account planning to leverage key stakeholders leading to positive outcomes​
  • Develops significant credibility and trust, and creates a compelling business case that leads to an agreed upon opportunity that results in an executed plan of action​
  • Coordinate and execute educational programs, attend conventions, and leverage Pfizer resources to benefit key customer segments.
  • To build advocacy in speakers and local key opinion leaders.
  • Manage designated accounts to achieve business objectives, identify key customers, and develop effective relationships to promote Pfizer GH&B products and services.
  • Collaborate with cross functional team members at the field and regional level (Senior Strategic Healthcare Partners (SSHP), Pharmacy Key Account Managers (PKAM) where applicable, Medical, Access, PSP, Marketing and others) to build and execute an integrated business plan that supports the strategy and objectives of the Global Hospital & Biosimilar business
  • To contribute to the positioning of promoted products on hospital formulary listings and treatment protocols.
  • Provide expertise on healthcare reform, healthcare systems, and health funding ecosystems to facilitate sound business decisions.
  • Analyze account activities, create account plans, and deliver activities that optimize sales opportunities and resource allocation.
  • Seek opportunities for synergy and partnership to achieve both Pfizer GH&B and customer goals.
  • Consistently demonstrate first class account selling and management. Monitor progress within key accounts and implement action plans as appropriate.
  • Operate with a Digital First multichannel mindset, demonstrating high capability and deployment of digital technology and channels, to further enhance customer experience, maximise colleague efficiency and ensure optimal patient access to our medicines
  • Identifies and reports adverse events and product complaints as per Corporate procedure, including Your Reporting Responsibilities (YRR) training.

The ideal candidate must demonstrate high proficiency in the following competencies:

  • Territory and Hospital Navigation - This is the ability of the IKAM to effectively manage a portfolio of specialized pharmaceutical products and conduct proper account planning according to commercial needs; quickly become familiar with the various clinical pathways established by hospitals to treat patients using our medications; consistently develop an accessible, broad, and deep network of contacts; identify key decision-makers, enablers, and potential advocates for our promoted products; and quickly become familiar with each hospital’s unique ecosystem.
  • Commercial Agility - This is the ability of the IKAM to possess a good understanding of specialized pharmaceutical product manufacturing, the Canadian supply chain, and the various forces leading to product shortages; grasp the B2B business environment, understand the main financial drivers in hospitals and KPIs related to customer roles, and convert clinical features into commercial benefits; understand the rationale behind our pricing structure and convey confidence when communicating our hospital prices, when necessary; and negotiate agreements based on overall value while understanding the fundamentals of contractual language.

• Value Creation - This is the ability of the IKAM to demonstrate a consultative mindset with customers; To deliver overall value to key accounts while developing productive partnerships; To conduct presentations in front of customers that are compliant to our code of conduct and impactful; To manage ongoing field projects with focus and within the set timeframes; To quickly become familiar with the overall operational dynamic of the provincial healthcare system.

• Clinical Agility - This is the ability of the IKAM to possess the basic knowledge of the therapeutic fields of our promoted products along with their respective clinical profiles, including indications and dosage regimens; To seek and entertain regular interactions with customers that are value-based; To quickly become familiar with the competitive environment.

The ideal candidate possesses the following qualifications:

· University degree in business administration or science with a minimum of five years of pharmaceutical sales experience.

· Demonstrated record of success in customer-facing positions, preferably in a specialty environment.

· High level of business acumen, strategic business planning abilities, and proficiency in using computer software.

· Excellent communication, presentation, negotiation, and interpersonal skills.

· Established network of key stakeholders influencing territory business.

· Experience in product management, sales training, or sales administration is an asset

· Ability to travel frequently and maintain a valid driving license.

· Bilingualism (French and English): An advanced level of English, both spoken and written, is required to enable the individual to collaborate effectively with colleagues and partners located elsewhere in Canada and internationally daily as part of their responsibilities.


The annual base salary for this position ranges from $107,925 to $179,875.

The salary range provided applies to Canada only and does not apply to any other locations outside of Canada.


Gestionnaire – Clients institutionnels (GCI) – Secteur hospitalier et produits biosimilaires – Marché mondial (SHPBMM), Pfizer Canada

Responsable de la stratégie relative au Secteur hospitalier et produits biosimilaires – Marché mondial (SHPBMMM) pour les territoires visant à favoriser l’accès et à assurer la croissance de la gamme de produits grâce à un engagement stratégique auprès des parties prenantes.

Objectif du poste :

Assurer la croissance des ventes et favoriser l’accès auprès des hôpitaux et des clients institutionnels en influençant les décisions thérapeutiques, les listes de médicaments et les protocoles. La personne titulaire sera chargée d’atteindre ou de dépasser les objectifs de vente, arrimés aux stratégies de marketing des territoires ou régions. Elle atteindra ces objectifs en apportant de la valeur ajoutée aux fournisseurs au moyen de la gestion efficace des comptes, afin d’offrir aux patient·e·s une prise en charge et des soins optimaux, tout en maximisant les possibilités de vente.

Fonctions principales :

· Concevoir et appliquer des plans d’affaires pour les comptes qui répondent aux priorités commerciales du territoire qui lui a été attribué au sein du SHPBMM de Pfizer

· Établir et entretenir des relations d’affaires à long terme avec les principales parties prenantes, notamment les pharmacien·ne·s, les professionnel·le·s de la santé, les cabinets médicaux, les responsables des décisions des autorités sanitaires, les établissements et les groupes d’achat

· Posséder une connaissance approfondie des objectifs, des stratégies et des priorités de la clientèle et appliquer ses connaissances à la stratégie commerciale et à la planification des comptes pour mettre à profit les principales parties prenantes et obtenir des résultats positifs

· Gagner une crédibilité et une confiance importantes, et élaborer une analyse de rentabilité convaincante qui débouche sur une occasion convenue, puis sur l’exécution d’un plan d’action

· Coordonner et mettre en œuvre des programmes de formation, participer à des congrès et exploiter les ressources de Pfizer au profit de segments de clientèle clés

  • Contribuer au perfectionnement des aptitudes de défense des intérêts des conférenciers et conférencières ainsi que des leaders d’opinion clés locaux

· Gérer les comptes désignés pour atteindre les objectifs commerciaux, repérer les client·e·s clés et développer des relations efficaces pour promouvoir les produits et services du SHPBMM de Pfizer

· Collaborer avec les membres des équipes interfonctionnelles sur le terrain et à l’échelle régionale (premier·ère partenaire stratégique – Soins de santé [PPSSS], gestionnaire - Comptes pharmacies le cas échéant, Affaires médicales, Accès, PSP, Marketing et autres) afin d’élaborer et de mettre en œuvre un plan d’affaires intégré qui soutienne la stratégie et les objectifs du SHPBMM

  • Contribuer à faire inscrire les produits promus sur les listes de médicaments des hôpitaux et les protocoles de soins

· Fournir une expertise sur la réforme des soins de santé, les systèmes de santé et les écosystèmes de financement de la santé afin de faciliter la prise de décisions commerciales éclairées

· Analyser les activités des comptes, créer des plans de compte et réaliser des activités optimisant les possibilités de vente et l’affectation des ressources

· Chercher les possibilités de synergie et de partenariat afin de contribuer à l’atteinte des objectifs du SHPBMM de Pfizer et de la clientèle.

· Faire preuve en tout temps d’excellence en matière de gestion et de vente des comptes. Surveiller les progrès accomplis auprès des comptes principaux et mettre en œuvre les plans d’action en conséquence.

· Mettre à profit différents canaux et privilégier le numérique, en démontrant une forte capacité et un déploiement efficace des technologies et des canaux numériques, afin d’améliorer l’expérience client, d’optimiser l’efficacité du personnel et de garantir un accès optimal des patient·e·s à nos médicaments

· Veiller à la reconnaissance et à la déclaration des manifestations indésirables et des plaintes relatives aux produits, conformément aux normes de l’entreprise, dont la formation intitulée Responsabilités en matière de pharmacovigilance


Le ou la candidate idéal·e doit parfaitement maîtriser les compétences suivantes :

  • Navigation dans le territoire et le secteur hospitalier : Savoir gérer efficacement une gamme de produits pharmaceutiques spécialisés et assurer une planification adéquate des comptes conformément aux besoins commerciaux. Se familiariser rapidement avec les différents parcours cliniques mis en place par les hôpitaux pour traiter les patient·e·s à l’aide de nos médicaments. S’employer constamment à développer un réseau de contacts bien étendu, vaste et accessible. Repérer des décideurs·euses/catalyseurs clés ainsi que des défenseurs·euses potentiels pour nos produits en promotion. Se familiariser rapidement avec l’écosystème particulier de chaque hôpital.
  • Agilité commerciale : Posséder une bonne compréhension de la fabrication de produits pharmaceutiques spécialisés, de la chaîne d’approvisionnement canadienne et des divers facteurs à l’origine des pénuries de produits. Saisir l’environnement commercial interentreprises, comprendre les principaux facteurs et les indicateurs de rendement clés des hôpitaux liés aux rôles de la clientèle et transformer les caractéristiques en avantages commerciaux. Comprendre la logique qui sous-tend notre structure de prix et inspirer confiance lors de la communication de nos prix aux hôpitaux, au besoin. Négocier des ententes fondées sur la valeur globale tout en maîtrisant les principes fondamentaux du langage contractuel.

• Création de valeur : Faire preuve d’un état d’esprit axé sur le soutien consultatif à la clientèle. Apporter une valeur globale aux comptes clés tout en développant des partenariats productifs. Assurer des présentations percutantes auprès de la clientèle tout en se conformant à notre code de conduite. Gérer les projets sur le terrain en cours avec attention et dans les délais impartis. Se familiariser rapidement avec la dynamique opérationnelle globale des systèmes de santé provinciaux.

• Agilité clinique : Pouvoir acquérir rapidement les connaissances de base du champ thérapeutique des produits en promotion qui lui ont été assignés, dont leurs profils cliniques respectifs, leurs indications, la posologie, etc. Rechercher et entretenir des interactions régulières fondées sur la valeur avec la clientèle. Se familiariser rapidement avec la concurrence.

La candidature idéale satisfera aux exigences suivantes :

· Diplôme universitaire en administration ou en sciences, et cinq ans d’expérience au minimum dans la vente de produits pharmaceutiques

· Succès éprouvé à un poste équivalent où le ou la titulaire doit interagir avec la clientèle, préférablement dans un domaine spécialisé

· Sens aigu des affaires, aptitudes à la planification stratégique et maîtrise des logiciels.

· Excellentes aptitudes pour la communication, la présentation d’exposés, la négociation et les relations interpersonnelles.

· Réseau établi de parties prenantes clés exerçant une influence sur les activités commerciales du territoire.

· Expérience en gestion de produits, en formation à la vente ou en gestion des ventes, un atout

· Capacité à voyager fréquemment et à détenir un permis de conduire valide

· Bilinguisme (français et anglais) – Un niveau avancé d’anglais, tant à l’oral qu’à l’écrit, est requis afin de permettre à la personne de collaborer efficacement avec des collègues et partenaires situés ailleurs au Canada et à l’international de façon quotidienne dans le cadre de ses responsabilités.


Le salaire annuel de base pour ce poste varie de 107,925 $ à 179,875$.

L’échelle salariale fournie s’applique seulement au Canada, et ne s’applique à aucun autre endroit à l’extérieur du Canada.

CS e-Storage is looking for a Project Quality Manager to plan, lead, execute, and monitor all project quality work. This individual serves as the main point of contact for project quality management and acts as a quality ambassador for coordination with various stakeholders, including owner representatives, EPC contractors, equipment suppliers, O&M service providers, and CS e-storage team members. Description

OpenDor Media is searching for a Director of Events to own a growing calendar of live shows and donor events, from the first request to the final debrief, and turn each one into an experience worth showing up for. You will be the front door for every event request, work with our Chief Marketing Officer to set priorities and assign ownership, and run the room on site when it counts. Your work shapes how people experience OpenDor Media in person, and the events you deliver show people who we are and why our work matters.

OpenDor Media is a leading global non-profit media company for the 21st century. We educate, entertain, and engage our audiences by bringing to life big ideas and authentic stories, and by celebrating all things Jewish.

This role is an exempt, fully remote position that includes travel to events 1-2 times per month.

What you'll own

  • Flagship live shows: Be the person who makes each show happen: set the budget, secure approvals, book the venue and production team, and lead on site, working with Content and Development on the stage conversation, VIP reception and guest list.
  • Donor events: Plan and deliver parlor events and donor gatherings in Los Angeles, New York, Miami and other cities, giving our Development team the right setting to deepen relationships with supporters.
  • The events pipeline: Be the front door for every event request, recommending priorities to the Chief Marketing Officer so each event gets the right owner, investment and lead time, and keep one OpenDor Media events calendar.
  • Support across the organization: Serve as Marketing's events liaison, bringing logistics and a consistent standard to speaking engagements, live episodes, tours and conferences led by division heads.
  • Budgets and suppliers: Run the events budget, negotiate supplier contracts, and build the templates, checklists and trusted network of venues, caterers and AV partners that make each event easier than the last.
  • Results and learning: Measure every event against its targets, from the right audience in the room to money raised within 90 days, and carry the lessons into the next plan.

What we're looking for

  • Strategic about where we show up: You think about audience, cost and payoff before logistics, and you help leadership put resources behind the events that matter most.
  • A clear decision maker: You can look at a request and quickly shape the right plan for it, including the format, scale, owner and resources, and explain your thinking in a way people get behind.
  • An owner from start to finish: You take an event from the first brief to the final debrief, handling the venue, suppliers, run of show and day-of details yourself so nothing falls through the cracks.
  • Calm in the room: When the AV fails or a speaker runs late, you are the steady voice running the show, and the guests never notice.
  • Able to balance multiple priorities: You build the timeline, track every moving piece across teams and suppliers, and hold stakeholders to their dates without spending the goodwill that gets the next event done.

Requirements

  • You have 6+ years in live events, experiential marketing, agency production, nonprofit galas or live entertainment.
  • You have run donor, VIP or high-net-worth events for 150 to 1,000 guests, end to end.
  • You manage budgets and suppliers with confidence, including negotiating contracts.
  • You keep complex, multi-stakeholder projects on schedule.
  • You are based in the US, can travel one to two times a month, can work evenings and some weekends around events, and keep regular overlap with UK and Israel hours.
  • You know AI and embrace it. You use AI tools to make your own work faster and cleaner, you have hands-on experience with Claude specifically.
  • You write and speak fluent English and work comfortably in Google Workspace and Slack.
  • You are committed to OpenDor Media's mission and values.

﻿These are not required, but they help:

  • Experience in a Jewish nonprofit or community organization or familiarity with Jewish and Israeli audiences
  • Live podcast, broadcast or stage production experience
  • Established venue and supplier networks in Miami, New York or Los Angeles
  • Working knowledge of kashrut, Shabbat and Jewish holidays in event planning
  • Experience with Wrike

Who We Are:

OpenDor Media provides inspiring and informative content on all issues relating to Judaism and Israel, and those that affect young Jews today. We are proudly and transparently positive about Israel and Zionism, Jewish values and ideals. We celebrate the riches of Jewish and Israeli history and culture. We do so in a voice which is authentic, credible and therefore trusted. We embrace complexity and recognize and give voice to multiple perspectives on difficult issues. We push the boundaries of innovation, creativity and good old hard work. From our leadership team to new and veteran team members, we all strive to embody our core values:

  • Fueled by creativity: We think and act creatively in everything we do, with the agility and flexibility to apply creativity whatever role we play.
  • Inspired by excellence: We are driven to excel at whatever we do. Our teams are always ready to go the extra mile to get the very best results.
  • Powered by positivity: We bring positivity to work every day, for a fun, creative and inviting work environment that brings out the best in everyone.
  • Driven by self-improvement: Like our content, no issue is taboo, and we are open to constructive ways to improve and develop into the best professionals we can be.
  • Empowered by collaboration: We thrive on sharing knowledge, teamwork, being a “mensch,” and leveraging everyone's talents to achieve a sum greater than the parts.

Benefits

  • Fully remote with flexibility to work from anywhere
  • Competitive salary
  • Paid days off for Jewish and national holidays with vacation and sick time available from your first day
  • Comprehensive Healthcare coverage
  • 401(k) retirement plan with an employer match
  • High level of autonomy and direct access to leadership
  • A warm, collaborative culture and great colleagues

Salary

The salary for this position is $100,000 to $125,000 annually for a U.S.-based candidate. The final salary will be determined based on careful consideration of several factors, including the candidate's location, experience in similar roles, and expertise related to the qualifications above.

Improvado is a marketing data platform for enterprise brands and agencies. You will own how our revenue runs and how it is measured. That covers Salesforce and the GTM tools, the path from signed contract to paid invoice, the revenue data model, and the reports leadership decides from. You work closely with the analytics team: you don’t have to build the data models yourself, but you must read them, spot what is wrong and say what to change. You work through AI agents daily, doing the work of a bigger team.

Salesforce and GTM stack

Contract to cash

Revenue analytics and data model

AI and automation

  • Use coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) for queries, scripts and Salesforce automation, and always verify their output.

Ownership

jobs.excerpt: Company OverviewOrbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Orbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies. We convert complex information and operational systems into decisive outcomes, giving public institutions and critical enterprises the tools to move faster, see clearer, and act first in an increasingly contested world.

We are not a consulting firm and not a systems integrator. Every Orbis team is built around practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, and every engagement is judged on one thing: whether it produces working capability, not slide decks. Solutions forged from experience; that is how we build, and it is how we hire.

Job Summary

This role drives international growth by advancing the Obsidian Autonomy joint venture, supporting European business development and leading strategic pursuits across regions. It partners with the EVP, International, to execute portfolio priorities, develop new opportunities and partnerships, strengthen cross-functional collaboration, and implement scalable processes that improve business development and operational effectiveness. The role also builds a comprehensive understanding of Orbis’ business model, commercial practices, and delivery capabilities to accelerate growth and execution across the company.

Key Responsibilities

Primary Focus & Flexible Support

Your initial focus will be (1) the growth of the Obsidian Autonomy joint venture and (2) direct support to the Orbis BD Lead, Europe, on pursuits, proposals, partner engagement, and pipeline development. (3) also serve as a flexible senior resource for the EVP, International. As new opportunities emerge in any region, the EVP may direct you to stand up, support, or lead a pursuit. The EVP, International will work with you to balance your workload and support your ability to shift between priorities as the portfolio demands.

  • DRIVE: Bring momentum to the international portfolio. Work for the EVP, International across the whole of the portfolio, carry his priorities into the regions, and lead initiatives where the opportunity calls for it. Move opportunities forward across different regions, close gaps between the regions and headquarters, and extend that energy to the broader company, including the Defense vertical, where it helps.
  • GROW: Support the growth of the Obsidian Autonomy joint venture and take ownership of new pursuits, programs, and partnerships as they emerge, standing them up and running them through to a permanent owner where appropriate.
  • LEARN: Develop a working command of the Orbis business end to end, from how we price and contract to how we deliver and support, across products, services, financials, and contracting practices.
  • BUILD: Identify where process, standards, and shared playbooks would improve speed, quality, and consistency across International and the wider company, and lead the effort to put them in place.
  • CONNECT: Partner with Finance, Legal, People, Operations & Delivery (OPD), and Product Development & Engineering (PDE) to make cross-functional execution smoother, and support firm-wide strategy implementation and business development.

Specific Duties

DRIVE: Drive Momentum Across Regions

  • Work with the EVP, International across different regions, aligned on priorities in support of country managers and regional leads; provide initial support to the BD Lead, Europe; engage with partners and customers on pursuits, proposals, negotiations, and engagement.
  • Lead initiatives independently. Carry opportunities that lack a natural owner or that span regions, own them end to end, make the calls needed to keep them moving, and maintain flexibility to support areas that may need additional senior capacity.
  • Represent Orbis with international government and industry counterparts, including in-country.
  • Support Defense and other company priorities where international experience, relationships, or capacity add value.
  • Produce an aggregate international update when appropriate that highlights pipeline movement, program accomplishments, client feedback, and opportunities for growth or expansion.

GROW

  • Support the growth of Obsidian Autonomy, the Orbis UAE joint venture, including pipeline development, proposals, pricing, and partner engagement.
  • Help manage the Orbis side of the JV relationship, including commercial and IP matters, in coordination with Legal and the executive team.
  • Align Obsidian's offerings with the Orbis product roadmap and delivery capacity.
  • Take on new pursuits, programs, and partnerships as they arise and lead select captures end to end, including teaming, solution shaping, pricing strategy, and negotiation.
  • Contribute to program proposals and concept pitches. Participate in the pricing and review process before proposals are sent to clients to ensure consistency with firm quality standards and alignment with strategy.
  • Build relationships with clients and potential clients where appropriate. Seek to limit single points of connectivity for the firm and invest in sustained and upcoming relationships.

LEARN

  • Within the first 120 days, learn the business development cycle through engagement with Orbis International colleagues to understand best BD practices; hone skills and build confidence to sell Orbis products and services to international clients.
  • Develop fluency in Orbis products and services, the delivery model, program financials, and contracting and export practices.
  • Spend time with country managers, program leads, and functional teams to understand how work actually gets done and where it slows down.
  • Provide feedback to OPD and PDE to make our Product and Service offerings better, more capable of solving customer problems, and more marketable.

BUILD

  • Identify where process, standards, and shared playbooks would improve speed, quality, or consistency across International and the wider company, and lead the effort to put them in place.
  • Establish repeatable approaches for how international pursuits are run, from qualification through capture, pricing, and handoff to delivery.
  • Raise the bar of execution by setting and modeling standards for proposals, customer engagement, and internal reporting.
  • Within the first year, deliver recognizable improvements in how international pursuits are run, with repeatable processes adopted across regions.

CONNECT

  • Partner with Finance, Legal, People, Delivery, and Product to make cross-functional execution smoother and to strengthen the connection between International and the rest of the company.
  • Understand trends and changes with the potential to disrupt the firm's key international opportunities and proactively share insights and recommendations with the EVP, International and the executive team.
  • Support internal concept and capability development with your experience, client insights, and abilities.
  • Support the establishment of a one-firm culture linking the international regions and the JV with the firm as a whole.

Required Qualifications

  • Senior experience in national security, defense technology, or international government business, with a record of building and closing complex deals, sustained in-country engagement with government and industry partners, and leading teams through growth.
  • Strong commercial judgment across pricing, contracting, partnerships, and export considerations
  • Experience building structure in a fast-moving environment without slowing it down; comfort operating across regions, cultures, and time zones; and the ability to earn trust quickly with country managers, executives, customers, and partners.
  • Clearance Required: TS/SCI

Physical Requirements

  • Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
  • Participation in virtual and in-person meetings
  • Ability to attend planned meetings and/or work in classified spaces within the specified work regions
  • Ability to travel internationally as required by the business

Orbis Benefits

Beyond the opportunity to work alongside practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, joining Orbis means real ownership over outcomes that matter; the chance to build technology that gives the United States Government and its allies a genuine decision advantage, not just another dashboard. From competitive retirement matching to a PTO policy that encourages real time off, we're committed to creating an environment where our team can do their best work and still have a life outside of it.

Our comprehensive benefits package is designed to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. A full list of benefits is shared with candidates following an initial conversation with our HR team, so you'll have a clear picture of the support and resources available to you as part of the Orbis team.

Orbis Locations

Orbis works in whatever arrangement the mission requires. Depending on the role, that might mean five days a week on a customer site, full-time in one of our offices, a hybrid schedule, or fully remote work; our team is spread across 25 states and four countries to match. We make sure every team member has the tools and access needed to do the work, wherever that work happens.

Travel is common across many Orbis roles, particularly those supporting customer missions in the field.

Orbis is headquartered in McLean, VA, with additional office locations in Taipei, Taiwan, and Canberra, Australia.

Orbis is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We are committed to providing a work environment free of discrimination and harassment, and we make employment decisions based on merit,

qualifications, and business need. Orbis does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law.

Orbis complies with all applicable equal opportunity and non-discrimination laws in every jurisdiction in which we operate. Reasonable accommodation is available to applicants and employees with disabilities upon request.

Créée en 2023, Golden Hire est la première agence de recrutement spécialisée dans l'accompagnement des infopreneurs et des entreprises digitales. Notre mission : recruter les meilleurs talents pour booster la performance de nos clients.
