Pour soutenir notre croissance, nous recherchons un(e) Recruteur(se) Freelance pour alimenter en continu notre pipe de candidats qualifiés, en lien direct avec le Responsable Recrutement.

Ton rôle : sourcer, préqualifier et évaluer les meilleurs talents pour nos clients.

Si tu es passionné(e) par le sourcing et la chasse de talents et que tu veux rejoindre une agence de recrutement en pleine structuration, ce poste est fait pour toi !

🎯 Tes missions:

En lien étroit avec le Responsable Recrutement, tes missions seront les suivantes :

Sourcing & chasse

  • Tu définis et affines ta stratégie de chasse (mots-clés, canaux, ciblage).

  • Tu chasses activement des profils sur LinkedIn, notre ATS, nos bases de données candidats et tout autre canal pertinent.

  • Tu rédiges et envoies des messages d'approche, en volume et en qualité et tu suis tes relances.

  • Tu traites quotidiennement les candidatures entrantes dans notre ATS.

  • Tu es force de proposition sur les canaux : si la chasse sur les outils existants ne donne pas les résultats attendus, tu ne te contentes pas de constater le blocage, tu proposes activement de nouvelles pistes (nouveaux réseaux, groupes, communautés, plateformes, approches multicanal).

  • Tu te maintiens à jour sur les meilleures pratiques de sourcing dans l'écosystème infopreneur/digital : tu sais où se trouvent les bons profils, et où ils se trouveront demain.

  • Tu es orienté(e) solution : quand le vivier est mince, tu cherches comment le débloquer, tu arrives avec des solutions, pas des problèmes.

Préqualification

  • Tu mènes les préqualifications téléphoniques pour les profils chassés afin de valider les critères clés : disponibilité, motivations, compétences de base, adéquation avec le poste.

  • Tu rédiges une synthèse concise et exploitable pour chaque profil présenté au Responsable Recrutement : points forts, points de vigilance, éléments factuels observés, critères validés/non validés et recommandation argumentée

  • Tu ne transmets que les profils qui passent le filtre : la qualité de ce qui remonte est de ta responsabilité.

Entretiens :

  • Tu conduis en autonomie les premiers entretiens sur les rôles opérationnels.

  • Tu utilises la trame d'entretien préparée en amont.

  • Tu évalues rigoureusement : compétences, soft skills, adéquation culturelle, motivation réelle.

  • Tu creuses au-delà des réponses superficielles ou incomplètes : tu vas chercher des faits et du concret, tu n'hésites pas à challenger les profils sur les points essentiels.

  • Tu envoies une synthèse au Responsable Recrutement avec des recommandations claires.

Relation & suivi candidats

  • Tu es le premier point de contact des candidats : tu présentes le poste et le contexte, tu réponds aux questions, tu vérifies l’adéquation avec le profil.

  • Tu assures un suivi actif des candidats tout au long du process : relances, mises à jour, coordination des disponibilités.

  • Tu organises les entretiens avec le Responsable Recrutement pour les profils validés.

  • Tu donnes un retour qualitatif, personnalisé et constructif à chaque candidat non retenu.

  • Tu prends des références sur les profils avancés dans le process, avant présentation au client.

  • Tu veilles à ce qu'aucun candidat ne reste sans nouvelles : l'expérience candidat est l’un des piliers de Golden Hire.

Reporting & visibilité

  • Tu partages proactivement tes actions : le Responsable Recrutement est informé de l'avancement de la chasse au fil de la semaine (profils contactés, réponses reçues, entretiens planifiés).

  • Tu remontes les blocages sans attendre : vivier qui ne donne rien, profil prometteur qui se désiste, volume en dessous des attentes, tu signales immédiatement pour qu'on puisse ajuster.

  • Tu arrives à ton point hebdo avec le Responsable Recrutement avec tes chiffres à jour et un debrief clair des actions passées et à venir.

🔎 Profil recherché:

💼 Expérience:

  • Tu as 2 à 3 ans d'expérience minimum en recrutement dans des environnements avec de forts enjeux, du sourcing volumique et délais serrés. Idéalement en cabinet ou ESN.

  • Tu peux démontrer un vrai track record chiffré sur du recrutement volumique et/ou pénurique.

  • Tu as évolué dans des environnements changeants et exigeants : tu sais avancer sans process figé et t'adapter à des briefs différents.

  • Tu as eu des missions où le besoin a évolué en cours de route, où il fallait distinguer ce que le client disait chercher de ce qu'il lui fallait réellement, ou faire évoluer la cible après les premiers entretiens.

  • En bonus : tu as une expérience ou une bonne connaissance du monde de l'infopreneuriat (coaching, formation en ligne, business digital), et/ou une expérience de sourcing/recrutement sur des rôles digitaux (Closer, Setter, CSM, Marketing).

🔨 Compétences:

  • Tu maîtrises le sourcing et la chasse : LinkedIn Recruiter, jobboards, CVthèques… tu maîtrises les outils, mais surtout tu sais construire une stratégie efficace pour repérer et attirer les bons profils.

  • Tu sais identifier lorsqu'un brief doit être affiné ou recalibré et faire remonter des observations concrètes au Responsable Recrutement à partir des premiers retours terrain.

  • Tu es à l’aise avec les outils de travail en remote comme Slack, Notion, la suite Google et les ATS.

  • Tu utilises l'IA comme levier de productivité et d’analyse pour cibler les bons profils, affiner tes stratégies de chasse, rédiger des messages pertinents sans pour autant lui déléguer ton jugement de recruteur.

  • Tu es à l’aise pour mener des entretiens en visio en toute autonomie, tu sais creuser au-delà des informations superficielles avec un vrai sens de l’écoute et de l’analyse.

  • Tu sais suivre des KPI, les interpréter et ajuster ton approche en fonction des résultats.

  • Tu es capable de mener beaucoup d'appels, clairs et concis, pour préqualifier efficacement en 10-15 min : tu aimes le contact candidat.

  • Tu rédiges sans faute et es à l'aise pour écrire des messages d'approche maximisant l’engagement.

🤝🏻 Qualités personnelles:

  • Tu vises l’efficacité, tu veux que chaque recrutement aboutisse, avec un vrai souci de qualité.

  • Tu es en veille constante sur les pratiques de sourcing et l'usage de l'IA.

  • Tu acceptes le feedback, tu cherches à t'améliorer et tu as une vraie curiosité pour progresser dans ton métier.

  • Tu vois un recrutement compliqué comme un challenge motivant, pas comme un découragement : tu explores de nouveaux canaux plutôt que de te limiter aux plateformes classiques en cas de blocage. Tu arrives avec des solutions, pas juste avec des problèmes.

  • Tu es autonome : tu avances seul(e) sans qu'on ait besoin de te relancer et tu tiens tes engagements. Tu gères efficacement ton temps, priorises les tâches, structures ton travail et respectes les délais.

  • Tu es réactif(ve) et disponible, capable de répondre rapidement aux besoins et demandes. Tu sais tenir des délais de recrutement serrés.

  • Tu es capable de réorganiser rapidement ta semaine lorsqu'une mission devient prioritaire, qu'un brief évolue ou qu'un recrutement nécessite soudainement davantage de chasse ou d'entretiens.

  • Tu es le premier point de contact entre Golden Hire et les candidats : tu communiques avec clarté, tu sais donner des feedback constructifs.

  • Tu as une excellente communication, à l'écrit comme à l'oral, aussi bien avec les candidats qu'avec l'équipe interne.

  • Tu évalues les candidats avec objectivité et exigence, en t’appuyant sur des critères clairs et des observations concrètes.

  • Tu aimes ce que tu fais, tu as envie d’avoir de l’impact et ça se voit.

🚫 Cette mission n'est pas pour toi si…

  • Tu viens avec des problèmes plutôt que des solutions.

  • Tu te décourages lors des recrutements compliqués.

  • Tu n’es pas à l’aise sur des recrutements de profils pénuriques où il faut aller vite et apporter du volume et de la qualité.

👉 Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

  • 100 % télétravail et horaires flexibles : travaille d'où tu veux, quand tu veux, tant que les résultats sont au rendez-vous.

  • Missions stimulantes et variées : concentre-toi sur des projets à fort impact, auprès des meilleurs infopreneurs du marché francophone, sans prospection commerciale à gérer.

  • Méthodologie et cadre déjà en place : tu bénéficies d’un cadre structuré avec une méthodologie éprouvée, des templates, un système de suivi des candidatures et des outils de sourcing pour te concentrer sur l’essentiel : sourcer et recruter efficacement.

  • Accompagnement personnalisé : tu es formé(e) à nos process, tu reçois du feedback régulier et tu n’es jamais laissé(e) seul(e) face à une difficulté.

  • Bienveillance et esprit d’équipe : l’entraide, la confiance et la convivialité sont au cœur de notre ADN, même à distance.

  • Possibilité d'évoluervers un rôle de Responsable Recrutement, avec relation client et gestion de A à Z de tes propres clients, voire management d'autres recruteurs (selon ton niveau d’engagement, de fiabilité et de performance)

📅 Modalités :

  3. Entretien final

Budget & Forecast Process Ownership

Strategic Support

jobs.description:
*CANDIDATES MUST BE LOCATED IN THE UNITED STATES**

About SafelyYou

SafelyYou’s passionate mission is to empower safer, more person-centered care across senior living through world-leading AI, industry-changing hardware, and remote expert clinicians, significantly improving outcomes for residents while increasing peace of mind for families and reducing costs for communities.

Originating in 2015 as the doctoral research of CEO George Netscher—and inspired by his own family's experience with Alzheimer's disease—SafelyYou was spun out of UC Berkeley’s Artificial Intelligence Research Lab, one of the top five AI research groups in the world. And today, our company is solving critical challenges in senior living, from resident falls and ER visits to staffing concerns, length of stay, and NOI. All helping ensure that communities can focus on improved care for residents while still reaching their financial goals.

SafelyYou is one of five most innovative fall technologies referenced in the Senate Falls Report (2019), a winner of the McKnight’s Tech Partner of the Year, and has been named to Fortune’s Impact 20 list, which recognizes companies making people’s lives better through innovation.

Your Role at SafelyYou
SafelyYou is looking for a builder — a Director of FP&A who will own and shape the financial

planning function at a pivotal moment in our growth. This is a high-impact, high-visibility role reporting directly to the VP of Finance. You will be the primary architect of how we plan, forecast, and measure financial performance across a business with both SaaS and hardware dimensions.

We’re looking for someone who can translate numbers into stories to drive decisions — who understands that the value of FP&A is not in the outputs it produces, but in the actions it enables.

You will work directly with the CEO, COO, and department heads to ensure financial clarity drives better resource allocation, faster decision-making, sharper forecasting, and stronger operating discipline.

You will inherit an existing foundation — financial models, budgets, and reporting packages are in place— and will have the opportunity to assess, refine, and, where necessary, rebuild them, maturing the function to match our next stage of growth.

This is a director-level individual contributor role to start, with the understanding that, as the function is built out, external or internal resources could be added to build out a small team over the next few years.

Salary Range:$170,000 to $190,000 annually

Key Responsibilities:

Financial Planning

  • Lead the annual budget and mid-year budget refresh processes across all functions, with clear ownership of planning dimensions by cost center, headcount, product line, and customer type

  • Develop and maintain a long-range financial plan that connects strategic objectives to operating assumptions

  • Work with senior leaders to set sales and revenue targets by product, for both contracted and utilization models

  • Partner with HR and Operations to support headcount planning by building models for both operational and COGS resource allocation, evaluating short-term and long-term trade-offs

Forecasting

  • Partner with sales and business development to build robust pipeline and sales forecast models, providing operational teams with timely visibility into volume, timing, and resource requirements

  • Maintain a risk and opportunity tracker updated monthly, surfacing material variances before they land in the actuals

  • Build and maintain SaaS and hardware-specific forecasting models incorporating ARR, net revenue retention, churn, implementation pipeline, and inventory purchase and deployment schedules

Performance Reporting

  • Design and own the monthly management reporting package for internal leadership and quarterly board decks

  • Own the FP&A side of the monthly close — coordinating with Accounting on accruals, reconciling actuals against forecast, and ensuring a clean, validated financial view is in place before management reporting is distributed

  • Establish a single, authoritative source of truth for key metrics and build and maintain dashboards that give leadership real-time visibility into business performance

  • Assess the current FP&A technology landscape, identify and implement best-in-class tools, and drive automation and efficiency across planning, forecasting, and reporting through great tooling and AI

Performance Analysis

  • Translate financial variances into root cause analysis with clear operating implications — drilling from board-level numbers down to the specific business unit, product, or customer driver

  • Connect financial findings to recommended actions, not just observations

The Ideal Candidate:
Experience

  • 7+ years of progressive FP&A experience, with at least 3 years in a senior or lead role

  • Required: experience in a SaaS business with recurring revenue metrics (ARR, NRR, CAC, LTV, gross margin)

  • Required: experience in a business with a hardware or physical product component — understanding of COGS, installation economics, and inventory dynamics

  • Required: startup or high-growth environment experience; comfort operating without established processes, building from scratch, and prioritizing ruthlessly

Skills

  • Exceptional financial modeling capability — three-statement models, scenario analysis, and driver-based forecasting

  • Strong command of SaaS metrics and unit economics

  • Experience building or improving FP&A infrastructure: data definitions, model architecture, reporting workflows, and automation

  • Expert level in both Google Sheets and Microsoft Excel

How You Work

  • Skilled at distilling complex financial information into concise, board-appropriate narratives; equally comfortable presenting to the CEO and walking a department head through a cost center variance

  • Proactive and transparent communicator who surfaces risks and issues early, frames them in context, and arrives with a point of view on what to do about them

  • A natural collaborator who knows how to build alignment without letting it slow things down — able to bring the right people along and still hit the deadline.

  • Bias toward clarity and action — produces analysis that is easy to comprehend and changes decisions, not analysis that gets filed

  • Comfortable with ambiguity and able to prioritize across competing demands in a lean team environment

Why Join Us? You Can Make a Difference!

SafelyYou offers a competitive compensation package, including but not limited to:

  • A mission-driven company culture

  • Fully remote

  • Competitive salary & benefits, including fully paid employee premiums for Medical, Dental, and Vision

  • 401k Program

  • Monthly Education, Well-being & WFH stipends

  • Non-accrual PTO

  • Growth Potential

  • Company Retreats

  • Medical & Family/Parental Leave

At SafelyYou, we believe that a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace makes us a more relevant, competitive, and resilient company. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workforce that celebrates diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, color, ancestry, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital or family status, disability, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.

We value all the perspectives our team members bring to the table, and that is why we don’t look for culture fit, but culture add. We want to hear from YOU! We encourage you to apply even if you do not fit 100% of the technical requirements.

Blending Program Management

  • Evaluate blending opportunities to improve product value, flexibility, capacity, and operational efficiency.
  • Develop blending strategies based on product specifications, supply availability, terminal capabilities, customer requirements, and economics.

  • Establish appropriate controls for blend components, treat rates, recipes, inventories, and finished product specifications.

Technical and Operational Support

  • Provide technical expertise and operational support to terminal teams for blending activities.
  • Troubleshoot blending system, equipment, process, and product quality issues.

  • Establish operating parameters and controls necessary to achieve consistent and reliable blending performance.
    Support terminal teams in resolving blending-related operational issues.

Product Quality and Compliance

  • Work closely with Product Quality to ensure blended products meet applicable specifications and customer requirements.
  • Develop and maintain blending procedures that support consistent product quality.
  • Ensure blending processes are aligned with applicable ASTM, API, regulatory, and company requirements.
  • Participate in investigations of off-specification product, contamination, blending errors, or other product quality incidents.
  • Develop and implement corrective and preventive actions related to blending activities.
  • Support audits, inspections, and compliance activities related to blending operations.

Process Standardization and Continuous Improvement

  • Develop standardized blending procedures and best practices for use across the terminal network.
  • Identify opportunities to improve blending accuracy, reliability, capacity, flexibility, and cost performance.
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives related to blending operations.
  • Establish performance metrics to measure blending effectiveness and goal attainment.
  • Evaluate lessons learned from blending projects and incidents and incorporate improvements into company standards.
  • Support the development and maintenance of blending-related sections of the Operations Manual and applicable SOPs.

Inventory and Economic Optimization

  • Work with Supply & Trading and Commercial teams to understand supply, demand, and blending requirements.
  • Optimize component inventories and blending capacity to support operational and commercial objectives.
  • Evaluate blending opportunities based on product availability, specifications, storage capacity, and economics.
  • Support analysis of blend yields, component usage, product quality, and value extraction.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce product losses, improve component utilization, and increase blending flexibility.

Systems, Data and Reporting

  • Work with IT and Data Systems to develop automated blending systems, controls, dashboards, and reporting.
  • Establish appropriate data requirements for monitoring blending performance.
  • Track and analyze blending metrics, including component usage, blend accuracy, product quality, inventory, losses, and operational performance.
  • Support development and implementation of systems that improve visibility and control of blending operations.
  • Maintain accurate blending documentation, procedures, recipes, and operational records.

Team Leadership and Training

  • Provide technical leadership and training to terminal personnel responsible for blending activities.
  • Develop training materials and operating guidance for blending processes and systems.
  • Foster a culture of operational discipline, continuous improvement, and accountability.
  • Work with terminal leadership to ensure blending procedures are properly implemented and consistently followed.
  • Provide subject matter expertise to cross-functional teams on blending-related projects and initiatives.

Project and Change Management

  • Lead or support blending-related projects from concept through implementation.
  • Participate in Management of Change (MOC) processes associated with blending systems, procedures, equipment, and products.
  • Coordinate with Engineering, Operations, EHS, Product Quality, IT, Supply & Trading, and Commercial teams during project development and implementation.

  • Support project commissioning, startup, and post-implementation evaluation.

The Corporate Project Manager, Quality and Professional Governance supports the Corporate Director of Healthcare Quality and Safety to ensure Shriners Children’s resources, policies, processes, and documentation align with Joint Commission (JC) and National Committee for Quality Assurance (NCQA) standards and requirements for professional practice quality and professional governance.   • Collaborate with others in the planning, development, and implementation of regulatory standards and process changes applicable to licensed independent practitioners, related to quality functions.

  • Provide guidance and oversight to Medical Staff Office ensuring maintenance of Medical Staff Bylaws, standard privileges, and other documents in accordance with SHC MS Bylaws, HRPR, JC standards, and state laws.

Major Technical Tender Return Coordinator

Role Purpose

The Major Technical Tender Return Coordinator is responsible for the leadership, coordination, and management of all major technical tender submissions, ensuring the delivery of high-quality, compliant, and professionally presented proposals to clients. The role serves as the central coordination point between the sales team, internal factories, technical departments, and engineering resources to develop compelling and technically robust tender returns.

This position owns the complete tender return package, from enquiry review through submission, while supporting the transition of successful projects into the post-order delivery phase. A key element of the role is presenting technical solutions, equipment selections, and tender submissions directly to consultants, contractors, end users, and clients.

---

Key Responsibilities

Major Tender Return Management

  • Take overall responsibility for the coordination and delivery of major technical tender submissions.
  • Manage the complete tender return process from enquiry receipt to final submission.
  • Review client specifications, tender documentation, and project requirements.
  • Develop submission strategies to ensure commercial and technical requirements are effectively addressed.
  • Ensure all tender returns are submitted on time and to the highest professional standard.
  • Maintain tender schedules, document control, and submission records.

Technical Data Coordination

  • Coordinate all technical information required for tender submissions.
  • Liaise with internal factories and technical departments to gather and validate product information.
  • Ensure technical data sheets, performance selections, calculations, drawings, and supporting documentation are accurate and complete.
  • Verify compliance with project specifications and identify any technical deviations.
  • Coordinate project-specific technical responses and clarifications.

Factory Coordination

  • Act as the primary point of contact between the UK business and internal manufacturing facilities.
  • Coordinate factory input relating to equipment selections, technical data, drawings, compliance documentation, and programme requirements.
  • Ensure factory responses align with project specifications and client expectations.
  • Facilitate communication between internal stakeholders and factory engineering teams.

jobs.excerpt: Our Mission:6sense's mission is to multiply what matters: growth, retention, and efficiency.
jobs.description:
Our Mission:

6sense's mission is to multiply what matters: growth, retention, and efficiency. We envision a future where companies, teams and people reach their full potential.

Our People:

People are the heart and soul of 6sense. We serve with passion and purpose. We live by our Being 6sense values of Win as One Team, Stay Curious, Do The Right Thing, Own the Outcome, and Create Belonging. Every 6sensor plays a part in deﬁning the future of our industry-leading technology. 6sense is a place where difference-makers roll up their sleeves, take risks, act with integrity, and measure success by the value we create for our customers. We want 6sense to be the best chapter of your career.

Enterprise AI Business Solutions Partner

Business Solutions Partner — GTM & Finance Systems

Location

Costa Rica

Function / Dept
Business Technology — Enterprise Applications

Reports to

Director, Enterprise Applications

Position Summary

6sense is seeking an Enterprise AI Business Solutions Partner to help transform how business functions leverage AI, automation, and enterprise technology to achieve their goals.

This role sits at the intersection of business consulting, AI solution design, automation engineering, and value realization. You will partner with teams across Go-to-Market, Customer Success, Support, Legal, Finance, and Partner Operations to identify opportunities where AI and automation can simplify work, improve user experiences, reduce costs, and accelerate business outcomes.

Unlike a traditional Business Systems Analyst or Business Solution Partner, this role is expected to move beyond requirements gathering. You will evaluate business processes, build proof-of-concepts, create AI agents, develop low-code automations, and validate business value before solutions are scaled into production. Working closely with the Enterprise AI Engineering team, you will translate complex business challenges into technical requirements and implementation plans while independently delivering design prototypes and lightweight solutions using platforms such as Microsoft Copilot, Claude, Workato, and other approved enterprise AI technologies.

A successful candidate combines strong business analysis skills with hands-on technical aptitude. They can engage stakeholders, map workflows, build basic automations, create AI-powered solutions, measure outcomes, and communicate recommendations to both business and technical audiences.

This is a growth role within a new Enterprise AI career track. You will work under the guidance of the Lead Enterprise AI Business Solutions Engineer and will be measured on business outcomes, including adoption, productivity gains, automation impact, cost avoidance, and process improvements. As you progress, you will take increasing ownership of a portfolio of business capabilities, including identifying, developing, delivering and maturing measurable AI-driven value.

Responsibilities

Tool Inventory & AI Efficiency Discovery

  • Build and maintain the AI and tool inventory for your assigned function: owner, use case, active users, annual cost, renewal date, AI features in use, contract exit terms and replacement feasibility.
  • Find where AI features we already pay for are unused, duplicated or overlap with other tools, and document the findings.
  • Track renewal dates and flag every contract at least 120 days before the notice date so a build-vs-buy decision can be made in time.
  • Run discovery interviews and working sessions with stakeholders to understand how work actually gets done, and surface the business problem behind the requested feature.
  • Map current processes and estimate the time spent, the number of people involved and the frequency, so every opportunity has a baseline.

Build-vs-Buy Analysis & Business Cases

  • Prepare the inputs for build-vs-buy analysis: what the tool does, how deeply it is integrated, compliance burden, usage compared with cost, and realistic replacement scope.
  • Contribute to business cases that compare three-year build, run and support cost with vendor cost, working with the Lead and with Enterprise AI Engineers on the build side.
  • Agree baselines with business owners before work starts and record their sign-off, so savings and hours returned can be validated later.
  • Recommend which candidates to pursue first, using renewal timing, savings potential and build feasibility.

Prototyping & Applied AI

  • Build prototypes and simple agents with Claude and Copilot to test whether a tool, or part of a workflow, can be replaced or improved.
  • Write clear, build-ready context for Enterprise AI Engineers: the process, the data involved, example inputs and outputs, acceptance criteria and edge cases.
  • Help define evaluation criteria, guardrails, human-in-the-loop checkpoints and escalation paths before anything reaches production.
  • Design the process around the AI: what changes for the seller, agent or analyst, what training is needed and how exceptions are handled.
  • Bring AI fluency to stakeholders: help non-technical teams understand what these tools can and cannot reliably do, and set realistic expectations.

Stakeholder Partnership

  • Serve as the named Business Solutions Partner for your assigned function, and the point of contact for intake, priorities and status.
  • Translate business needs into clear, buildable stories and acceptance criteria, and translate technical trade-offs back into language stakeholders can act on.
  • Keep stakeholders informed on what is changing, what is being built and what may move more slowly during the transition.
  • Escalate misalignment, scope drift and risk early to the Lead before they become executive issues.

Hands-On Salesforce & Delivery

  • Configure and deliver declarative Salesforce solutions (flows, validation rules, record types, page layouts, permission sets, reports and dashboards) for small requests, with guidance on larger ones.
  • Understand Apex, integrations and data model implications well enough to scope work accurately and hold a credible technical conversation with engineers.
  • Own UAT for your function: define test scenarios, coordinate stakeholder testing and support release sign-off.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of processes, solution designs and system dependencies.

Measurement & Ways of Working

  • Track adoption (percent of target users active) for anything shipped in your function, and report what is working and what should be retired.
  • Report hours returned and spend avoided using the agreed baseline, and flag figures that are not yet validated.
  • Work in the team’s agentic delivery model: use the intake agent, async standups and automated sprint summaries instead of status meetings, and give feedback on what to improve.
  • Contribute to team standards for the inventory, business case template and requirements.

Skills & Experience

Required

  • 2–4 years of relevant experience as a business analyst, business solution partner, business systems analyst, Salesforce administrator or operations analyst supporting business stakeholders, preferably at a SaaS company.
  • Hands-on Salesforce administration experience (Sales Cloud and/or Service Cloud), including Flow Builder, validation rules, permission sets and reporting.
  • Salesforce Certified Administrator, or obtained within the first six months in the role.
  • Daily, practical use of AI tools such as Claude, Copilot or similar, with solid prompt design and an understanding of their limits.
  • Strong spreadsheet and data fluency: cleaning data, building summaries and sizing a problem.
  • Process mapping and structured interviewing skills.
  • Clear written and spoken English; able to present findings to U.S.-based stakeholders.
  • Must be located in Costa Rica and able to maintain consistent working overlap with U.S. business hours.

Preferred

  • Experience putting an AI or automation solution into a live business process, even a small one, and measuring the result.
  • Familiarity with GTM processes (lead to cash, pipeline, forecasting) or Support operations (case management, routing, knowledge), or with Finance, Legal or Partner operations.
  • Basic financial literacy: reading a vendor cost, comparing build and run cost, and calculating a payback period.
  • Exposure to SQL, APIs or low-code tools; interest in using Claude Code under guidance.
  • Salesforce Certified Advanced Administrator, Business Analyst or Agentforce Specialist.
  • Experience in an Agile team; familiarity with Jira, Asana or similar.
  • Bilingual English/Spanish.

What we value

  • Curiosity and a bias to build and test, not just to document.
  • Honesty about what is validated and what is an estimate.
  • Comfort with change, since this track is new and will keep evolving.

How This Role Is Measured

  • Accuracy and completeness of the tool inventory for your function.
  • Percent of renewals in scope identified and reviewed at least 120 days before the notice date.
  • Prototype quality, as rated by the stakeholder and the engineering lead.
  • Hours returned and spend avoided on initiatives you support, validated by the business owner.
  • Adoption of anything shipped in your function.

What Success Looks Like

First 90 days

  • Inventory for your function is complete and reviewed with business owners.
  • Renewal calendar for your tools is documented, with the next three renewals ranked by savings potential.
  • Two or more stakeholder discovery sessions completed, with baselines drafted for the top opportunities.
  • First prototype built with Claude or Copilot and reviewed with the Lead and an engineer.

First year

  • Your stakeholder group treats you as its partner for systems and AI work and routes requests to you rather than escalating.
  • At least two prototypes evaluated end to end, and at least one taken to production with Enterprise AI Engineers, with measured impact.
  • At least one initiative with a documented baseline, business-owner sign-off and a validated hours-returned or spend-avoided number.
  • Renewals for your function reviewed before notice dates, with a documented decision on each.
  • You are operating toward IC4: leading a build-vs-buy analysis from discovery to recommendation with little guidance.

Our Benefits:

Full-time employees can take advantage of health coverage, paid parental leave, generous paid time-off and holidays, quarterly self-care days off, and stock options. We’ll make sure you have the equipment and support you need to work and connect with your teams, at home or in one of our oﬃces.

From wellness days to ERG-hosted events, we celebrate and energize all 6sense employees and their backgrounds.

About Stripe

About the team

Stripe is beloved by developers for the simplicity of our APIs, the thoroughness of our documentation, and our focus on developer experience. The Technical Solutions Engineering (TSE) team is the glue that supports our developer-users and champions developer experience as being central to the overall experience of our users. TSE interacts directly with developer-users more than any other team at Stripe, so your role will have a significant impact on what Stripe is known for and values most. When we do our job well, developers all over the world are able to smoothly launch and grow their businesses on Stripe, whether they’re integrating payments for the first time or building complex financial systems.

What you’ll do

TSEs understand the fundamentals of programming incredibly well and eagerly jump in and familiarize themselves with others’ code. You will do a wide variety of things, including explaining technical concepts about Stripe’s products, build and debug integrations with developers, and produce/improve guides that help our users solve particular problems to be successful with Stripe. jobs.description:
An applied research team within NVIDIA’s Networking Systems & Software Architecture group is solving some of AI’s hardest infrastructure problems. The team builds systems-level software that moves data between GPUs, nodes, and storage at the speed modern AI demands—spanning low-level transport optimization, hardware-software co-design, and communication frameworks that plug directly into production AI stacks. The team's charter expands into emerging domains including quantum computing interconnects.

The Senior Architect role is to own modules and projects end-to-end—from scoping research questions to shipping production code. It calls for a recognized expert who drives technical decisions, pulls in ideas from research and industry, and regularly prototypes new approaches to prove a point. The work lives at the boundary of applied research and production engineering!

What you will be doing:

  • Architecting and implementing high-performance communication and memory management libraries for distributed AI

  • Driving hardware-software co-optimization with GPU, DPU, NIC, and switch teams through GPUDirect RDMA, NVLink, and next-generation interconnects

  • Profiling and optimizing data movement across GPU memory, system DRAM, NVMe, and network fabrics

  • Integrating networking capabilities into AI serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM

  • Contributing to and maintaining open-source projects, mentoring engineers, conducting design reviews, and prototyping experimental technologies to evaluate their viability

What we need to see:

  • 12+ years in systems software and/or networking with demonstrated ownership of complex projects.

  • MS, PhD or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.

  • Solid understanding of high-performance networking: InfiniBand, RoCE, RDMA, NVLink, GPUDirect.

  • Strong C/C++/Rust systems programming with comfort in performance profiling and low-level debugging.

  • Understanding of ML systems concepts—transformer architectures, KV cache mechanics, model parallelism, or distributed training and inference patterns.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • Knowledge of ML inference frameworks (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM) and their communication requirements.

  • Knowledge of storage networking (NVMe-oF, GPUDirect Storage, S3).

  • Background of Reinforcement Learning systems.

With competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package, NVIDIA is widely regarded as one of the most desirable technology employers in the world. jobs.title: Principal Technical Consultant - Operational Technology, Network Security
jobs.excerpt: AHEAD builds platforms for digital business.  By weaving together advances in cloud infrastructure, automation and analytics, and software delivery, we help enterprises deliver on the promise of digital transformation.
jobs.description:
AHEAD builds platforms for digital business. By weaving together advances in cloud infrastructure, automation and analytics, and software delivery, we help enterprises deliver on the promise of digital transformation.
At AHEAD, we prioritize creating a culture of belonging, where all perspectives and voices are represented, valued, respected, and heard. We create spaces to empower everyone to speak up, make change, and drive the culture at AHEAD.
We are an equal opportunity employer, and do not discriminate based on an individual's race, national origin, color, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, marital status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law, whether actual or perceived.
We embrace all candidates that will contribute to the diversification and enrichment of ideas and perspectives at AHEAD.

About AHEAD

AHEAD helps organizations modernize and secure the technology that runs their business. We are building a deeper Operational Technology capability for clients in manufacturing, energy, utilities, healthcare, transportation, and other industries where uptime, safety, and resilience matter. This role helps shape that capability while delivering meaningful client work.

The Role

The Principal Technical Consultant, Operational Technology is a senior technical leader and trusted advisor, and the primary technical resource on OT Assessments and SRDP (strategy, roadmap, design, and plan) engagements. This is a hands-on role. You will lead technical discovery, facilitate workshops, analyze industrial environments, build architecture and roadmap deliverables, guide delivery teams, and present recommendations to client leaders. You should be equally comfortable discussing a PLC network with an automation engineer, an operating model with plant leadership, and investment priorities with a CISO or CIO.

What You Will Do:

    Lead OT assessments and advisory engagements

    • Serve as the primary technical lead for OT Assessments, OT strategy work, and SRDP workstreams.
    • Plan and facilitate discovery workshops, site visits, technical deep dives, and executive working sessions.
    • Establish a safe, non-disruptive discovery approach that respects production schedules, safety requirements, and change control.
    • Assess the client environment across assets, networks, control systems, dependencies, ownership, and operational constraints, and evaluate maturity across people, process, and technology.
    • Identify risks, gaps, single points of failure, and lifecycle concerns affecting security, reliability, visibility, and resilience.
    • Produce current-state and future-state architecture views, findings, maturity assessments, and prioritized roadmaps that connect recommendations to business impact, investment, and sequencing.
    • Own the technical quality of deliverables and present findings to engineering teams, plant and operations leaders, and executives.

    Apply deep OT and cybersecurity expertise

    • Analyze OT and ICS architectures spanning PLCs, HMIs, SCADA, DCS, historians, MES, engineering workstations, safety systems, and connected edge environments.
    • Evaluate IT/OT connectivity, Purdue-aligned design, zones and conduits, industrial DMZs, segmentation, remote access, and third-party connectivity.
    • Assess asset inventory, passive visibility, communication flows, protocol use, legacy platforms, and compensating controls.
    • Evaluate identity and access, endpoint protection, vulnerability and patch management, monitoring, incident response, backup, and recovery practices. • Balance security recommendations against safety, availability, performance, maintenance windows, and long OT lifecycles.
    • Apply recognized standards including NIST SP 800-82, ISA/IEC 62443, and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, plus applicable regulatory requirements.
    • Bring a point of view on secure remote operations, edge computing, industrial wireless and private 5G, cloud-connected OT, and OT data.
    Lead technical teams and delivery quality
    • Lead and delegate work across technical consultants, engineers, and client resources on one or more workstreams.
    • Break complex problems into work packages with clear approach, decision points, and acceptance criteria.
    • Coordinate with Project Managers, account teams, and other AHEAD practices to deliver an integrated solution.
    • Review technical work for accuracy and clarity, and mentor consultants on architecture, analysis, documentation, and client interaction.
    • Contribute to repeatable methods, templates, and reference architectures for the OT practice.

    Contribute to business development

    • Participate in discovery and qualification meetings as the OT subject matter expert.
    • Help shape scopes of work, estimates, work breakdown structures, assumptions, risks, and proposals.
    • Support technical solutioning and proposal presentations with senior client stakeholders.
    • Develop practical thought leadership, internal enablement, and client briefings that strengthen AHEAD's OT brand.

What You Will Bring:

    Required Qualifications

    • 10 or more years delivering complex technology, cybersecurity, network, or engineering solutions, with significant Operational Technology or ICS experience.
    • Demonstrated experience leading OT or ICS assessments, architecture, segmentation, cybersecurity, or modernization engagements.
    • Strong understanding of control-system architectures and industrial protocols such as Modbus, DNP3, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, or OPC UA.
    • Strong OT networking and security depth, including routing and switching, firewalls, industrial DMZs, segmentation, remote access, identity, and monitoring.
    • Ability to explain the operational impact of technical decisions where safety, availability, and production continuity are critical.
    • Experience producing architecture diagrams, maturity assessments, prioritized roadmaps, and executive presentations.
    • Experience facilitating workshops with stakeholders from the plant floor through executive leadership.
    • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to tailor complex material to the audience.
    • Demonstrated ability to lead technical teams, delegate, review work, and mentor others.
    • Willingness to travel to client sites as engagements require.
    • Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

    Preferred Qualifications

    • Experience with ISA/IEC 62443, NIST SP 800-82, NIST CSF, NERC CIP, FDA, or other industry-specific requirements.
    • Background in manufacturing, energy, utilities, water, healthcare, transportation, chemicals, or pharmaceuticals.
    • Experience with OT asset discovery and passive monitoring platforms, industrial firewalls, secure remote access, or OT security operations.
    • Experience with IT/OT convergence, edge platforms, industrial wireless, private 5G, or OT data platforms.
    • Experience developing estimates, work breakdown structures, service briefs, or statements of work.
    • Certifications such as GICSP, GRID, CISSP, ISA/IEC 62443, or CCNP/CCIE.

How You Will be Successful:

    In your first year, you will independently lead OT discovery and assessment work that clients trust, produce client-ready deliverables that move decisions forward, earn credibility with both plant-floor and executive stakeholders, strengthen the delivery team through coaching and review, and contribute reusable OT methods that improve how AHEAD delivers.

Why This Role Matters:

    OT consulting is not about applying enterprise IT controls unchanged to a plant floor. It takes technical depth, operational humility, and the ability to make progress without losing sight of safety, reliability, or recovery. If you have spent your career understanding how industrial environments work and want to help organizations make them more secure and resilient, this role puts that experience in front of the clients who need it.
The compensation range indicated in this posting reflects the On-Target Earnings (“OTE”) for this role, which includes a base salary and any applicable target bonus amount. This OTE range may vary based on the candidate’s relevant experience, qualifications, and geographic location.

Why AHEAD:

Through our daily work and internal groups like Moving Women AHEAD and RISE AHEAD, we value and benefit from diversity of people, ideas, experience, and everything in between.
We fuel growth by stacking our office with top-notch technologies in a multi-million-dollar lab, by encouraging cross department training and development, sponsoring certifications and credentials for continued learning.

jobs.description:
The Company

Serving the People Who Serve the People

Granicus is driven by the excitement of building, implementing, and maintaining technology that is transforming the Govtech industry by bringing governments and its constituents together. We are on a mission to support our customers with meeting the needs of their communities and implementing our technology in ways that are equitable and inclusive. Granicus has consistently appeared on the GovTech 100 list over the past 5 years and has been recognized as the best companies to work on BuiltIn.

Over the last 25 years, we have served 5,500 federal, state, and local government agencies and more than 300 million citizen subscribers power an unmatched Subscriber Network that use our digital solutions to make the world a better place. With comprehensive cloud-based solutions for communications, government website design, meeting and agenda management software, records management, and digital services, Granicus empowers stronger relationships between government and residents across the U.S., U.K., Australia, New Zealand, and Canada. By simplifying interactions with residents, while disseminating critical information, Granicus brings governments closer to the people they serve—driving meaningful change for communities around the globe.

Want to know more? See more of what we do here.

Job Summary

Granicus serves more than 7,000 public-sector agencies and powers approximately 30 billion digital interactions annually. Within the Office of the CTO, we operate an AI-native software development lifecycle: a production engineering model in which autonomous agents perform high-confidence implementation work and senior engineers orchestrate, review, and own the outcome. The model is established and operating; we are scaling it across additional delivery teams.

This role joins one of those teams. Our engineering standards are calibrated to the practices used by leading software and AI organizations — generator-verifier architecture, eval-driven development, staged deployment, and high-volume autonomous pull-request pipelines — operated within a FedRAMP-authorized environment. We are hiring practitioners who will set and uphold these standards, not engineers who simply use AI tooling.

Operating constraints (non-negotiable): agents execute only within branches; all agent-generated code passes senior human review before merging to production; autonomous execution is a force multiplier and does not transfer accountability away from the responsible engineer. Compliance obligations — NIST 800-53 Rev 5, WCAG, SOC 2, and applicable FedRAMP authorizations — are treated as engineering requirements and a source of competitive advantage.

Why this role exists

High-volume autonomous agent pipelines are straightforward to demonstrate and difficult to operate safely, performantly, and auditably at scale. This role owns that problem. It is responsible for the generator-verifier architecture, agent orchestration patterns, the eval-driven development discipline, and a continuous integration and delivery system engineered for a high volume of autonomous agent pull requests — all within a security boundary that keeps model inference inside the VPC (AWS Bedrock) and sandboxes agent actions (WASM-isolated runtime with encrypted credential storage). The role sets the engineering standards inherited by every delivery team and is the final human accountability gate before agent-generated code merges to productio

What Your Impact Will Look Like

  • Own the generator-verifier architecture — the loop in which generator agents produce changes and verifier agents, automated tests, evaluation suites, SAST/DAST, and policy checks validate them, enabling volume to scale without quality regression.
  • Define agent orchestration patterns — task decomposition, dispatch, sandboxing, and reassembly across the agent array, including secure state and credential handling via WASM-isolated runtimes and encrypted credential vaults.
  • Build and operate CI/CD for autonomous pull-request volume — a pipeline that triages, tests, and routes a high volume of agent-generated pull requests while keeping human review efficient and high-signal.
  • Establish eval-driven development as the default discipline — define measurable acceptance criteria so changes are validated against evaluation suites rather than subjective judgment.
  • Own the security boundary — in-VPC inference via AWS Bedrock (including GovCloud), least-privilege agent permissions, and an explicit mapping from NIST 800-53 Rev 5 controls to concrete pipeline guardrails, so that compliance is enforced by the architecture rather than by manual audit.
  • Serve as the final human accountability gate — define and enforce the requirement that no agent-generated code reaches production without senior human review, supported by review tooling that maximizes signal.
  • Define the engineering standards inherited by every team — branching model, review protocol, evaluation conventions, and staged deployment, and maintain the reference implementation the organization builds on.
  • Govern graduated autonomy — define the criteria by which a workstream advances from supervised to autonomous execution, supported by measured agent reliability rather than assumption.

Ownership and growth

Ownership from Day One—

  • Generator-verifier loop and orchestration patterns for a delivery team
  • CI/CD engineered for agent pull-request volume with human review as a hard gate
  • In-VPC Bedrock inference and sandboxed agent runtime as the security boundary
  • Evaluation conventions and the branching and review protocol

Scope you will Grow Into—

  • Generator-verifier loop and orchestration patterns for a delivery team
  • CI/CD engineered for agent pull-request volume with human review as a hard gate
  • In-VPC Bedrock inference and sandboxed agent runtime as the security boundary
  • Evaluation conventions and the branching and review protocol

You Will Love This Job If You Have

Required

  • Architecture of systems at scale with accountability for outcomes. Distributed systems, CI/CD, and developer platforms where your design decisions carried significant operational consequence.
  • Deep CI/CD and developer-platform expertise. You have built pipelines that other engineers depend on — testing, staged deployment, rollback, and observability — with demonstrated reliability and performance.
  • Hands-on experience operating LLM agents in production paths, including orchestration, tool use, sandboxing, evaluation, and the failure modes that emerge at volume.
  • Security-architecture expertise. Least-privilege design, secrets management, network boundary enforcement, and threat modeling, with work that withstands both audit and adversarial review.
  • A track record of setting standards adopted by others. A branching model, review protocol, or platform pattern in active use because you defined it.
  • The ability to serve as an accountability gate without becoming a bottleneck. You design review tooling and conventions that maintain high signal and low latency.

Preferred

  • High-assurance security architecture is strongly preferred for this role specifically. Demonstrated experience designing and defending a security boundary within FedRAMP, FedRAMP High, defense, financial services, or healthcare, including direct experience with formal audit. Candidates without experience operating inside an audited boundary are unlikely to be effective setting the standard for one.
  • NIST 800-53 Rev 5 fluency, including the ability to map controls to engineering guardrails directly.
  • AWS Bedrock or GovCloud experience maintaining inference and data within a compliance boundary.
  • Experience with eval-driven development or generator-verifier architectures at a frontier-model or leading platform organization.

Indicators of a strong fit

  • You regard making autonomy safe and auditable as the central technical problem, and it is the problem you want to own.
  • You hold strong, evidence-based positions on pipeline reliability and operational resilience.
  • You prefer validation against evaluation suites to subjective assessment of a pull request.
  • You read NIST 800-53 as an engineering specification rather than as administrative overhead.
  • You are prepared to own the standard the organization builds on and accept the accountability that entails.

Indicators this role is not a fit

  • You prefer feature development to platform and standards work. This role’s leverage is deliberately indirect.
  • You consider compliance to be administrative work to delegate. Here it is architecture you own.
  • You favor delivery speed over demonstrable safety when the two conflict. Within a FedRAMP boundary, demonstrable safety takes precedence.
  • You expect autonomy to mean the absence of review. The review gate is the core deliverable and is yours to safeguard.
  • You are uncomfortable declining a request for greater autonomy than a workstream’s measured reliability supports.

Pay Range

USD $175,000.00 - USD $222,000.00 /Yr.

About Us

Don’t have all the skills/experience mentioned above? At Granicus, we are trying to build diverse, inclusive teams. We do not have degree requirements for most of our roles. If you don’t meet every requirement above but are excited to learn more, we encourage you to apply. We might just be able to find another role that could be a perfect fit!

Security and Privacy Requirements

  • Responsible for Granicus information security by appropriately preserving the Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (CIA) of Granicus information assets in accordance with the company's information security program.
  • Responsible for ensuring the data privacy of our employees and customers, their data, as well as taking all required privacy training in a timely manner, in accordance with company policies.

The Team

  • We are a remote-first company with a globally distributed workforce across the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, India, Armenia, Australia, and New Zealand.

The Culture

The Impact

  • We are proud to serve dynamic organizations around the globe that use our digital solutions to make the world a better place — quite literally. We have so many powerful success stories that illustrate how our solutions are impacting the world. See more of our impact here.

The Benefits

At Granicus, we offer a comprehensive and flexible benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance—starting from day one. Here’s what you can expect as a U.S.-based team member:

Flexibility & Balance

  • Flexible Time Off – Take the time you need to rest, recharge, and live your life.
  • Company-Wide Wellbeing Days – Paid days off to unplug and focus on your mental health.
  • Work From Home Reimbursement – Support a productive home office environment.
Health & Wellness
  • Multiple Health Plan Options – Including a 100% employer-paid plan.
  • Employer HSA Contributions – When enrolled in a High-Deductible Health Plan.
  • Fitness Reimbursement Program – Stay active, your way.

Family & Future
  • Paid Parental Leave – For both birthing and non-birthing parents.
  • Traditional & Roth 401(k) – With a generous company match.
  • Life & AD&D Insurance – 100% employer-paid coverage for peace of mind.
Growth & Recognition
  • Online Learning Platforms – Fuel your professional development.
  • Competitive Salary & Bonuses – Your contributions are valued and rewarded.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Granicus is committed to providing equal employment opportunities. All qualified applicants and employees will be considered for employment and advancement without regard to race, color, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, physical or mental disability, age, genetic information, sexual or affectional orientation, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, familial status, military or veteran status or any other status protected by applicable law.

jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The world is having a monetization moment – every ambitious company is replatforming their billing solution in response to AI. Stripes Billing is a team of deep functional and technical specialists who both lead and advise on deals for one of the most strategically important products in Stripe’s portfolio. Billing Sales is tasked with attacking a $100B market opportunity for automating the entire order to cash process and helping companies not get left behind in the AI era.

What you’ll do

As the Head of Grower Sales (Billing), you will use your leadership and management skills to manage and grow a team of Account Executives to drive expansion and retention of Stripe Billing across the AMER region. You will build and lead a team of sellers, while collaborating with the core sales leadership, marketing, product marketing, and product teams to develop deep product and industry knowledge and drive strategic deals. You will own the coaching, development, and performance of your team, driving the forecast of the business. jobs.description:
EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

Program Consultant (Implementation and Integration Specialist) – Western Canada

Pan-Canadian Integrated Youth Services Collaboration Centre

The newly established pan-Canadian Integrated Youth Services Collaboration Centre (IYS-CC) aims to support development, implementation and evaluation of Integrated Youth Services (IYS) best practices, quality services, and engaged research across Canada. There are emerging or established IYS networks in every province and territory in Canada, with local IYS locations in more than 100 communities. IYS networks deliver mental health, substance use, primary care, education, employment, housing and other health, social and community services to youth ages 12 to 25 years. The IYS model is characterized by its commitments to equity, engagement, measurement and continuous learning. IYS networks work in close connection to the ACCESS Open Minds Indigenous Youth Mental Health and Wellness Network. The IYS-CC operates in Ontario through the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health (CAMH).

As an employment equity employer, CAMH actively seeks First Nations, Inuit and Métis candidates, those from diverse ethno-cultural backgrounds, women, people with disabilities, people who have experienced mental health and substance use challenges, and additional diverse identities, for our workforce.

Position Description

The pan-Canadian Integrated Youth Services Collaboration Centre (IYS-CC) hosted by CAMH is recruiting a Program Consultant (Implementation and Integration Specialist) to support IYS backbone organizations in British Columbia, The Yukon, Alberta, and Northwest Territories. This position will report to the IYS-CC Program Manager and can be based anywhere in Canada. The Program Consultant will play a key role in supporting deliverables of the IYS-CC by supporting IYS networks in Western Canada to implement their network backbone structures and learning health system processes. The Program Consultant will be guided by implementation science and a collaborative partnership approach, to work with a diverse team of other implementation specialists, IYS leaders, youth, service providers, researchers, health equity specialists, and other partners and advisors.

The successful candidate will work across networks utilizing specific capacities and expertise in the areas of Implementation Science, Quality Improvement, change management, stakeholder engagement, co-development, coaching and systems change. The successful candidate will have a strong background in anti-oppressive and anti-racist practice, excellent knowledge of equity frameworks and tools, and significant experience supporting others to identify, prioritize, and develop actions that advance meaningful and sustained change and equitable outcomes. The successful candidate will bring expertise and experience in working within IYS and/or systems that support youth mental health.

Responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

  • Applying and integrating evidence informed approaches to change such as Implementation Science, Quality Improvement and service/system design to support IYS leaders to develop and implement backbone structures and learning health system processes;

  • Engaging and fostering collaborative relationships with partners to develop a shared understanding and vision;

  • Developing an understanding of the local mental health and substance use systems in order to support contextualized implementation;

  • Understanding and reviewing trends, engaging and listening to stakeholders needs, and monitoring and synthesizing evaluation data, to identify gaps and opportunities to strengthen implementation activities for improving equitable outcomes;

  • Assisting partners (internal and external) with implementing practice and/or system change through facilitation, coaching, problem solving, focused capacity building, consensus building, decision making and conflict resolution;

  • Developing effective implementation processes, high quality resources and tools, and evidence informed trainings, based on understanding needs and contexts of stakeholders, service providers, youth, and leads;

  • Building and supporting the capacity of organizations/agency to support sustainable and effective change; and

  • Supporting the implementation of feedback loops and improvement cycles across and within organizations.

The IYS Collaboration Centre hosted by CAMH supports a healthy workplace that embraces diversity, encourages teamwork and complies with all applicable standards and requirements.

Job Requirements:

The successful candidate will possess a Master’s degree in the field of social work, counselling, psychology, public health, public policy, or a related health or social service discipline (or equivalent). Successful candidate will have at least three (3) years’ experience in the field of health promotion/prevention, community health and/or mental health and substance use services or other related health services with a focus on youth mental health implementation. Successful candidate will have:

  • Expertise in health or mental health program planning and implementation with a variety of organizations/agencies, with experience in the Indigenous health and/or mental health and/or substance use sector. Experience working within IYS is considered an asset.

  • Thorough understanding of principles and practices of Indigenous engagement is required. Demonstrated knowledge of First Nations, Inuit and Métis communities, cultures, perspectives and health service providers.

  • Demonstrated commitment to principles of equity, inclusivity, respect and social justice.

  • Demonstrated ability to partner effectively and work in collaboration with geographically and culturally diverse partners, stakeholders of diverse backgrounds, and equity seeking groups

  • Demonstrated skills and commitment to data driven/evidence-informed decision making.

  • Experience working within an Implementation Science framework or other evidence informed implementation or Quality Improvement framework.

  • Demonstrated ability to provide guidance and leadership to collaborative partnerships and experience facilitating or contributing to program planning.

  • Demonstrated ability to coach partners and colleagues using strength-based problem solving, active listening, motivational interviewing, modeling and other coaching strategies.

  • Experience in assisting organizations/agencies with system change initiatives through facilitation, problem solving, decision-making and conflict resolution.

  • Excellent organizational, planning and time management skills, with the ability to multi-task, produce and coordinate projects to tight deadlines.

  • Expertise in health equity and a proven track record of engaging others in open, meaningful and productive dialogue about equity, racism, and oppression.

  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate and work on a team, as well as function independently with minimal supervision.

  • Demonstrated ability and commitment to supporting the engagement of young people and family members with lived experience in planning and implementation activities, preferably within a mental health/substance use context.

  • Demonstrated strong interpersonal, communication (oral/written), community engagement, and creative problem-solving abilities are required.

Other Skills:

  • Bilingualism (French/English) and/or the ability to speak an Indigenous language is considered an asset.

Travel throughout Western Canada (more frequent) and to other parts of Canada (less frequent) will be required.

If you are interested in this position, please ensure that you apply before 5pm EST of the closing date. If your application is received past 5pm EST of the closing date, your application will not be accepted.

Compensation & Benefits:

  • Salary is competitive and based on experience, with a hiring range of $85,682.95 – $107,103.68per year.
  • Employees in this role may progress within the full pay range of $85,682.95 – $128,524.42 per year
  • CAMH’s Total Rewards: Includes participation in HOOPP defined benefit pension plan, flexible work arrangements, and ongoing professional development support.

This role allows professionals to apply their expertise in a mission-driven environment dedicated to public health outcomes.

At time of hire, CAMH will require all new hires and rehires to provide proof of educational qualifications relevant to the position they hold with CAMH and as required by the specifications in the job posting, in accordance with policies

AHR 3.1.3 Recruitment and Selection and AHR 3.1.15 Credentialing of Professional Personnel.

Internal transfers** will be required to provide proof of educational qualifications for any additional qualifications relevant to their new position.

CAMH is a fully affiliated teaching hospital and research institute of the University of Toronto. As a CAMH employee, you will contribute to our mission by supporting teaching, research, and clinical care across the hospital.

CAMH is dedicated to equity, diversity, and inclusion. Our commitment is to foster a workplace, teaching, and learning environment that is inclusive, respectful, and free from discrimination or harassment.

CAMH strongly encourages applications from candidates who reflect the diversity of the communities we serve, including First Nations, Métis, and Inuit Peoples; Black and other racialized communities; LGBTQ2S+ communities; women; and people with disabilities, including those with lived experience of mental health and substance use challenges.

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds. Thank you to all who apply; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. If you require accommodations during the application or recruitment process, please let us know.

The ED-GRL is a key member of the global Early Development regulatory team (EDRT). The role plays a critical role across the Early Development organization, acting as a key strategic advisor and enabler of accelerated, patient-centric development pathways. In close collaboration with cross-functional partners and the broader regulatory team, this role provides high-quality, timely regulatory guidance to support early asset progression—from pre-nomination activities and scientific advice through early clinical development and regulatory interactions—ensuring robust regulatory foundations and smooth transition into later-stage development.

  • Provide global regulatory leadership for assigned early development programs, ensuring clear regulatory strategy, risk identification, and alignment of cross-functional teams.

  • Ensure patient-centricity is embedded in regulatory strategy
  • Represent EDRT within key early development governance forums and ensure consistent regulatory input across stakeholders in a timely manner to support business decisions
  • Serve as the conduit between EDRT and asset teams to facilitate a smooth transition of programs
  • Partner with ED Regulatory Lead to develop and implement infrastructure and process improvements
  • Mentor and coach EDRT members
  • Build relationships with internal stakeholders

  • Experience integrating biomarker strategy, patient engagement and patient-relevant evidence into regulatory and development plans.
  • Strong understanding of current and evolving global regulations, guidelines, and regulatory expectations and health care business practices relevant to early and late clinical development globally.

  • Highly developed organizational and project management skills, with the ability to prioritize, delegate and manage multiple workstreams in a fast-paced environment.

  • Pragmatic, creative and hands-on, combining strategic thinking with the ability to execute and deliver high-quality work under challenging timelines.

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

This is a dynamic, high energy role in which you will bring the Internet of Things to mid-sized customers, building Samsara's business and bringing the benefits of sensor data to customers. Typical sales will be $20k to $100k, and involve POCs, multiple stakeholders, managing trials, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to executives and CXOs.

This is a remote position open to candidates based in Canda

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world of operations is vast. Your customers are often out in the field and the best way to catch them is live on the phone. Samsara’s top reps do constant research to find companies and contacts to expand their pipeline.
  • You have innate curiosity in how businesses work: One day you’ll meet with someone in waste management and the next you may be learning about the inner workings of a food distribution center. Our top sales team members seek to learn the ins and outs of the businesses they support in order to make a larger impact.
  • You are a life-long learner: Samsara sales are complex. You will need to learn about businesses where you previously had little knowledge. The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work.
  • You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customers value earned trust and human relationships built over time.
  • You want to be with the best: Samsara’s high-performance Sales culture means you’ll be surrounded by the best and challenged to go farther than you have before.

Minimum requirements for this role:

  • 2+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role
  • Experience independently closing new deals larger than $10,000 in annual revenue.
  • Must be located in Canada

An ideal candidate has:

  • Proven track record of consistent quota achievement
  • Experience selling in the midmarket space - medium to large deals sizes
  • Experience with high-volume cold calling
  • Must demonstrate a growth mindset and a willingness to be collaborative with your teammates and in your selling process
  • SFDC familiarity

Annual on-target earnings (OTE) range for full-time employees for this position is below and depends on your city of residence. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual OTE Salary
$172,500—$189,750 CAD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. Belonging at Samsara

Accommodations
