jobs.excerpt: Pay: PHP 80k to 100k per month Cellexia Labs currently serves customers in markets all over the world, with our fastest-growing communities in Europe, the US, Canada, and Australia.
jobs.description:
Pay: PHP 80k to 100k per month

Cellexia Labs currently serves customers in markets all over the world, with our fastest-growing communities in Europe, the US, Canada, and Australia. We're a fully remote, international team, small by design, where everyone owns something real and decisions are made by the people closest to the work.

You'll write the copy that sits at the center of our growth. It's work that goes live quickly and is measured by real results, so you'll know what worked within days.

For a gifted writer who's fascinated by persuasion and wants their work judged by results, this is a rare opportunity: ownership of the voice of a growing brand.

A few examples of your responsibilities

Write words that move people. Stories and copy that pull a skeptical reader in, build belief, and move them to act. You'll lead with the angle, the hook, and the proof that earn the click and the order.

Script video that holds attention. Write the scripts for the videos that carry our brand: the hook in the first seconds, the story that keeps people watching, and the line that closes it.

Own the brand voice. Make Cellexia Labs sound like itself everywhere a customer meets us: confident, clear, and credible.

Turn insight into messaging. Dig into customer reviews, support conversations, and ingredient science to find the language customers actually use, then build every piece around it.

Make complex things simple. Take formulation details and ingredient science and turn them into benefits a customer understands in seconds, while staying accurate and compliant.

Test relentlessly. Ship variations of angles, hooks, and openings, read the results with the marketing team, and double down on what wins. Your best work is the work the data backs.

What we look for

Command of the craft. You write sharply and clearly, and you can tell a line that lands from one that merely sounds good. You edit your own work hard.

A pull toward persuasion. You're fascinated by what makes people say yes: the customer's doubts, the offer, the proof, the words that earn trust. You don't need a background in sales or persuasion. You need real curiosity about how words move people, and the drive to learn from what the numbers tell you.

Ownership. You treat every piece of copy as yours until it performs. You hold yourself to a bar that keeps rising.

Curiosity. You research before you write. You're willing to understand ingredients, customers, and competitors until the words come from real understanding.

Team spirit. You support the best idea, not your own. You take feedback well and give it generously.

Relevant experience. [2+] years of professional writing, with a portfolio that shows it. Experience in beauty, skincare, or other consumer brands is a strong advantage. Excellent written English is essential.

What we offer

Fast decisions, minimal bureaucracy. You'll never wait on a chain of sign-offs. Your ideas are taken seriously here, whatever your title or tenure, and the best ones get tested.

Competitive pay, set for where you live. We pay well above local market norms.

Yearly bonuses of up to 40% of your annual salary. When the brand grows, you share in it.

Monthly and yearly subsidies to do your best work. Every month, we put money toward the things that make you more productive: wellness, focus, hardware and internet upgrades, and more. You know what you need better than we do, so you decide how to use it.

Impact you can see. Copy goes live fast here, and results come back quickly. You'll watch your words move the numbers.

A small team that moves fast. Good ideas get tested quickly.

Work from anywhere. Fully remote, with an international team and the flexibility that comes with it.

A path that grows with the company. As Cellexia Labs scales, the writer who shapes our voice is the writer best placed to lead it.

The selection process

We care about what you can do, not how polished your CV looks. That's why our process is built around how you think and work, not just where you've worked.

Step 1: Apply. Submit your application and CV through this link:

jobs.title: Sales Lead / Senior Sales Manager
jobs.excerpt: Grow into Group Head of Sales: run revenue like a founder, across a small group of software companies Find where revenue is stuck.
jobs.description:
Grow into Group Head of Sales: run revenue like a founder, across a small group of software companies

Find where revenue is stuck. Fix it with your own hands. Hand it on. Move to the next.

Remote on UK hours, within reach of Jersey · Full time · £100,000 base · About £175,000 on target, uncapped · £100,000 of equity

Who this is for

Somewhere right now there is a strong senior salesperson or sales lead who is ready to take the next step. They have closed significant deals themselves, helped improve sales processes, and are ready to take ownership of a sales function. They want the opportunity to build a team, grow into a Head of Sales role, and own part of the result. If that is you, read on. If you would rather inherit a team and a playbook, this is a good place to stop.

Where this is going

We are a founder-led group of B2B software companies serving the private wealth and governance world: WealthComply (FATCA and CRS compliance automation), MinuteMaster (board minutes and governance automation) and a third venture that is in stealth. We sell to trust companies, fund administrators and private wealth firms across Europe, the Middle East, Asia and the Caribbean.

Today the founder carries every deal from demonstration to signature himself, and a small business development team books the first meetings. Within a year we want revenue arriving every month without him. This role builds that, one stage at a time.

The role

You will grow into running revenue the way a founder would. You find the one place where it is stuck, do that work yourself until it flows, write down how, hand it to someone you hire or train, and move to the next. Today that place is the stretch between a good demonstration and a signed customer, so you start by selling, often in person in Jersey, Guernsey, London and Switzerland. Expect about seventy per cent of your week on whichever stage is stuck. You work closely with the founder, gradually take ownership of our business development team, and build the rest of the team as each stage starts to work. You report to the founder. Nobody has held this job before you.

You will be judged on five things

  1. Revenue collected every month, on both products.
  2. A pipeline that anyone can read and trust.
  3. The founder out of the sale within six months.
  4. Stages that keep working after you move on.
  5. Customers who stay and grow, with nothing sold that the product cannot do.

This role will not suit you if

  • You want a large team to manage from your first day. You start with a small BD team, and the rest is built one working stage at a time.
  • You want to stop selling and focus only on managing others.
  • Your answer to slow sales is more outbound volume. Our market is a few hundred firms that know each other.
  • You sell by promising. Our buyers work in compliance, and they check.
  • You want a guaranteed bonus, or you find it hard to be corrected.

Who you are

  • You are an experienced senior salesperson, sales lead or sales manager, ready to grow into a Head of Sales role. You may have coached or mentored other sellers, but you don't need to have led an entire sales function before.
  • You have helped improve a sales process, fix what was not working, or build something from nothing. You can show the numbers before and after.
  • You still sell. You have closed significant new business yourself in the last three years, sold to several people inside regulated firms, and you can name the customers.
  • You know how trust companies, corporate service providers and fund administrators buy, or you have sold to firms like them.
  • AI is already how you work, well past drafting emails. You know where it goes wrong, and you check.
  • Humble, hungry, happy. You would rather be corrected than be right, your forecast is honest, and people are glad when you join the call.

What we offer

  • A £100,000 base, and variable pay on all the revenue your team brings in and grows. At target your total is about £175,000. In a strong year it is £250,000 or more, and there is no cap.
  • £100,000 of equity, so you share in the value you help create. If we hit our plan, it will be worth many times that. If we miss, it could be worth nothing.
  • A team that is yours to build, a founder who will hand over his deals, and a written path to Group Head of Sales and eventually Group Chief Revenue Officer.
  • A CRM and tool stack being rebuilt so that you can question them, and act on them, in plain language.
  • Remote on UK hours, a week in Jersey each month for the first quarter, travel paid, budgets for home office, learning and wellbeing, and a pace we can keep.

How we hire

Four steps, then an offer, over about four weeks. After each step we tell you where you stand within two working days.

  1. Apply: your CV or LinkedIn and three short questions (about 30 minutes).
  2. A call with our recruiter (30 minutes).
  3. A working session with our founder and our head of product (about two hours, by video). In the first hour you walk us through a sales process you improved or a significant deal you closed, then sell to us. In the second you work through a real pipeline with an AI assistant beside you.
  4. A paid trial: two days of real work with us, arranged around your notice period. You meet the people you would lead and one of our co-founders, and we take your references.

The offer comes with a sixty-day review against outcomes we agree together. We mean that both ways.

How to apply

Apply through the link. Along with your CV or LinkedIn profile, we ask three short questions: a sales process you improved or helped build, what was stuck, what you did with your own hands and the numbers before and after (up to 300 words); three significant new customers you closed yourself in the last three years, with deal size and how each started (up to 200 words); and your location, notice period, pay expectation and weakest "who you are" point. No cover letter. If you are not sure you tick every box, apply anyway.

  • A collaborative, high-ownership culture
  • Opportunities for development and career growth

Why Join Steer?At Steer, we align our mission of transforming the auto repair experience for shop owners and their customers with your passion for growth, innovation, and excellence.

Here, you’ll find opportunities to expand your skills, take on career-shaping challenges, and contribute to the future of the auto repair industry, all while enjoying comprehensive benefits and flexible work arrangements to support your well-being.

Join Steer to be part of a forward-thinking, flexible, and collaborative culture where you are empowered to do meaningful and impactful work.

jobs.excerpt: Role DescriptionWe are seeking a CMMC Compliance Lead to join Commercial Cyber Operations.
jobs.description:
Role Description

We are seeking a CMMC Compliance Lead to join Commercial Cyber Operations. This person is the customer-facing lead for CMMC Level 1 and Level 2 engagements and owns NIST SP 800-171 interpretation, scoping, documentation, and assessment readiness from kickoff through the C3PAO assessment and into sustainment. Compliance Lead decides what the systems must satisfy, can configure the controls personally in Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 GCC High, writes the record that proves it, and verifies the result the way an assessor would.

This is not a coordination role. The Compliance Lead scopes the assessment boundary, authors the System Security Plan and supporting documentation, directs and where needed performs control implementation, assesses the finished environment against the CMMC Level 2 Assessment Guide, and stands next to the customer during the assessment. They are the day-to-day point of contact for their assigned customers and answer CMMC questions with authority and in plain terms. Customer environments vary: Windows and macOS fleets, GCC High and Google Workspace tenants, Jamf and Intune, cloud and on-prem enclaves. This person has to be versatile enough to work in all of them.

Responsibilities

The listed responsibilities are not exhaustive and additional responsibilities may be assigned based on the evolving needs of the organization. We are seeking a dynamic individual who is able to adapt and take on new responsibilities as they arise.

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned customers for the life of the engagement: run kickoff, working sessions, and status reporting; answer CMMC and NIST SP 800-171 questions directly and accurately without escalation.
  • Scope the CMMC assessment boundary: trace FCI and CUI flows, categorize assets per the CMMC Level 2 Scoping Guide (CUI, Security Protection, Contractor Risk Managed, Specialized, Out of Scope), and produce the boundary, data-flow, and network diagrams.
  • Lead each engagement through the standard delivery process from intake to assessor-ready package, holding the stage gates and evidence standards.
  • Author and maintain the System Security Plan, policies and procedures, POA&M, and evidence library at the assessment-objective level; score self-assessments and SPRS submissions under the DoD Assessment Methodology and 32 CFR Part 170.
  • Implement the technical controls hands-on in the customer tenant: identity, MFA, and conditional access in Entra ID or Google Cloud Identity; least privilege and privileged-account separation; data protection in Microsoft Purview or Google Workspace DLP; FIPS-validated encryption; configuration baselines. Decide which requirement each setting satisfies and why, and split the heavier build work with the Technical Implementation Engineer.
  • Stand up and operate endpoint management across Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android with Microsoft Intune and Jamf (Apple Business Manager, Android Enterprise): enrollment, compliance policies, CIS or DISA STIG baselines, BitLocker and FileVault, patching, and removable-media control.
  • Build the logging and monitoring stack the AU, RA, and SI practices require: centralized audit logging and alerting in a SIEM (Microsoft Sentinel, Google SecOps, Splunk, or similar), log retention and review cadence, vulnerability scanning and remediation tracking, and backup and recovery verification.
  • Assess the finished environment against the CMMC Level 2 Assessment Guide using examine, interview, and test methods; run the pre-assessment readiness review and close gaps before the C3PAO arrives.
  • Prepare customers for C3PAO assessments and support them during assessment week: evidence presentation, interview coaching, assessor questions, and post-assessment POA&M closeout.
  • Run sustainment for customers: continuous monitoring cadence, change reviews, annual affirmations, and reassessment readiness.
  • Improve the practice: turn repeatable work into templates, checklists, and automation, and contribute domain content to the team's internal AI tooling.

Minimum Experience and Qualifications

  • Experience taking defense contractors through NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC Level 2 end to end, from scoping through assessment, including at least one organization you personally led through a successful C3PAO or DIBCAC assessment as the consultant, assessor, or internal compliance lead.
  • Proven ability to write assessor-ready documentation: System Security Plans at the assessment-objective level, policies and procedures, POA&Ms, and data-flow and network diagrams.
  • Hands-on experience implementing NIST SP 800-171 technical controls yourself in Microsoft 365 GCC High (Entra ID, Intune, Purview, Defender) or Google Workspace (Admin console, Cloud Identity, context-aware access, endpoint management): the admin-console work, not only the policy; able to validate what an implementation engineer built rather than accept a screenshot.
  • Endpoint management experience across Windows and macOS (iOS and Android a plus) with at least one of Microsoft Intune or Jamf: enrollment, compliance and configuration policies, disk encryption, patching, and hardening baselines.
  • Experience centralizing audit logs and alerts in a SIEM or log platform (Microsoft Sentinel, Google SecOps, Splunk, or similar) and operating vulnerability scanning, patch management, and backup to satisfy the AU, RA, SI, and MP practices.
  • Working knowledge of networking and perimeter controls (firewalls, VPN and secure remote access, segmentation, DNS, wireless), enough to scope the boundary and verify the SC practices.
  • Customer-facing lead: runs meetings, explains requirements in plain terms to executives and IT staff, documents decisions, pushes back constructively, and delivers without close supervision.
  • Ability to run multiple concurrent engagements (typically 4–6), track milestones, and report status in a remote, asynchronous environment (Slack, Notion, Google Workspace).

Preferred Experience and Qualifications

  • CMMC Certified Assessor (CCA) strongly preferred; CMMC Certified Professional (CCP) at minimum. Lead CCA designation or Registered Practitioner Advanced (RPA) a plus.
  • Hands-on implementation experience in both Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 GCC High, including GCC High migrations and Google Workspace configurations built to NIST SP 800-171.
  • Depth in Apple Business Manager, Android Enterprise, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Sentinel, or Google SecOps; CIS Benchmarks or DISA STIG hardening; Windows Server and Active Directory in hybrid environments.
  • CUI enclave design and migration: GCC High, Azure Government, AWS GovCloud, or on-prem enclaves, including FedRAMP Moderate equivalency evaluation of cloud service providers and scoping of external service providers.

Travel Expectations/Requirements: 10%–25% (customer kickoffs, on-site readiness reviews, C3PAO assessment weeks)

Full compensation packages are based on candidate experience. Compensation ranges are established using national benchmarking data and apply across all geographic locations within the United States.

At Nerdio, our mission is to simplify the lives of IT professionals and maximize their Microsoft cloud and end user computing investments.

We partner with Enterprises and Managed Service Providers all over the world to add value on top of their existing native Microsoft investments like Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD), Windows 365, and Microsoft Intune.

Created in 2016, Nerdio has always taken a market-leading and collaborative approach to cloud deployment and management. Today, Nerdio is used in over 50 countries by more than 15,000 organizations of every size and vertical. We’re committed to delivering exceptional service and support, which starts with identifying and supporting the best staff possible.

We are a fast-moving, nimble company looking for individuals who are collaborative, empathetic, driven and who love to move at the speed of light. If you want to be part of the AVD transformation that Microsoft and Nerdio are leading, then we want to speak with you.

About the Role

We are looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead a growing AI-native R&D team of 10+ engineers. This dual-track role combines direct people management with hands-on coding, architecture, and technical execution. You will remain close to the work, establish responsible AI-assisted development practices, and earn technical trust by helping solve the group’s most difficult engineering problems.

You will own the technical execution of complex problems from initial concept through implementation, evaluation, product validation, and production readiness. You will use AI coding agents and agentic frameworks as part of your daily workflow and help the team do the same without sacrificing code quality, security, reliability, or architectural discipline. You will turn ambiguous needs into clear, testable specifications, measurable evaluation criteria, and executable engineering backlogs, then ensure validated concepts are production-ready or transferred to product engineering through clear documentation and structured handoffs.

What You'll Do

People Leadership

  • Lead and mentor the team, fostering a culture of ownership, accountability, experimentation, and continuous improvement.
  • Run effective 1:1s, performance reviews, and career development conversations that help each engineer grow, thrive, and understand what success looks like.
  • Set clear expectations, provide timely feedback, recognize strong contributions, and address performance or team-health concerns directly and constructively.
  • Hire, onboard, and develop engineers who can operate effectively in a fast-moving environment where tools, practices, and technical assumptions evolve quickly.
  • Create an inclusive, psychologically safe team environment where engineers can challenge ideas, learn from failed experiments, and make decisions with appropriate speed and rigor.
  • Balance the demands of people leadership and hands-on engineering, protecting focus while staying technically credible and accessible to the team.

Technical Leadership and Hands-On Engineering

  • Own R&D initiatives end to end. Take ideas through specification, technical design, implementation, testing, evaluation, product validation, documentation, production readiness, and a structured handoff to product engineering with a high degree of independence and accountability.
  • Build with AI in the loop. Use AI coding assistants, LLM APIs, coding agents, and agentic frameworks such as Microsoft Agent Framework or comparable orchestration technologies to accelerate coding, review, testing, and debugging, while exercising sound judgment about when not to rely on them. End-to-end SDLC experience using AI Factory and AI harness processes.
  • Turn vague needs into executable specifications. Work with stakeholders to define scope, assumptions, technical constraints, acceptance criteria, evaluation measures, and an actionable engineering backlog. Iterate through short feedback loops as evidence and requirements evolve.
  • Develop the team’s AI engineering capabilities. Mentor engineers in writing precise specifications and prompts, reviewing generated code critically, designing tests and evaluations, and identifying hallucinations, security risks, and architectural drift.
  • Set and uphold a high engineering bar. Establish and enforce practical standards for architecture, clean code, code review, automated testing, secure development, documentation, and production readiness.
  • Make sound architectural decisions. Guide system design across distributed services, APIs, data flows, agent orchestration, and cloud infrastructure, balancing rapid experimentation with maintainability and scale.
  • Measure and improve the workflow. Create feedback loops that evaluate both software outcomes and the effectiveness of AI-assisted engineering practices, then turn lessons into repeatable team standards.
  • Partner across functions. Work with Product Management, Architecture, Security, and engineering stakeholders to identify high-value R&D opportunities, define technical and product validation criteria, and determine when validated concepts are ready for productionization or transfer to a product team.

Required Qualifications

  • 7+ years of professional software engineering experience, including ownership of complex systems from design through production.
  • 4+ years of engineering management experience with direct responsibility for coaching, performance management, hiring, career development, and team health.
  • Demonstrated success leading an engineering team of comparable size while remaining hands-on with prototypes, incubation code, architecture, critical technical reviews, and the productionization of validated concepts.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals across backend development, distributed systems, system design, API design, testing, and clean code.
  • Hands-on experience using AI coding assistants, coding agents, and agentic workflows in real software delivery work, not only demonstrations or personal experiments.
  • Strong proficiency in C#/.NET, or comparable backend expertise with the ability to become productive quickly in C#, plus experience integrating LLM APIs into applications or engineering workflows.
  • Experience with a major cloud platform such as Microsoft Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud, containerized development with Docker, and container orchestration technologies such as Kubernetes.
  • Practical knowledge of observability, including structured logging, metrics, tracing, monitoring, alerting, and evaluation of AI-powered features.
  • Ability to review AI-generated code critically for correctness, security, maintainability, testing gaps, and architectural fit.
  • Working knowledge of responsible AI-assisted engineering practices, including source-code and data-handling boundaries, human review, testing, traceability, and secure use of approved tools.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, sound technical judgment, and comfort turning ambiguity into decisions and executable plans.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building or leading an R&D, incubation, platform, or advanced engineering team working through high levels of uncertainty.
  • Experience building products or leading engineering teams in the Microsoft cloud, virtualization, or end-user computing ecosystem, including Azure, Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows 365, Microsoft Intune, or comparable technologies.

  • Background in DevOps practices, CI/CD pipelines, and infrastructure as code.
  • Experience establishing AI-assisted engineering standards or governance across a team or organization.
  • A record of improving engineering culture through technical mentorship, onboarding, internal tooling, technical talks, or documented engineering standards.

What Success Looks Like

  • The team converts ambiguous ideas into precise specifications, rapid experiments, measurable evaluations, and validated product opportunities.
  • Engineers use AI-assisted workflows effectively while retaining human accountability for architecture, security, testing, and code quality.
  • Validated concepts are transferred to product engineering through clear documentation and structured handoffs.

Applied AI R&D

We would particularly like to understand two things:

What did you build before the current AI wave?

What are you building with AI today?

jobs.excerpt: Sentinel Blue is hiring a Client Engineer for our Operations team.
jobs.description:
Sentinel Blue is hiring a Client Engineer for our Operations team. This role is a senior, client-facing engineer who serves as a trusted technology advisor across Sentinel Blue’s client portfolio. This role sits within the Operations team and is built for an engineer who can operate at both the strategic and technical level. The perfect candidate is someone who can assess a client’s environment, understand their goals and constraints, and provide clear, actionable direction.

This is not a pure advisory role. You will be reviewing and modifying configurations, evaluating vendor proposals, identifying security and compliance implications, and producing documentation clients can act on. You will also collaborate internally to connect client needs to the right delivery teams or external partners.

This is a full-time position that is fully remote.

This position may require access to technology, technical data, or information that is subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations. Employment in this position is contingent upon either verification of U.S. person status as defined under applicable export control regulations (which includes U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, and certain protected individuals such as refugees and asylees) or the ability to obtain any required export authorization. The company reserves the right not to apply for an export license and to decline to proceed with any applicant on that basis. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to citizenship status, national origin, or immigration status.

A day in the Client Engineer role:

You might open a conversation with a client who wants to evaluate a new business intelligence platform. You'll work through what they're trying to accomplish, assess the hosting and infrastructure implications, identify where it touches identity or compliance, and produce a structured recommendation even if Sentinel Blue won't own the full implementation. That same week, you might be standing up the server infrastructure to host it, working through a configuration issue blocking a data connection, or troubleshooting why an integration with their identity provider isn't behaving as expected. Later, you're on a call reviewing a vendor proposal with a client's leadership team, helping them understand what questions to ask and what commitments to require. By end of day, you're translating that conversation into a written brief the client can take into their next board discussion.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the senior technology point of contact for assigned clients, owning the relationship at the strategic level.
  • Lead discovery conversations to understand client business goals, existing technology investments, and emerging needs.
  • Translate complex technical topics into clear guidance appropriate for non-technical stakeholders and executive audiences.
  • Represent Sentinel Blue on client calls with credibility, clarity, and a consultative approach.
  • Engage clients on technology requests and questions that fall outside standard managed service scope, including specialized platforms, line-of-business applications, and bespoke infrastructure needs.
  • Assess unfamiliar systems and platforms quickly, understanding hosting requirements, integration dependencies, security posture, and compliance implications even without deep prior experience with the specific tool.
  • Deploy, configure, and troubleshoot infrastructure and applications as part of client engagements, including standing up servers, modifying system configurations, and resolving application-level issues.
  • Provide guidance aligned with CMMC, NIST 800-171, and CIS Controls as applicable to client context.
  • Identify gaps, risks, and remediation priorities across client environments and communicate them clearly.
  • Help clients evaluate vendor proposals and technology investments, including RFP support, contract review from a technical lens, and total cost of ownership analysis.
  • Assess vendor security posture, SLA commitments, and integration readiness in the context of the client's environment.
  • Produce clear client-facing deliverables including assessments, roadmaps, briefing documents, and recommendation reports.
  • Collaborate with internal IT Operations, SOC, and GRC teams to route client needs to the right delivery function.
  • Contribute to internal knowledge by documenting patterns, assessments, and guidance for recurring client scenarios.

What We Can Offer:

Sentinel Blue is a young company with a focused mission: We’re bringing enterprise-class cybersecurity to small and medium sized businesses. Frankly, we’re pushing the envelope of how things are done and constantly seeking innovative ways to meet that mission. The pace is fast, and we’re always learning new things. This is a great place if you want to expose yourself to new and emerging technologies, want to be challenged, and want to build your skills. Further, success in this role can quickly transition into a senior engineering, architectural, or technical leadership role. The right person will find themselves in a fun, dynamic environment, working on interesting problems and making a real difference.

You will be required to achieve a Security+ certification in the first 6 months of hire; we’ll cover your certification costs and provide paid time for you to study!

Requirements:

  • 5–8 years of relevant experience in cloud infrastructure, IT consulting, or technology advisory roles with demonstrated client-facing ownership.
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft 365, Azure, Entra ID, and modern identity and endpoint management.
  • Demonstrated ability to assess unfamiliar technology platforms and produce actionable recommendations without requiring end-to-end ownership of the system.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to brief executive and non-technical audiences clearly and confidently.
  • Troubleshooting skills and follow-through, including validation and documentation.
  • Experience engaging with compliance frameworks such as CMMC, NIST 800-171, or CIS Controls in a practical engineering or advisory context.
  • CompTIA Security+ required within 6 months of hire if not already held.

Desired Qualifications:

  • MSP, MSSP, or consulting background with responsibility across multiple client environments.
  • Hands-on experience in Azure Government, Microsoft 365 GCC High, or other FedRAMP Moderate environments.
  • Familiarity with vendor evaluation, RFP processes, and technology procurement advisory.
  • Experience assessing line-of-business or specialized applications (e.g., BI platforms, ERP/CRM systems, industry-specific tools) from an infrastructure, security, or compliance lens.
  • Proficiency in core networking fundamentals and practical exposure to platforms such as Fortinet, Meraki, Ubiquiti UniFi, or Cloudflare Zero Trust.
  • Familiarity with backup, recovery, and data retention concepts in cloud environments.
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, or a related field.

Benefits:

  • Fully paid individual healthcare, vision and dental insurance for the employee.
  • Paid certification and training opportunities.
  • Three weeks of paid vacation + 10 paid holidays.
  • A supportive environment with a focus on keeping healthy work-life balance.
  • Retirement benefit (401k) with company match
Salary: $120,000 – $160,000 / year

As your initial project assignment, you will support the unique needs of our client as a Cloud Migration Engineer II.

Project Summary


The Cloud Migration Engineer II is a senior hands-on engineer who owns moderate-to-high complexity and multi-tier application migrations from on-premises data centers to Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services (AWS). The role independently assesses technical readiness, selects and adapts approved migration patterns, coordinates technical execution, resolves cross-domain issues, and ensures that migration, validation, rollback, and stabilization activities are completed safely and consistently. The role remains hands-on and is not a people-manager or architect position. The role is remote.


Key Responsibilities


  • Owns moderate-to-high complexity or multi-tier application migrations from technical assessment through cutover, rollback, stabilization, and handoff.
  • Analyzes incomplete application and infrastructure information, validates complex dependencies and readiness risks, and recommends remediation before migration.
  • Selects and adapts approved Azure and AWS migration patterns and runbooks within program guardrails to address application-specific requirements.
  • Reviews target-environment configuration and resolves design or integration issues involving compute, Windows and Linux operating systems, networking, storage, virtualization, identity, security, and application services.
  • Coordinates technical migration execution, including replication, synchronization, shutdown and startup sequencing, decision points, specialist engagement, escalation, cutover, and rollback activities.
  • Leads diagnosis and resolution of cross-domain migration issues and determines when an architect or shared engineering specialist must be engaged.
  • Reviews migration readiness, runbooks, automation, validation results, technical evidence, and rollback viability before key migration decisions.
  • Develops or improves reusable PowerShell, Bash, Python, infrastructure-as-code, and migration automation assets using approved GitHub repositories and program standards.
  • Authors or approves runbooks and technical procedures for complex migration patterns and identifies systemic improvements to migration-factory methods, automation, guardrails, and controls.
  • Guides Cloud Migration Engineer I staff, reviews technical work, and serves as a technical escalation point without acting as a people manager.

Required For This Opportunity


  • US Citizen
  • Minimum five years of progressively responsible infrastructure engineering, systems administration, cloud engineering, or migration experience, including independently leading complex server or application migrations
  • Demonstrated ability to assess technical readiness, analyze incomplete dependency information, select among approved migration approaches, and adapt runbooks for application-specific requirements
  • Hands-on experience with Azure and/or AWS cloud environments, including target configuration, migration tooling, validation, troubleshooting, and operational handoff
  • Advanced troubleshooting experience across Windows Server, Linux, networking, storage, virtualization, identity and access management, security controls, and application dependencies
  • Experience installing, upgrading, configuring, and troubleshooting Windows Server and Linux environments, including Red Hat, Oracle Linux, CentOS, or similar distributions
  • Experience managing Windows and Linux file systems, including PowerShell-based Windows administration and Linux Logical Volume Manager (LVM) and ZFS
  • Experience supporting migrations with Azure File Sync, AWS DataSync, rsync, robocopy, Azure Files, NFS, and/or Amazon Elastic File System (EFS)
  • Experience establishing performance baselines, diagnosing performance issues, and recommending cloud target sizing based on existing-system data
  • Ability to develop or improve PowerShell, Bash, Python, infrastructure-as-code, or similar automation supporting deployment, configuration, migration, rollback, and validation
  • Experience reviewing another engineer’s runbooks, automation, validation evidence, or migration artifacts and providing technical guidance
  • Experience applying or validating STIG controls and/or DoD security requirements within secure and compliant engineering procedures

Nice to Have Skills


  • Experience with Azure Government or AWS GovCloud environments
  • Current associate-level cloud certification strongly preferred, such as Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate, AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate, or AWS Certified SysOps Administrator – Associate
  • Advanced or complementary certification such as Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert, Microsoft Certified: DevOps Engineer Expert, AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional, AWS Certified DevOps Engineer – Professional, HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate, or a relevant security credential
  • Experience leading technical cutover and rollback decisions within defined program authority
  • Experience migrating multi-tier applications and resolving cross-domain migration issues
  • Experience developing reusable Terraform, Bicep, CloudFormation, or other infrastructure-as-code modules
  • Experience using GitHub and GitHub Copilot for source control, peer review, collaboration, and AI-assisted engineering
  • Federal program delivery experience and familiarity with ServiceNow-based change management

jobs.description:
Job Description

A bit about this role

Are you looking to build your career in cybersecurity while making a real difference for the members who depend on us? Our Cybersecurity Governance, Risk Management, and Compliance (GRC) team is looking for a Third-Party Security Risk Analyst to help run the day-to-day work of our Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) program. You'll work alongside senior team members to assess our vendors, document risk, and keep our partnerships secure. It's hands-on work that directly shapes how safely we operate.

Your Responsibilities and Impact will include:

Support the onboarding and reassessment of third-party vendors under the Security purview. You'll gather information, document risks, facilitate stakeholder discussions, evaluate inherent and residual risk, and track follow-up actions and remediation activities.

  • Impact Assessments & Tiering: Perform initial impact assessments on new and existing vendors and assign risk tiers using established criteria, such as data classification, system access, criticality to operations, and regulatory exposure. The tier sets the level and cadence of due diligence each vendor requires.
  • Risk Assessments: Carry out standardized third-party risk assessments under the direction of senior team members, including reviewing security questionnaires, SOC reports, and supporting evidence.
  • Assessment Tracking: Track assessment status and follow up with risk domain owners so submissions arrive on time.
  • Risk Documentation: Document risk findings and ratings, including inherent and residual risk scores, clearly and consistently.
  • Remediation Follow-Up: Monitor open findings and remediation commitments, and escalate overdue items.
  • Contract Support: Help verify that vendor contracts include the required Infosec addendum clauses.
  • Program Documentation: Help maintain procedures, templates, and guidelines so the program stays organized and repeatable.
  • Audit Support: Support internal and external audits of the vendor risk program by preparing evidence and responding to requests.
  • Innovation: Support efforts to improve AI-enabled automation into the vendor risk program.
  • Emerging AI Risk: Help evaluate AI usage in vendors’ products and services, including how they protect data, manage model and platform risk, and meet contractual and regulatory expectations.

At the Heart of It

You'll execute the full TPRM lifecycle, from initial vendor assessments through ongoing monitoring and offboarding. Along the way you'll help third-party services join our ecosystem without compromising our security or our values.


Why Step Into This Role

This role is a strong foundation for a career in cybersecurity GRC. You'll get direct mentorship from experienced TPRM and security professionals and exposure to Legal, Procurement, Compliance, and ERM. You'll also get the chance to grow your skills while contributing to Devoted's resilience against cybersecurity threats.


Required skills and experience:

  • Practical experience in third-party risk management, vendor management, procurement, information security, compliance, or audit (relevant internships count)
  • Basic understanding of third-party risk concepts, governance policies, and common security frameworks (e.g., HITRUST, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, SOC 2)
  • Exposure to vendor lifecycle procedures, including onboarding, ongoing monitoring, and offboarding
  • Exposure to contract clause review for security, privacy, and business resilience controls
  • Familiarity with findings or vulnerability remediation tracking
  • Awareness of software and hardware supply chain risk
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data and spot gaps or inconsistencies in vendor responses
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple assessments at once
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfort working cross-functionally with Legal, Finance, Risk, Procurement, and business stakeholders

Desired skills and experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in risk management, information security, privacy, compliance, business, or a related discipline
  • 3-5 years of experience in a third-party risk management role, including vendor management
  • Familiarity with cloud security controls and shared responsibility models across major providers (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP), including how to evaluate a vendor's cloud environment during an assessment
  • Awareness of AI-related risks and controls, such as data usage and retention, model transparency, and responsible AI practices, and of emerging frameworks like the NIST AI Risk Management Framework or ISO/IEC 42001
  • Knowledge of healthcare regulations such as HIPAA and HITRUST
  • Relevant certifications, or progress toward them (e.g., CISA, CIA)

Salary Range: $58,000 - $110,000/year

The pay range listed for this position is the range the organization reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for this position at the time of the posting. Once the interview process begins, your talent partner will provide additional information on the compensation for the role, along with additional information on our total rewards package. The actual base salary offered will depend on a variety of factors, including the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, specific and unique skills, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job.

jobs.excerpt: About IFS LogisticsIFS Logistics (built and launched as 7bridges, now part of IFS) is an AI-native enterprise logistics platform.
jobs.description:
About IFS Logistics

IFS Logistics (built and launched as 7bridges, now part of IFS) is an AI-native enterprise logistics platform. We unify transport data, optimise carrier spend, and automate execution for enterprise shippers and logistics companies. We're a small, dedicated team inside IFS, reporting into the commercial organisation rather than central R&D. Pure SaaS, zero consultancy.

The role

This is not a traditional "add AI to an existing system" role. You will own the product surface of our audit product end to end — the checks that tell a customer a delivery was late or a carrier charged them incorrectly, the queue where those findings get reviewed and actioned, and the self-serve configuration that lets a customer build their own checks without us.

Audit & Visibility is becoming a standalone product. A staff engineer leads the squad and brings the backend depth; you bring the product surface. You will set the approach for it, partner directly with the squad's Product Lead on product, and be the second technical voice in the squad. You are also the day-to-day mentor for the Junior engineer joining alongside you — that is part of the job, not an extra.

Your depth is frontend and product engineering. Every engineer here is expected to be genuinely fullstack; the profile describes where your depth is, not a boundary you stay inside. You will write Django, design the API contract you consume, and reason about what BigQuery and dbt are doing underneath your screens.

What you'll work on

  • The audit review queue at real scale — tens of thousands of findings per tenant, filtered, triaged, actioned and evidenced.
  • Self-serve check configuration: customers building, previewing and versioning their own audit checks. "Customers configure and manage it, not IFS" is a product principle, not an aspiration.
  • Explainability for incorrect-charge detection — why this charge was flagged, against which rate card, at which version — reproducible months later for a dispute.
  • The Django endpoints, data contracts and pagination behaviour behind all of it.
  • Where the agent sits in each of these flows: agentic audit creation, human review at minimal, meaningful points, and the guardrails that make that safe against a customer's freight spend.

What we're looking for

  • Around five to eight years building and shipping production software, with real depth in React, TypeScript, state and interaction design at scale.
  • You have owned a product surface end to end including the ambiguity in it — you closed the open questions rather than waiting for someone to close them for you.
  • Genuinely fullstack: you write the Python/Django side, you argue about the API contract, and you know when a client-side answer is the wrong answer.
  • Strong on performance and scale in the interface: pagination, virtualisation, server-side filtering, and knowing which of those the data volume actually demands.
  • You build human-in-the-loop and explainability interfaces and treat auditability as a feature, not logging.
  • You raise the bar on other people's work. Review, pairing and direct feedback are things you do by default, and you are happy mentoring an engineer earlier in their career.
  • AI-native in practice: Cursor and Claude daily, good at giving an agent the right context, better at spotting when its output is confidently wrong.
  • You form and state a view. Ambiguity is the job, not a blocker.

Nice to have

  • Design-system ownership, or working shoulder to shoulder with a designer on a complex data surface.
  • Django REST, BigQuery, dbt, Cube Cloud, GCP.
  • LLM agents, RAG or evals in production.
  • Shipped an agent that does real work, like agentic audit or fulfilment-rule automation, and the instinct to build a simulation to prove the logic first.
  • Logistics, supply chain, freight, or any finance-adjacent domain where being wrong costs money.

Tech stack

React, TypeScript · Python (Django REST) · BigQuery, dbt, Cube Cloud, Superset · Pub/Sub, Datastream · GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, GitLab CI/CD · LLMs, RAG, agent frameworks, evals · Cursor + Claude, Notion (SDD Central), Jira.

What success looks like — first 6 months

  • You own the audit review and configuration surface end to end, and the open questions in it get closed by you.
  • Self-serve check configuration is in production, with preview and versioning, and customers use it without us.
  • The queue performs at the largest tenant's data volume, measured, not assumed.
  • The Junior engineer in the squad is productive and shipping reviewed work independently, and can say what they learned from you.
  • Quality standards in the squad are visibly higher: code review on all merge requests, no direct-to-prod, acceptance criteria per ticket — real, not aspirational.

Why this role exists now

Audit & Visibility is becoming a standalone product and the product surface is where its value is either visible or invisible to a customer. The Staff Engineer holds the backend and leads the squad; they cannot also be the only person setting the approach on the product side. We are shifting from feature-driven engineering to agent-led product architecture, and this is one of the surfaces where that shift has to actually land.

You'll need to be based in either the UK or the Netherlands - we're a remote team with clusters of people in London and Amsterdam.

We embrace flexibility and hybrid work opportunities to support diverse needs and lifestyles, while also valuing inclusive workplace experiences. By fostering a sense of community, we drive innovation, strengthen connections, and nurture belonging. Our commitment ensures you can work in a way that suits you best, while also engaging with colleagues to share ideas and build meaningful relationships.

IFS is a billion-dollar revenue company with 7000+ employees on all continents. Our leading AI technology is the backbone of our award-winning enterprise software solutions, enabling our customers to be their best when it really matters–at the Moment of Service™. Our commitment to internal AI adoption has allowed us to stay at the forefront of technological advancements, ensuring our colleagues can unlock their creativity and productivity, and our solutions are always cutting-edge.

At IFS, we’re flexible, we’re innovative, and we’re focused not only on how we can engage with our customers but on how we can make a real change and have a worldwide impact. We help solve some of society’s greatest challenges, fostering a better future through our agility, collaboration, and trust.

We celebrate diversity and understand our responsibility to reflect the diverse world we work in. We are committed to promoting an inclusive workforce that fully represents the many different cultures, backgrounds, and viewpoints of our customers, our partners, and our communities. As a truly international company serving people from around the globe, we realize that our success is tantamount to the respect we have for those different points of view.

By joining our team, you will have the opportunity to be part of a global, diverse environment; you will be joining a winning team with a commitment to sustainability; and a company where we get things done so that you can make a positive impact on the world.

We’re looking for innovative and original thinkers to work in an environment where you can #MakeYourMoment so that we can help others make theirs. With the power of our AI-driven solutions, we empower our team to change the status quo and make a real difference.

If you want to change the status quo, we’ll help you make your moment. Join Team Purple. Join IFS.

At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara’s Machine Learning, AI, Analytics & Data (MAAD) team builds the intelligence and technology that helps our go-to-market teams work faster, make better decisions, and spend more time with customers.

As the Director, GTM AI Engineering you’ll run our AI Engineering team for GTM. You’ll work closely with Data Science, Analytics, and Data Engineering to serve Sales, Customer Success, Support, Enablement, and GTM leadership. This is a hands-on Director role. Expect to spend about 70% of your time building (prototyping agents, writing code, designing evals) and about 30% leading the team, setting strategy, and influencing stakeholders.

You’ll build intelligent workflow experiences. That ranges from AI agents and copilots that take manual work off sellers’ plates, to signals for propensity and prioritization, to the data, evaluation, and measurement foundations that make these products reliable and trusted.

The ideal candidate is AI-native. You already run your own work through agents every day, you’ve shipped AI products to production, and you get as excited about a seller’s first “wow, this saved me an hour” moment as you do about a clean architecture.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US.

In this role, you will:

  • Build hands-on. Prototype, ship, and iterate on AI agents, copilots, and workflow automations for GTM teams, from the first demo to a production system people rely on.
  • Build the platform, not just the apps. Own the architecture of the shared GTM AI platform: orchestration, LLM and tool gateways, identity and access, and the MCP and SDK contracts that let the GTM web app, Salesforce, Slack, desktop, and Claude plugins share one set of governed capabilities.
  • Make evals a first-class discipline. Design evaluation frameworks for agent and LLM behavior, including golden datasets, LLM-as-judge, human review loops, and regression suites, and run them in development and production. Use transcript analysis and eval results to find failures, guide what to fix first, and show quality improving over time.
  • Lead with AI day to day. Use agents, coding assistants, and agent harnesses in your own daily work, and build the shared tooling, patterns, and harnesses that make the whole team faster.
  • Stay ahead of the curve. Track new models, agent frameworks, MCP and tool ecosystems, and context engineering, and turn them into practical recommendations for Samsara's GTM use cases: what to adopt, what to test, and what to ignore. Make clear build-versus-buy calls on vendor tools, not just models.
  • Drive adoption with the field. Be the go-to advocate for AI across Sales, CS, and Support. Run demos, earn credibility with reps and frontline managers, collect real feedback, and turn skeptics into power users.
  • Set the strategy. Own the technical and product strategy for GTM AI, including the data foundations, instrumentation, governance, and observability these products depend on. Decide which prototypes move onto the shared platform, which merge, and which retire. Own model routing across vendors and the per-user spend controls that keep AI cost in line with value. Influence senior leaders on AI priorities, investment, and the operating model.
  • Ship revenue-critical intelligence. Own the forecasting, propensity, and CRM data-quality work that sales leadership acts on, and keep it calibrated, validated, and clear about its limits. Be comfortable across data and analytics engineering, and act as a business leader when the work calls for it.
  • Partner across GTM, Product, and Engineering. Work with Sales, Customer Success, Support, Enablement, Operations, Product, and Engineering leaders to find high-value opportunities, define success metrics, and turn them into durable products.
  • Build for trust. Put a pragmatic responsible-AI approach in place: safety, privacy, reliability, and human-in-the-loop workflows with clear approval and escalation paths. Agents that act on CRM and customer data run with per-user, least-privilege permissions, and changes to systems of record get human approval first.
  • Automatically included
    • All Roles: Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
    • People Manager Roles: Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing AI Engineering team

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 10+ years across software engineering, machine learning, data science, or data platforms, including meaningful leadership experience. You still write code regularly.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant work experience.
  • Hands-on experience building and shipping LLM applications and agentic workflows to production, including tool use, retrieval, context engineering, and production reliability.
  • Production full-stack and cloud engineering experience (for example Python or TypeScript, AWS, and Databricks), including owning systems that other teams depend on.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and running evaluation frameworks for LLM or agent systems, and using them to drive quality decisions.
  • Daily, fluent use of AI agents and coding assistants in your own work, and a point of view on how they change the way teams build.
  • A track record of shipping internal or customer-facing AI/ML products with measurable business impact.
  • Experience with predictive modeling, experimentation, analytics, and data engineering foundations.
  • Strong product judgment and the ability to turn ambiguous business problems into simple, valuable solutions.
  • Excellent communication with both executives and frontline users. You can demo to a sales floor and present to a VP on the same day.
  • A people-first leadership style with a track record of hiring, developing, and keeping strong technical talent.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience building AI or decisioning products for Sales, Customer Success, Support, Marketing, or other GTM functions, ideally in a fast-growing enterprise SaaS environment.
  • Experience with CRM, customer data, support, and knowledge-management systems (such as Salesforce, Gong, Gainsight, Zendesk, and Databricks), and connecting agents to them (for example, through MCP servers or similar integrations).
  • Experience with agent SDKs and harnesses (such as Claude Code / Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, or similar) and LLM observability tooling, eval tooling such as Braintrust or MLflow, and model APIs from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google.
  • Experience operating AI products at scale, including cost management, monitoring, and governance.
  • A visible habit of learning in public, such as writing, talks, open-source work, or internal “what’s new in AI” sessions.

jobs.title: Product Engineer (100% Remote)
jobs.excerpt: In most companies a developer gets a ticket, builds it and moves on to the next one.
jobs.description:
In most companies a developer gets a ticket, builds it and moves on to the next one. Someone else talked to the customer, someone else decided what gets built, and whether it actually helped is someone else's question.

We're looking for developers who want to do the whole job: talk to the people who use the software, decide what to build, build it and stay on it until it works for them. That's what we mean by product engineer. We took the term from PostHog, who describe it well in their Product Engineer Handbook.

About us

is software for property management companies in Germany. Inbox, CRM, documents, telephony, video calls, team chat and AI agents in one platform, so property managers can do their daily work in one place. We're a small team based in Worms, Germany, working fully remote. We're self-funded and profitable.

What a product engineer does here

  • You talk to customers. You read the support requests and feedback for your area, look at how customers use it and talk to them directly. Nobody filters it for you.

  • You decide what to build. For your area you decide what comes next, based on what customers need and what matters for the company. You write down why, so the team can follow and give feedback.

  • You ship early. The first version goes to a few customers as soon as it's useful. Then you improve it based on what they say and do.

  • You build all of it. Data model, backend, frontend and UI. The result has to be clean, simple and intuitive to use, not only working.

  • You do support for your area. When something breaks or a customer is stuck, you fix it and tell them it's fixed.

  • You check whether it worked. Your job isn't done when the feature is live. You look at whether customers use it and whether it solved their problem.

  • You automate what you can. When a customer asks a support question, you add the answer to our knowledge base and update our internal agent, so next time it's handled automatically. A lot already runs on its own here, bug fixes are already processed semi-automatically, and we keep automating more.

Examples of what you could work on

  • A customer wants to bring their old file storage into our document management, with their own folder structure and thousands of documents, and it should be fast and AI-supported. You look at how they've organized their files, build the import as a general feature for all customers, set it up for them and test it with their folder structure. Then you check whether the AI assigned every document to the right building, apartment or contact and fix what doesn't fit.

  • A customer reports that the inbox agent gave a tenant a wrong answer. You look at what the agent did, fix the tool or its instructions and let the customer know.

  • Only a few customers build their own agents in the sandbox. You find out why, by looking at the data and talking to customers, make the setup simpler and check whether more customers use it afterwards.

  • Property managers do the same task fifty times a day and it takes too many clicks. You notice it, talk to them about how they work and make it faster.

Our tech stack

Everything is TypeScript, from the database schema to the frontend.

Backend: Convex (database & serverless functions)

Frontend: Next.js, React, Tailwind, shadcn/ui

Agents: Vercel AI SDK, LiveKit for voice

You'll build with Claude and get as many AI tokens as you need.

Salary

  • $1500 - $3000 per month before taxes with room for growth and promotion in the months & years ahead

  • Permanent employment contract in your country of residence through our partner Deel (EOR)

Benefits

  • 100% remote work

  • Flexible hours

  • Self-funded & profitable, no VC money to burn through

  • Small team, what you build goes live

  • Quick decisions, no pointless meetings and no layers of approval

Our Health Program

  • Private room in hospital, worldwide coverage

  • Free choice of doctors & specialists, no health check, pre-existing conditions don't matter

  • Partner and kids are covered as well

  • Surgery, cancer care, MRI/CT/PET scans and diagnostics fully covered

  • Dental treatment & surgery covered at 90%

  • $675/year for physio, osteopathy, chiropractic and acupuncture

  • $100 per night in-patient cash benefit, up to 20 nights

  • Prescription drugs, vaccinations, glasses/contacts, home nursing and ambulance covered

Our values

  • Get things done, every day matters

  • Transparency and honesty, especially when it's hard

  • High standards for our own work and each other's

Requirements

Requirements

  • Fluent English

  • More than a year of experience shipping production code

What we look for

  • You care more about whether customers can get their work done than about the perfect implementation.

  • You have a good eye for aesthetics and UI design. You don't just ship whatever the AI generates. You keep working on the interface until it's clean and as simple and intuitive as possible for the people using it.

  • You finish things. A feature that's 80% done doesn't help anyone, so you stay on it until it works well.

  • You have an opinion on what to build and back it up with what customers say and do. When the feedback says otherwise, you change your mind.

  • You take feedback well and give honest feedback yourself.

  • You write clearly. As a remote team we work a lot in writing: issues, short proposals, PR descriptions.

  • You understand the basics of the business: who our customers are, what they pay for and why they stay.

  • You write almost all of your code with AI and understand architecture well enough to judge what it writes.

  • You'd rather automate a task than do it twice.

  • You're a generalist and learn new things quickly.

Nice to have

  • You've built your own product or side project that real people used, or you've worked directly with customers before.

  • Experience designing databases and optimizing query performance & cost

  • Experience building production agents, queues and long-running workflows

This role is not for you if

  • you want someone else to decide what you build and hand you tickets

  • you'd rather not deal with customers or support

  • you want to polish code for weeks before anyone sees it

  • you like to move on to the next idea before the last one really works

How we hire

  1. Intro call

  2. Interview with our founder about your background and the things you've built

  3. Reference call with a previous manager

  4. Offer

For a closer look at what we're building, check out our YouTube channel (it's in German).

Role Details

Powered by our proprietary Human Orchestrated Model™ (HOM), we architect reliable:

Money is moving onto the internet, and the shift has a name: Open Money. This is money that is open, portable, agentic, and owned by you. MetaMask spent the last ten years building it; with 100M+ downloads, users in ~190 countries, and trillions in cumulative transaction volume, it's the most trusted self-custodial financial platform on the internet. Now we're building the operating system for your money: one place to hold, move, grow, and use anything you own. Join a remote-first, global team rebuilding how money works: a problem that touches everyone, every day.

About the role

MetaMask is building the infrastructure for a decentralised web. Our TechOps team keeps that infrastructure running — reliably, securely, and at scale. As a Senior Systems Administrator, you'll own the technical backbone that our engineers, product teams, and operations depend on every day.

You'll work across cloud and SaaS environments, driving improvements that raise the bar on system reliability and operational maturity. You'll be expected to bring judgment, initiative, and technical depth — and to operate with significant autonomy.

As a member of the TechOps team, you will drive the operational reliability of the technical ecosystems utilized by our global workforce. Beyond day-to-day administration, you will spearhead high-impact infrastructure initiatives that define our organizational maturity and technical trajectory. As the main IT point of contact for our employees, you will also assist with technical projects as we scale various teams.

What you'll do

  • Ticket management and remote support
  • Hardware and software support
  • Networking
  • Videoconferencing (both digital and physical)
  • Onboarding and offboarding tasks for new hires and departing employees
  • Procuring and shipping equipment to remote employees across the EU
  • General technical assistance
  • Execution of large-scale technical projects and company-wide technology initiatives
  • Work as part of the team responsible for the administration, performance, and reliability of cloud infrastructure across multiple environments, including Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, Zoom and Atlassian

jobs.excerpt: We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production.
jobs.description:
We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production. That means orchestrating multi-step workflows with retries, skips, and parallel execution; keeping long-running work persistent and observable; and serving per-tenant retrieval at scale. This isn't about wrapping an LLM in an API call, it's the hard backend engineering that makes agents dependable.

Our stack is Python (FastAPI) on AWS, with Terraform. We hire on engineering depth and judgment, not on a keyword count, and we work in whichever language you're strongest in during the interview (more below). As a Senior Engineer, you will own backend services and the orchestration layer on top of them, from design through deployment, operation, and the on-call that follows.

Our team is based in Tehran and pays salaries monthly in USD.

What You Will Do:

  • Design, build, and own backend services and the agent-orchestration layer end to end.

  • Build resilient systems that stay correct under load and degrade gracefully when a model, tool, or dependency fails.

  • Ensure operational excellence by making long-running, multi-step work observable and debuggable in production.

  • Shape technical direction through rigorous code reviews, mentorship, and pushing back on specifications when they misalign with engineering reality.

  • Drive the full software development lifecycle, translating ambiguous requirements into durable architectures and actionable technical plans.

What We Are Looking For:

  • 5+ years building and operating production backend systems, with deep ownership of at least one non-trivial service you can talk through end to end.

  • Deep fluency in your primary backend language, and the ability to pick up a new one fast. We work in Python; if it is not your daily language today, we expect you to ramp quickly.

  • Strong systems fundamentals — concurrency, data modeling, and failure modes — and the judgment to choose the right abstraction rather than the cleverest one.

  • Sound reasoning under ambiguity: you ask the clarifying question first, make the trade-offs explicit, and adapt when the constraints change.

  • Solid grasp of infrastructure and operations, including message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ), SQL and NoSQL stores, and running services in containers with an orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad, or similar).

  • Professional written English, enabling you to write crisp design documents and align stakeholders on complex technical trade-offs.

Even Better:

  • AWS (especially ECS) and Terraform, or comparable cloud and Infrastructure-as-Code experience.

  • Hands-on work with LLM, agentic, or RAG systems (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs, Hugging Face) and a real grasp of how non-deterministic agent steps differ from ordinary functions.

  • A recognized-bar engineering background, owned open-source work, or another verifiable standout signal.

How We Hire:

We use a deliberate, transparent two-stage process designed to see how you think and build:

  • 1. A 120-minute conversation focusing on your background and a collaborative system-design exercise and cultural fit..

  • 2. A 120-minute live technical session involving code review, live coding, and a self-review.

You may complete the technical session in your strongest language (Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, or TypeScript/Node.js). Web search is encouraged; AI assistants are not used. We want to see your fundamental engineering judgment.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive USD-based salary and a comprehensive benefits package.

  • Hybrid work flexibility with hours that support deep work.

  • The opportunity to work at the frontier of agentic AI, tackling hard problems with high ownership.

  • A highly educated, agile senior team that values pragmatism, learning, and continuous improvement.

If you would rather be judged on how you think than on a buzzword list, we would like to talk!

Job Summary

The role requires deep expertise in model compression, quantization, and hardware-aware optimization, along with strong systems engineering skills to ship reliable AI capabilities outside the data center. The ideal candidate has shipped edge AI in production environments where compute, memory, energy, and connectivity constraints fundamentally shape the engineering trade-offs.

  • Strong proficiency in Python and C++.
  • Hands-on experience with model compression, quantization, and pruning techniques.
  • Experience with at least one major edge inference framework.
  • Solid understanding of mobile and embedded hardware architectures.

  • Strong performance engineering and profiling skills.
  • Familiarity with on-device privacy and security considerations.
  • Strong communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience with custom NPU or DSP toolchains.
  • Familiarity with federated learning or on-device personalization.
  • Exposure to safety-critical or industrial edge deployments.
  • Open-source contributions to edge AI frameworks.
  • Experience optimizing LLMs for on-device inference.
